findings.title: A user-started download that fails gives no feedback: DownloadManager.errors has no listener and the only failure indicator is hidden on the search screen
findings.evidence: lib/services/download_manager.dart:69-72 `/// Emits a human-readable message when a user-initiated download fails — without this a failure was indistinguishable from a success (the ring simply disappeared).` / `Stream<String> get errors => _errorController.stream;` and :141 `if (!_errorController.isClosed) _errorController.add('$e');`. `grep -rn "\.errors" lib test` returns nothing: the stream has no subscriber (git log -S shows the listener existed in 8948897 and was dropped in the 5.0.0 rewrite 9f47aea). The only remaining failure UI is the red icon in lib/app/app_shell.dart:211-218 `if (_searchActive) TextButton(... '取消' ...) else ...[ const _DownloadsButton(), ...]` — i.e. it is replaced by 取消 exactly while the search view (where downloads are started) is open, and it is not visible at all on pushed routes (playlist page) or inside TrackSheet. lib/widgets/track_download_button.dart:119-154 has three states only (task / _isDownloaded / idle): after a failure it falls back to the idle download arrow. lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:253-280 likewise returns to the two buttons. FailedDownload.error is never displayed (download_management_sheet.dart:137 `detail: '下载失败'`).
findings.failure_scenario: On the search screen tap the download arrow on a Bilibili result (or 下载 in its sheet) while playurl is refused or the CDN request times out. The ring appears, then the control silently reverts to the plain download arrow: no snackbar, no failed state on the row, no reason. The listener cannot tell failure from 'not started'. The only trace is a red icon in the top bar that appears after leaving search with 取消. (The playback path does report: audio_player_handler.dart:613 '下载失败，未能播放'.)
findings.fix: Subscribe to DownloadManager.instance.errors next to handler.messages in AppShell.initState (app_shell.dart:51) and show a snackbar; emit a user-facing string (e.g. '「<title>」下载失败') instead of the raw '$e'. Optionally draw a failed state in TrackDownloadButton via DownloadManager.isFailed.

findings.title: A write error during download (disk full) makes `await sink.flush()` hang forever: the download never fails, stays in _inFlight and cannot be retried until the app is killed
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:534-548 `await for (final chunk in timeoutRes) { sink.add(chunk); received += chunk.length; ... } await sink.flush(); } finally { try { await sink.close(); } catch (_) {} }` — writes go through an IOSink whose errors are never observed during the loop. Dart 3.12.2 SDK: dart-sdk/lib/io/file_impl.dart:225-229 on a failed writeFrom `_subscription.cancel(); openedFile.close(); completer.completeError(e, stackTrace);`; dart-sdk/lib/io/io_sink.dart:257-267 the sink's onError, when not bound, only does `_completeDoneError(error, stackTrace)` — `_controllerCompleter` is left uncompleted and `_controllerInstance` non-null; later `sink.add` goes to the cancelled controller and is dropped; io_sink.dart:184-196 `flush()` then returns `_controllerCompleter!.future.whenComplete(...)`, a future nothing will ever complete. (`sink.done` also completes with an error nobody listens to -> unhandled async error.) Consequences up the stack: audio_download_service.dart:291-293 `finally { _inFlight.remove(id); }` never runs, so :267-268 `final existing = _inFlight[id]; if (existing != null) return existing;` hands every later caller the same dead future; download_manager.dart:142-145 never removes the task, and track_download_button.dart:124-128 sets `onTap = null` while a task exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Storage fills up while (or before) a song downloads: the first failing write (ENOSPC) silently kills the file consumer; the loop keeps pulling the rest of the file over the network and discarding it, then hangs at flush. The ring sits near 100% forever, the row is disabled ('下载中'), the top-bar counter never clears, and after freeing space both 下载 and 下载并播放 for that song join the hung future (the song never plays, `preparing` never clears for that selection). Only force-stopping the app recovers. Not executed (audit is read-only); derived from the SDK source cited.
findings.fix: Do not write through IOSink.add. Open the part with `part.open(mode: ...)` and `await raf.writeFrom(chunk)` per chunk (errors then throw in the loop and give back-pressure), closing the RandomAccessFile in finally. Minimal alternative: capture `sink.done.catchError` into a variable, throw it from inside the loop, and never call flush() after an error.

findings.title: Header timeout does not abort the request and getUrl has no timeout: four stalled CDN responses on one host make every later download hang without an error
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:47-50 `_client = biliHttpClient(connectionTimeout: 15s, idleTimeout: 60s)` with bili_http.dart:17 `int maxConnectionsPerHost = 4`; :432 `final req = await _client.getUrl(Uri.parse(url));` (no timeout); :443-446 `final res = await req.close().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 15), onTimeout: () => throw TimeoutException('CDN close timeout'));` — the timeout only abandons the future; `req.abort()` is never called. Dart SDK _http/http_impl.dart:2353-2356 a connection goes back to the pool only on `incoming.dataDone`; a response whose headers arrive after the 15 s is completed into a future nobody reads, its body is never listened to, so the connection stays in `_active` (:2187-2191 the parser subscription is paused). http_impl.dart:2664-2673 `if (... _active.length + _connecting >= maxConnectionsPerHost) { var completer = Completer<_ConnectionInfo>(); _pending.add(...); return completer.future; }` — queued requests have no timeout (connectionTimeout only wraps the socket connect at :2706-2708). http_impl.dart:1702-1708 `abort()` is what would `_httpClientConnection.destroy()`. Same unbounded waits at :453/:462/:470 `await res.drain<void>()` (no timeout on an error body). BilibiliSdk._httpGet (bilibili_sdk.dart:34-47) abandons requests the same way, but its getUrl is wrapped in a timeout so it fails instead of hanging.
findings.failure_scenario: On a slow or flapping link the CDN's response headers take longer than 15 s (or the path goes half-open after the request was sent). Each such attempt reports 下载失败 but permanently keeps one of the 4 connections for that CDN host:port. After the fourth occurrence in the life of the process (the media service keeps it alive for long periods), every further download whose link points at that host waits forever inside `_client.getUrl`: ring stuck at 0, no failure, no retry possible (the id stays in _inFlight), until the app is force-stopped.
findings.fix: On the header timeout call `req.abort()` before throwing; wrap `_client.getUrl(...)` in `.timeout(...)`; replace the un-timed `res.drain()` calls with `res.listen((_) {}).cancel()` (as already done at :495/:505) or add a timeout.

findings.title: Re-downloading from a search result re-registers the raw video copy, and auto-matching then overwrites the listener's own naming that 删除下载 promised to keep
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:775-786 removeDownloadedTrack: `/// Deletes the local audio for [track] but preserves the user's collection: playlist membership, Favorites, metadata and history all stay.` — it drops the entry from `_downloadedTracks` (:782) and AudioDownloadService.delete removes the meta JSON (audio_download_service.dart:229-235), so the edited copy survives only in playlists/recents. database_service.dart:767-771 saveDownloadedTrack: `if (_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id)) return; _downloadedTracks.insert(0, track);` inserts whatever copy the caller holds; from search that is the raw API Track (bilibili_sdk.dart:616-625, title = video title, named = false). library_controller.dart:202-204 `if (!known.contains(track.id)) TrackNaming.autoName(track);`; track_naming.dart:122-124 `_name` reads the library copy (`before = await _stored(track.id)`), which is not settled, and :195-203 saves the matcher's answer through DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata, which (database_service.dart:532-537) does `pl.tracks[idx] = updated` for every playlist — replacing the copy with `named: true, matcher: 0`. models/track.dart:45-48 states the matcher must never revisit the listener's answers.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener names a song by hand (编辑信息), keeps it in 收藏, later uses 删除下载 to free space. Weeks later they search for it again and download it from the Bilibili results. The library, player and track sheet now show the raw video title/UP主; with 自动匹配 on (default) the matcher runs on that raw copy and its guess overwrites the hand-edited title/artist/cover in 收藏 and every playlist. Downloading from the playlist row instead keeps the edit.
findings.fix: In saveDownloadedTrack, when a playlist or recents already holds this id with isNamed, register that copy (carrying over loudness) instead of the caller's.

findings.title: Abandoned partial downloads are never removed and are invisible in storage management
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:354-359 `} catch (e) { // Deliberately keep the .part file: the next attempt resumes it ...`. The only code that deletes `.part` / `.part.json` is `delete()` (:229-235, reached only through removeDownloadedTrack for a completed download) and `_discardPart` inside a new attempt for the same id. download_manager.dart:105-108 `void dismissFailed(String trackId) { if (_failed.remove(trackId) != null) _notify(trackId); }` drops only the record; :58-61 failures are not persisted, so after a restart nothing references the file. Playback-path failures (audio_player_handler.dart:608-615) are never listed at all. `grep -rn "\.part" lib` finds no sweep; database_service.dart:214-306 `_discoverAudioFiles` only looks at `.ready` files. audio_download_service.dart:201-205 storageBreakdown counts only `.m4a` files with a `.ready` sibling, so the bytes do not appear in the 下载 sheet total. ensureDownloaded also writes `audio_<id>.json` before any byte is fetched (:275), which is likewise left behind.
findings.failure_scenario: Start downloading a long video (a concert or compilation, 100+ MB), lose the connection at 80 %, then tap 忽略 or simply restart the app and never download that exact video again. The `.part` stays in bilibeat_audio for the life of the install, is not listed or counted anywhere in the app, and cannot be removed short of clearing app data. Every abandoned or failed 下载并播放 adds another.
findings.fix: Delete the partial in dismissFailed, and sweep bilibeat_audio at startup (next to _discoverAudioFiles) for `.part`, `.part.json`, `.tmp` and meta/audio files with no `.ready` sibling older than a few days.

findings.title: A failed download stays listed as failed after the same song is downloaded through 下载并播放
findings.evidence: lib/services/download_manager.dart:58-61 `Cleared per item on success, retry, or explicit dismiss.` but the only removals are :94 (retry), :107 (dismiss) and :130 (a new tracked start). A playback-path completion reaches :149-156 `if (task == null) { ... if (p.done) _notify(p.trackId); return; }` — `_failed` is untouched; and :127 `if (alreadyDownloaded) return;` returns before :130 `_failed.remove(track.id);`. library_controller.dart:209/:240 feed `failedTasks.length` to app_shell.dart:244-245/:264-266 (red icon); download_management_sheet.dart:133-137 lists every `_failed` entry as '下载失败' while :160-170 lists the same track under downloaded.
findings.failure_scenario: Tap 下载 on a search result; it fails. Then open the song's sheet and tap 下载并播放 (track_sheet.dart:86-91 -> handler.playTrack -> ensureDownloaded, untracked); it succeeds and plays. The home top bar keeps showing the red error icon, and the 下载 sheet shows the song twice — once as '下载失败' with 重试/忽略 and once as a stored download — until the user taps one of those buttons.
findings.fix: Remove `_failed[p.trackId]` in _onProgress when a `done` event arrives, and in startDownload before returning on `alreadyDownloaded`.

findings.title: The 416 'already complete' shortcut skips the size sanity check, so a rejected sub-1 KiB body is accepted as a finished download on the next attempt
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:555-557 `if (received < 1024) { throw Exception('音频文件异常 ($received 字节)'); }` runs after the body was written and the note saved (:514-516 `{'total': total, 'validator': ...}`), and the catch at :354-359 keeps both files. On the next attempt :437-438 sends `Range: bytes=$existing-`; :451-456 `if (res.statusCode == HttpStatus.requestedRangeNotSatisfiable && existing > 0) { await res.drain<void>(); if (known?.total == existing) { return (received: existing, total: existing); }` returns success without re-applying the <1024 check, and _download (:319-353) renames the part, writes `.ready`, sets the memo and registers the track.
findings.failure_scenario: A CDN node answers 200 with a short non-audio body that is not text/* or JSON (e.g. a 300-byte application/octet-stream error) with Content-Length 300. Attempt 1 correctly fails with 音频文件异常 but leaves a 300-byte .part and a note with total 300. On retry, if the link resolves to the same object, `bytes=300-` gets 416, total == existing, and the 300-byte file becomes a 'downloaded' song in the library that the player can only skip ('有歌曲无法播放，已跳过').
findings.fix: Discard the part and note before throwing at :555-557 (such a body is never worth resuming), and/or require `existing >= 1024` in the 416 branch.

find:downloads aa27dc.notes:
Method: read-only; nothing was built, run or sent to the network. SDK behaviour (IOSink/file consumer, HttpClient pooling) was checked by reading the Dart 3.12.2 sources under ~/flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/lib (io/io_sink.dart, io/file_impl.dart, _http/http_impl.dart), not by executing them — findings 2 and 3 rest on that reading.

Checked and found sound:
- Resume logic in _transfer: a .part is only continued when the note agrees (If-Range with a strong ETag or Last-Modified, Content-Range start == existing, total match, 'neither to go by' rejected); 200-instead-of-206 and If-Range mismatch restart from zero; an unrequested 206 is refused; 416 is accepted only when the recorded total equals the bytes on disk; truncated bodies fail via Content-Length (Dart raises on early close) plus the received<total check; expired links answering text/JSON are rejected before anything is written; Accept-Encoding: identity keeps Content-Length meaningful; redirects carry Referer/UA/Range.
- Per-chunk 30 s stall timeout cancels the response subscription (connection destroyed) and closes the sink before the error propagates.
- Same-track concurrency: _inFlight is claimed synchronously; DownloadManager._tasks/_pendingIsDownloadedCheck guard double taps; a user download joining a playback-path download shares one future and one .part.
- File naming: ids are validated by isSafeKey before any write/delete path; multi-part keys are bvid_p<page>, cid 0 from search resolves to the first page; Track.audioUrl is never set in app code so every attempt asks for a fresh link (no stale signed URL is persisted).
- Index vs disk: saveDownloadedTrack runs only after rename + .ready; startup prune/discovery (_discoverAudioFiles) repairs both directions from the per-track meta JSON; a failed _persistDownloaded self-heals on next launch; removeDownloadedTrack deletes ready first, clears the memo and tells the player (removeTracks) so a playing track is dropped from the queue.
- Delete-while-downloading is not reachable from the UI (删除下载 is offered only for tracks in the downloaded index).
- Subscriptions in TrackDownloadButton, DownloadManagementSheet and TrackSheet are cancelled in dispose; row recycling is guarded by id; progress events are per-id.
- macOS Release entitlements include network.client; Android manifest has allowBackup=false and usesCleartextTraffic=false.

Could not determine offline (depend on Bilibili's live behaviour, so not reported as findings):
- fetchAudioStream returns only DASH baseUrl; backupUrl is read only when baseUrl is absent (bilibili_sdk.dart:424-431) and _download never tries a second URL. If Bilibili hands out an unreachable PCDN/mcdn baseUrl (and http->https rewriting breaks an http-only node), the download fails although a working mirror was in the same answer.
- The `durl` branch is preferred when present (bilibili_sdk.dart:404-414); for videos without DASH that is a muxed video stream, and only durl.first is taken (multi-segment FLV would be truncated). With fnval=16 this should be rare.
- playurl is requested without the buvid cookies and has no fallback when refused (412/-352), unlike view/search; WBI keys are cached 12 h with no refresh on a signature refusal.
- A body with no Content-Length that is cut cleanly is accepted if >= 1024 bytes (no way to detect); CDNs normally send Content-Length.

Minor, not reported: download_management_sheet.dart:184-186 icon buttons are 44x48, under the 48 pt convention in CLAUDE.md; IOSink.add has no back-pressure (bytes buffer in memory if storage is slower than the network); no fsync before the rename, so a power loss seconds after completion could leave a short .m4a behind a .ready marker; _refreshLibrary in the sheet can apply an older snapshot if two refreshes complete out of order.

findings.title: Search results keep Bilibili's HTML entities in titles (&, ") - shown in every list and saved into the library
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:591-592 `final rawTitle = item['title'] as String? ?? '';` / `final cleanTitle = rawTitle.replaceAll(_htmlTagRegex, '');` - only tags are removed. bilibili_sdk.dart:620-621 `title: cleanTitle,` / `rawTitle: cleanTitle,`. Displayed verbatim: lib/widgets/song_tile.dart:92-93 `Text(` / `track.title,`. The only entity decoding in lib/ is LyricsEngine._preprocess (lyrics_engine.dart:166-170 `.replaceAll('&', '&') ... .replaceAll(''', "'")`), used for parsing only, never for the stored/displayed title. The repo's own corpus of real search answers proves the API escapes: test/fixtures/real_bilibili_titles.json contains `"title":"王菲&窦靖童合唱《誓言》"` and `"【周杰伦合集】" 要好好生活，要爱自己 ""`. The BV path (_tracksOfView, line 198) gets unescaped titles from the view API, so one video has two different titles depending on how it was found.
findings.failure_scenario: Search 王菲 誓言 -> the row reads `王菲&窦靖童合唱《誓言》`. Download it: title and rawTitle are persisted with the entity; the library, mini player, 正在准备「…」 banner and lock-screen item show it. It only disappears if auto-matching later renames the track; for anything the matcher declines (compilations such as `【周杰伦合集】" … "`, videos over 15 min, auto-match switched off) it stays for good, and rawTitle keeps it regardless. `&` between two singers is one of the most common characters in collaboration titles.
findings.fix: In _searchOnce decode entities after stripping tags (& < > " ' '   and numeric forms) for `title` (and `author`), via one helper shared with LyricsEngine._preprocess.

findings.title: 为你推荐 recommends songs that are already downloaded: knownIds is only favourites plus the last 30 plays
findings.evidence: recommendation_engine.dart:20-21 `/// Tracks the user already has; never recommend these back.` / `final Set<String> knownIds;`. Filled only inside absorb: line 84-85 `void absorb(Track t, double weight) {` / `known.add(t.id);`, which is called for `favourites` (94-96) and `history.take(30)` (98-100). recommend() loads only those sources (165-167: getFavoritesPlaylist, getRecentlyPlayed, getSearchHistory) - DatabaseService.getDownloadedTracks() is never consulted. Line 202 `if (profile.knownIds.contains(track.id)) continue; // already theirs`. search_view.dart:17 describes the section as `recommendations to download`; docs/archive/FEATURE_AND_BUG_LIST.md states 已在库中的曲目不再推荐.
findings.failure_scenario: Library of 200 downloaded 周深 songs, 20 favourited. The strongest seed is 周深 (Track.uploader of named tracks); page 1 of that search is his most popular videos, most of which are already downloaded as `<bvid>_p1`. Every one that is not a favourite and not among the 30 most recent plays passes the filter, so the list is largely songs the listener already owns (rows show the ⋯ button instead of download) and little that is new.
findings.fix: Pass the downloaded ids into the profile: in recommend() add `(await DatabaseService.getDownloadedTracks()).map((t) => t.id)` to knownIds (keep the 30-play limit for weighting only).

findings.title: 换一批 reloads the identical batch: refresh() always asks for page 1 with nothing excluded
findings.evidence: recommendations_controller.dart:43 `final tracks = await RecommendationEngine.recommend();` then 48-49 `_tracks = tracks;` / `_page = 1;`. The button: search_view.dart:145-146 `tooltip: '换一批',` / `onPressed: _recs.loading ? null : _recs.refresh,`. recommend() is deterministic for an unchanged profile: same seedQueries(), `page = 1`, `'order': 'totalrank'` (bilibili_sdk.dart:521), sort by score, `ranked.take(limit)`. The engine's own doc (recommendation_engine.dart:156-159) says `each refresh asks every seed for its next Bilibili page, so consecutive calls return disjoint batches`, and commit 636a508 implemented it that way (`每次刷新取各 seed 的下一页并排除已展示 id，连续刷新始终得到不重复的新曲目`); the controller rewrite lost it.
findings.failure_scenario: Open search, look at the 20 recommendations, tap 换一批: four seed searches go out and the same 20 songs come back in the same order. If the listener had scrolled to load more, the list is cut back to those first 20. The button never produces a different batch unless favourites/history changed in between.
findings.fix: Make refresh advance: request `page: _page + 1` with `excludeIds: _seen`, replace `_tracks` with that batch and keep `_seen`; wrap back to page 1 (clearing `_seen`) when a batch comes back empty.

findings.title: A BV number or link never reaches the end of its results: every scroll near the bottom re-requests the same video
findings.evidence: BilibiliSdk.search ignores `page` on the id paths: bilibili_sdk.dart:467-471 `final directId = extractBvOrAvId(query);` ... `final direct = await fetchVideoInfo(directId);` / `if (direct.isNotEmpty) return direct;` and 478-482 for short links. OnlineSearchController.loadMore: line 109 `final results = await BilibiliSdk.search(_query, page: page);`, 113-114 `for (final t in results)` / `if (_seen.add(t.id)) t,`, 116 `_page = page;`, 118-119 `// Only an empty page proves the end; a page of duplicates does not.` / `if (results.isEmpty) _reachedEnd = true;`. Trigger: search_view.dart:74-80 `metrics.pixels >= metrics.maxScrollExtent - 320` ... `_online.loadMore();` on every ScrollNotification. The 3 s quiet window (98-101) applies only after a failure.
findings.failure_scenario: Paste the BV number (or b23.tv link) of a 30-part album; 30 rows appear. Scroll towards the last parts: within 320 px of the end each scroll notification calls loadMore; page 2, 3, 4… return the same 30 parts, all duplicates, so `_reachedEnd` is never set. One `x/web-interface/view` request follows another for as long as the finger moves (for a short link also the b23.tv hop and the whole video HTML page each time), the footer spinner flickers on and off, and the burst invites a 412 on the endpoint that cid-less downloads and song naming depend on.
findings.fix: End paging for id queries: in BilibiliSdk.search return `const []` when `page > 1` and the id/short link resolved to a video (so the controller sets _reachedEnd after one extra call), or have search report that the result is a single video and set `_reachedEnd = true` on page 1.

findings.title: Video hints that could not be fetched look the same as hints that say nothing; the name decided without them is saved as final
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:261 `if (view is! Map && tags is! List) return VideoHints.none;`; 269 `final music = part == 0 ? null : await _recognisedMusic(bvid, part);` (null = `could not be asked`, line 312); 288 `musicTitle: music?.title ?? '',`; 291-292 `// Half an answer (one request failed) is used but not kept.` - not kept in _hintsMemo only. The tag request has no risk-control fallback (257 `_httpGet('$_baseUrl/x/web-interface/view/detail/tag?bvid=$bvid')`), and the music lookup is WBI-signed (318). Consumer: track_naming.dart:124-125 fetches hints, 146 `final found = await _ask(before, hints, uploader);`, 155-157 only `if (found == null && !settled)` is retried, otherwise 189-196 `_save(stored.copyWith(... named: true, ... matcher: matcher))`, after which `_settled` (track_naming.dart:101-102) never asks again. The engine relies on the missing evidence, e.g. lyrics_engine.dart:1102 `if (hints.musicTitle.isNotEmpty && !bestApart) { _remember(memoKey, null); return null; }`. The doc at bilibili_sdk.dart:247-248 promises `offline (or refused) is [VideoHints.none], and is asked again next time`.
findings.failure_scenario: Bilibili refuses the API (HTTP 412) or only `x/player/wbi/v2` fails (signature refused during the WBI fallback-key window, -352, a timeout) while NetEase answers. A downloaded video starts playing: fetchVideoHints returns none / tags without music, LyricsEngine.identify decides from the title alone - the recognised-music veto cannot fire and tags cannot confirm a cover's song - and whatever it finds is written with `named: true, matcher: <current>`. The song keeps that name and performer until the matcher constant is raised or the listener edits it; the complete evidence is never consulted.
findings.fix: Carry completeness in VideoHints (false when view, tags or the music lookup could not be asked - _recognisedMusic already separates null from `nothing`). In TrackNaming._name, when hints are incomplete do not persist an automatic name: `_attempted.remove(track.id); return;`.

findings.title: Any error code other than -352/412 is read as "no results" (search) or "no such video" (view)
findings.evidence: _searchOnce never checks `code`: 538-542 `if (isRiskControlled(primary)) { primary = null; }` / `if (primary != null) { body = primary;` (the plain fallback API is skipped), then 574-575 `final data = json['data'];` / `final dynamic rawResult = data is Map ? data['result'] : null;` and 630 `return [];`. isRiskControlled (643) knows only `if (code == -352 || code == 412) return true;` - Bilibili's JSON interception code is -412, positive 412 is the HTTP status. search() (494-501) then repeats unfiltered and returns that `[]`. Same in _tracksOfView: 195 `if (json['code'] == 0 && json['data'] != null) {` ... 240 `return [];`, although the contract above it (169-170) says `transport/API failure throws`. search_view.dart:239-245 renders `[]` as `没有找到，换个关键词或粘贴 BV 号试试` with no 重试.
findings.failure_scenario: The signed search answers HTTP 200 `{"code":-403,"message":"访问权限不足"}` (signature refused - what the hard-coded fallback keys produce, see wbi_signer.dart:175-177), or -799 (too frequent). It is not `risk controlled`, so it is taken as the answer, the unsigned fallback API that would have worked is never tried, and both the music-zone and the unfiltered attempt return []. The listener is told the song does not exist, with no retry button. Likewise a -352/-403 from the signed view fallback makes a pasted BV number `not found`.
findings.fix: In _searchOnce treat `json['code'] != 0` on the primary like a refusal (try the fallback API) and on the final body throw BiliApiException. In _tracksOfView return [] only for the not-found codes (-404, -400, 62002, 62004, 62012) and throw for the rest. Add -412 to isRiskControlled.

findings.title: One failed WBI key fetch switches all signing to the hard-coded pair for two minutes, even when live keys are in memory
findings.evidence: wbi_signer.dart:131-136 the cached live keys are returned only while `DateTime.now().difference(_cacheTime!).inHours < 12`. After that, 138-141 `final retryAfter = _retryAfter;` / `if (retryAfter != null && DateTime.now().isBefore(retryAfter)) { return _fallbackKeys; }` and on any fetch error 180-181 `_retryAfter = DateTime.now().add(_retryEvery);` / `return _fallbackKeys;` - `_cachedImgKey/_cachedSubKey` from the last successful fetch are ignored. The file itself says of the hard-coded pair (175-177) `B站 rotates these, so a stale pair signs requests that the API rejects`. Nothing clears `_cacheTime` when a signed request is refused, so a rotated key is also used for up to 12 h. Consumers: fetchAudioStream (bilibili_sdk.dart:389-398, `json['code'] == 0` else null -> audio_download_service.dart:305 `无法获取音源下载链接`), _recognisedMusic (318), _searchOnce (529).
findings.failure_scenario: The player has been alive since yesterday (keys older than 12 h) or was just opened in a lift; the single `nav` request times out. Connectivity returns seconds later, but for the next two minutes signParams does not try again and signs with the hard-coded pair: every download fails with 无法获取音源下载链接, keyword search reports no results (previous finding), and songs that start playing are named without Bilibili's recognised music (finding above). Each later nav failure repeats the two-minute window.
findings.fix: On fetch failure return the last live keys when any were ever fetched; use the hard-coded pair only when there are none. Clear `_retryAfter` as soon as any Bilibili request succeeds (or shorten it to seconds), and reset `_cacheTime` when a signed call answers -403 so the next call refetches.

findings.title: The 重试 button for a failed results page does nothing for 3 seconds after it appears
findings.evidence: online_search_controller.dart:98-101 `if (_loadMoreFailed &&` / `DateTime.now().difference(_lastFailure) < const Duration(seconds: 3)) {` / `return;`. `_lastFailure` is set at the moment the failure is published (123-124), which is the moment the button is shown: search_view.dart:253-254 `else if (_online.loadMoreFailed)` / `SliverToBoxAdapter(child: Center(child: _retry(_online.loadMore))),`. The explicit tap and the scroll trigger share the one throttled entry point.
findings.failure_scenario: Scroll to the end of results while offline: the next page fails and 重试 appears. Tap it straight away (within 3 s): loadMore returns before `_loadingMore = true`, so there is no spinner, no request and no feedback - the button looks dead. Only a tap after the window has passed works.
findings.fix: Give the button its own entry point (e.g. `loadMore({bool force = false})` or a `retryLoadMore()` that skips the quiet-window check); keep the window for scroll-triggered calls only.

findings.title: A failed recommendations page is retried on every scroll notification (no quiet window, unlike search)
findings.evidence: recommendations_controller.dart:81-86 `} catch (e) {` / `debugPrint('Load more recommendations error: $e');` / `if (pass != _pass) return;` / `}` / `_loadingMore = false;` / `notifyListeners();` - no failure flag, no timestamp. The guard at 62 is only `if (_loading || _loadingMore || _reachedEnd || _tracks.isEmpty) return;`. Caller: search_view.dart:77-78 `if (widget.query.value.trim().isEmpty) {` / `_recs.loadMore();` on every ScrollNotification within 320 px of the end. OnlineSearchController has the guard for exactly this (96-101 `A failed page gets a quiet retry window instead of re-firing on every scroll pixel`). One attempt is 4 seeds (recommendation_engine.dart:186-188), each up to two _searchOnce calls of two HTTP requests (bilibili_sdk.dart:496-501, 535-550).
findings.failure_scenario: Bilibili starts refusing search (412 / -352) while the listener scrolls 为你推荐. Every scroll notification near the bottom starts a new pass of up to 16 requests the instant the previous one fails, for as long as the finger moves - hammering the API precisely when it is rate-limiting, and toggling the footer spinner each time. Offline the same loop spins without the network.
findings.fix: Mirror the search controller: record `_lastFailure` in the catch block and return early from loadMore for a few seconds after a failure (with a separate path for an explicit retry).

findings.title: Short-link resolution downloads the whole video page inside a 6 s budget and discards a redirect it already has
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:108-115 `// Let HttpClient follow redirects automatically; we inspect redirects` / `final res = await req.close().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5));` / `final body = await res.transform(utf8.decoder).join().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5)).catchError((_) => '');` - the id is read from `res.redirects.last.location` (117-118) only after the final page (the www.bilibili.com video HTML, hundreds of KB) has been fetched. The caller caps everything: 478-479 `await _resolveShortLink(query).timeout(const Duration(seconds: 6));`, and on TimeoutException (484-486) falls through to a keyword search of the whole share text.
findings.failure_scenario: On a slow mobile connection paste `【周深《大鱼》-哔哩哔哩】 https://b23.tv/AbCdEfG`. b23.tv answers its 302 in a second, but connecting to www.bilibili.com and reading the page pushes the total past 6 s; the outer timeout fires and the Location that already named the BV is thrown away. The app then keyword-searches the title-plus-URL text and shows unrelated results or 没有找到.
findings.fix: Set `req.followRedirects = false` and read the `Location` header of the first response (looping manually over at most a couple of b23.tv/bilibili.com hops); only fall back to reading a body when there is no redirect.

findings.title: Short-link handling accepts any URL that merely contains "b23.tv" and follows redirects to arbitrary hosts and schemes
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:87-91: when the short-domain regex does not match, `RegExp(r'https?://[^\s]+').firstMatch(input)` takes the first URL of any host; the only check is a substring test, 97-99 `if (!urlStr.contains('b23.tv') && !urlStr.contains('bili2233.cn') && !urlStr.contains('acg.tv')) {`. Line 94 keeps a pasted `http://`. Redirects are followed by default (dart:io `_followRedirects = true`, `_maxRedirects = 5`, any http/https target; Flutter's engine leaves `may_insecurely_connect_to_all_domains = true`, so the manifest's `usesCleartextTraffic="false"` does not constrain dart:io). The body of whatever answers is read without a size limit (111-115) and its first BV-shaped string is trusted: 122-123 `final bvInBody = _bvId.firstMatch(body);` / `if (bvInBody != null) return 'BV${bvInBody.group(1)}';`.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener pastes share text containing `https://b23.tv.example.cn/x` or `https://example.cn/?u=b23.tv`. The app sends a GET to that host (revealing the device's IP), follows its redirects wherever they lead - including plain http and LAN addresses such as http://192.168.1.1/ - buffers up to 5 s of response in memory, and shows whichever video the page's first BV id names as the result of the search.
findings.fix: Parse the URL and require `uri.scheme == 'https'` and `uri.host` equal to (or a subdomain of) b23.tv / bili2233.cn / acg.tv; do not follow redirects automatically - accept a Location only when its host ends with bilibili.com (or one of the short domains); drop the body scan or cap its size.

findings.title: Past the last music-zone page, load-more continues with unfiltered results starting at that page number
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:494-501: `musical = await _searchOnce(query, musicOnly: true, page: page);` ... `if (musical != null && musical.isNotEmpty) return musical;` / `return _searchOnce(query, musicOnly: false, page: page);`. The empty-means-fallback rule was written for page 1 (comment 489-493: `fall back to an unfiltered search rather than telling the user their song does not exist`) but applies to every page; a page past the end of the music zone is a normal empty answer (630 `return [];`). The filter's purpose is stated at 522-523: `a keyword search that returns lectures, gameplay and news is noise`. RecommendationEngine pages the same call (recommendation_engine.dart:188).
findings.failure_scenario: A narrow query has two pages (about 40) of music-zone matches. Scrolling to page 3 gets an empty music answer, so page 3 of the all-zone ranking is appended instead - items 41-60 of a different list, i.e. gameplay/lecture videos, while the 40 best all-zone hits are never shown. The list then keeps growing with such results (two searches per page) instead of ending where the music results end.
findings.fix: Decide the mode on page 1 and keep it: have the controller remember whether page 1 came from the music zone (or pass a `musicOnly` flag back), and for page > 1 query only that mode so an empty page ends the list.

findings.title: A multi-part video found by keyword is offered as one song: part 1's audio under the whole video's title and total length
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:611-625: `// Search results are always the video's first part, and the search API does not return a cid` ... `id: '${bvid}_p1',` / `cid: item['cid'] as int? ?? 0,` / `title: cleanTitle,` / `duration: durationSec,` (the video's total). Download: audio_download_service.dart:299 `BilibiliSdk.fetchAudioStream(track.bvid, track.cid)` -> bilibili_sdk.dart:369-373 `if (cid == 0) { final infoList = await fetchVideoInfo(bvid); if (infoList.isNotEmpty) { cid = infoList.first.cid; } }` - the page list is fetched but only the first cid is used, and nothing writes the part's title, cid or duration back to the Track. Naming then uses that duration (track_naming.dart:74 `durationSeconds: track.duration`). The parts are only listed on the id path (_tracksOfView, 221-237).
findings.failure_scenario: Search 周深 专辑 and tap a result that is a 12-part album upload shown as 48:00. Only P1 (one 4-minute song) is downloaded, stored under the album video's title with duration 2880 s; there is no sign that eleven more parts exist and no way to reach them except finding the BV number elsewhere and pasting it. Because 2880 s exceeds the 15-minute limit, the matcher never names the track either.
findings.fix: When fetchAudioStream (or the track sheet) resolves a cid-less track and `infoList.length > 1`, surface the parts (e.g. open the id-path listing) or at least store P1's own cid, `"<video> - P1: <part>"` title and part duration on the downloaded Track.

findings.title: Links and BV numbers in the search history become taste terms and recommendation seeds
findings.evidence: recommendation_engine.dart:101-105 `for (final q in searches) { for (final token in tokenize(q)) { terms[token] = (terms[token] ?? 0) + _searchWeight; } }` with tokenize (61-63) taking every `[a-zA-Z0-9]{2,}` run of `LyricsEngine.cleanTitle(text)['songTitle']`. Every submitted query is recorded, pasted links included (online_search_controller.dart:69 `DatabaseService.addSearchHistory(query)`, up to 12 kept). cleanTitle leaves a URL intact apart from splitting on `/` (_noisyClean, lyrics_engine.dart:203), so `https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1…` yields https, www, bilibili, com, video and the lower-cased id, each +2.0 per link. seedQueries (132-137) takes the heaviest terms after two uploaders; score() (113-115) adds the same weights to any candidate whose title contains them.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener adds songs by pasting links (the empty state suggests 粘贴 BV 号). After three pasted URLs `https`, `www`, `bilibili`, `com` and `video` weigh 6 each, more than a title bigram from a single favourite (3). Two of them become seed queries sent to Bilibili search, and candidates with e.g. `Official Video` or `HTTPS` in the title are boosted by that weight, so unrelated videos enter and rise in 为你推荐.
findings.fix: Skip history entries that are ids or links when building the profile (`BilibiliSdk.extractBvOrAvId(q) != null || q.contains('://') || q.contains('b23.tv')`), or strip URLs before tokenising.

findings.title: Scrolling library matches under an edited, unsubmitted query loads more pages of the previous Bilibili search
findings.evidence: search_view.dart:77-81 `if (widget.query.value.trim().isEmpty) {` / `_recs.loadMore();` / `} else if (_online.hasSearched && _online.results.isNotEmpty) {` / `_online.loadMore();` - there is no check that the on-screen query is the submitted one (`_online.query == query`, the `submitted` test used at 188 to decide what is drawn). OnlineSearchController.loadMore pages `_query`, the last submitted text (online_search_controller.dart:109). The class comment (22-23) promises `Bilibili is only queried on submit ... so typing never fires network requests`; the 3.8.1 fix covered only the cleared field (app_shell.dart:92 `if (text.trim().isEmpty) _services.onlineSearch.clear();`).
findings.failure_scenario: Search 周深 on Bilibili, then change the field to 周 without submitting: the view now shows the library matches and the 在哔哩哔哩搜索 row. Scrolling that list near its end silently requests page 2, 3, … of the old 周深 search - network traffic for results that are not on screen, and a previous result list that has grown when the old query is typed back.
findings.fix: Only page online results when they are what is displayed: `else if (_online.query == widget.query.value.trim() && _online.results.isNotEmpty) _online.loadMore();`.

find:network a127be.notes:
Read-only audit; nothing was run and no network requests were made. Plugin/SDK behaviour was checked from source (dart:io http_impl.dart, sky_engine hooks.dart, engine switches.cc / FlutterDartProject.mm).

Checked and found sound:
- WBI signing: the mixin table matches the published 64-entry table; keys are sorted, values have !'()* removed before both signing and sending, Uri.encodeComponent matches encodeURIComponent for what remains (space as %20, upper-case hex), wts is added before signing, w_rid is MD5 of query + mixin key. The test in test/bilibili_requests_test.dart covers the sent-equals-signed property.
- TLS: no badCertificateCallback, no HttpOverrides, no http:// literal in the request code; cover and stream URLs are upgraded to https.
- Identifiers: buvid3/buvid4 come from Bilibili's SPI endpoint, live in memory only (1 h), are never persisted and are sent only as a Cookie to api.bilibili.com; dart:io drops Cookie on cross-origin redirects. No account, no login.
- Stale-result tokens in OnlineSearchController (_token, _historyToken) and RecommendationsController (_pass): an older request cannot write into a newer query's results or loading flags; clear()/search() reset the flags a returning stale call skips.
- Response parsing: _httpGet turns non-200, non-UTF-8 and timeouts into null; view/playurl/hints/music/WBI/fingerprint parsing is inside try/catch or type-checked; the untyped casts in the _searchOnce result loop can throw a TypeError, but both callers catch everything. An HTML 200 body ends as BiliApiException, not as an empty list.
- extractBvOrAvId boundaries and case handling; query encoding on every URL built from user text.
- LocalSearch: normalisation, all-terms-must-match and ranking behave as documented; the SearchView cache is invalidated correctly because LibraryController replaces the downloaded list (List.unmodifiable) on every reload.
- HttpClient lifecycle: static clients for the process lifetime with connection and idle timeouts; error bodies are drained.

Smaller observations not raised as findings:
- `await res.drain<void>()` on non-200 answers has no timeout (bilibili_sdk.dart:49, wbi_signer.dart:151, fingerprint_service.dart:40); a stalled error body would hang that call. Error bodies are tiny, so the window is small.
- No overall deadline on a search: on a connection that hangs rather than fails, the first search waits roughly 60 s (SPI 10 s + nav 10 s + primary and fallback 10 s each, then the unfiltered retry 20 s) before 无法连接哔哩哔哩 appears; a retry about 40 s.
- No single-flight for WBI keys or buvid: the four parallel recommendation seeds at cold start each fetch nav and SPI (8 requests instead of 2, four different buvids at once).
- `getUrl(...).timeout(10 s)` with a 15 s connectionTimeout on the SDK client can orphan a request whose handshake completes between 10 and 15 s, holding one of the 10 per-host connections for the life of the process.
- A random fallback buvid3 is cached for a full hour after one failed SPI call (the WBI equivalent is 2 minutes); I could not establish that Bilibili treats it differently from an SPI-issued one.
- RecommendationsController loads once per app session; a first run that loaded with an empty profile keeps showing 听几首歌之后，这里会有推荐 until 换一批 is tapped or the app restarts.

Could not determine offline:
- Whether Bilibili ever returns `{"code":-412}` with HTTP 200 (with HTTP 412 the body is discarded by _httpGet and handled as a failure), and which code the search endpoint uses for a refused signature (-403 vs -352); the confidence on the error-code finding reflects this.
- Whether the hard-coded WBI pair is currently valid; the WBI finding rests on the file's own comment that such a pair is rejected.
- Whether `view/detail/tag` returns a `tag_type: "bgm"` entry named 发现《…》. bilibili_sdk.dart:276 filters only `topic`, and none of the 126 videos in test/fixtures/zhoushen_videos.json carries such a tag although most have recognised music. If the live API does return it, production tags differ from the surveyed fixture and that tag would enter the matcher's tag-as-song candidates (lyrics_engine.dart:891-895). Worth one live check by whoever owns matching.

findings.title: Re-downloading a song from search re-enters it as the raw video copy; the matcher then overwrites the listener's own edits kept in playlists and history
findings.evidence:
lib/services/database_service.dart:767-771 `static Future<void> saveDownloadedTrack(Track track) async { await _ensureLoaded(); if (_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id)) return; _downloadedTracks.insert(0, track);` -- only the downloaded list is consulted; the caller's copy goes in as is.
lib/services/database_service.dart:775-777 (removeDownloadedTrack doc) `Deletes the local audio for [track] but preserves the user's collection: playlist membership, Favorites, metadata and history all stay.`
lib/services/database_service.dart:532-537 and 540-543 (updateTrackMetadata) `for (final pl in _playlists) { final idx = pl.tracks.indexWhere((t) => t.id == updated.id); if (idx != -1) { pl.tracks[idx] = updated; } }` / `_recentlyPlayed[recIdx] = updated;`
lib/state/library_controller.dart:202-204 `for (final track in _downloaded) { if (!known.contains(track.id)) TrackNaming.autoName(track); }`
lib/services/track_naming.dart:121-122 `final before = await _stored(track.id); if (before == null || _settled(before)) return;` (_stored reads getDownloadedTracks only) and 188-196 `await _save(stored.copyWith(title: found.title, uploader: found.artist, coverUrl: found.coverUrl, named: true, rawUploader: uploader, matcher: matcher));`
lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:95-96 `// The listener's own answer: the matcher never revisits it.` / `matcher: 0,`
Entry point with a raw copy: lib/screens/search_view.dart:250 `_songs(_online.results)` -> lib/widgets/track_download_button.dart:151 `DownloadManager.instance.startDownload(widget.track);` -> lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:352 `await DatabaseService.saveDownloadedTrack(track);`. No test covers delete + re-download.
findings.failure_scenario: 1) The listener names song X in 编辑信息 (title, artist, a picked cover; stored with named=true, matcher=0) and X is in 收藏 or a playlist. 2) They free space with 删除下载: X leaves the downloaded list, the playlist/history copies keep the edit. 3) In a later session they find X again in 哔哩哔哩 search results (or 为你推荐) and tap the download button on that row. The raw search Track (video title, UP主, thumbnail, not named) becomes the library copy. 4) LibraryController.reload sees a new id and calls TrackNaming.autoName; _name only looks at the downloaded copy, finds it unsettled, and on a match calls updateTrackMetadata, which replaces the matcher-0 copies in every playlist and in history with the automatic answer. The listener's title/artist are gone and their picked cover file becomes unreferenced (swept a day later). If the matcher finds nothing, the copies simply disagree: 歌曲 and the player show the video title, the playlist row shows the edited name. (Re-downloading from the playlist row itself is fine, because that passes the edited copy.)
findings.fix: Resolve by id before inserting: in saveDownloadedTrack, if a copy with the same id already exists in a playlist or in _recentlyPlayed and isNamed, insert that copy (carrying over the freshly measured loudness) instead of the caller's, and write it to the per-track metadata file with force. That keeps matcher=0 so TrackNaming leaves it alone.

findings.title: Favouriting an already-named song from Bilibili results stores the raw search copy in 收藏
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:102-105 `Future<void> _toggleFavorite() async { Haptics.light(); await DatabaseService.toggleFavorite(widget.track); }` -- while everything shown in the sheet, and 加入歌单 at :188 `PlaylistPicker.show(parent, [track]);`, uses `_latest()` (:236-243 `/// The library's copy carries any edits made since the sheet's caller captured its [Track].`).
lib/services/database_service.dart:736 `favorites.tracks.insert(0, track);` (caller's copy stored verbatim).
lib/screens/search_view.dart:250 `_songs(_online.results),` and 266-269 `return SongTile(track: track, queue: queue, onTap: ...)` -- online rows carry raw search Tracks.
lib/widgets/song_tile.dart:120-121 `services.library.isDownloaded(track.id) ? _MoreButton(track: track, queue: queue)` and :147 `onPressed: () => TrackSheet.show(context, track, queue: queue),` (also :57 onLongPress).
findings.failure_scenario: A song that is downloaded and named (library shows 大鱼 / 周深 with the album cover) appears in the 哔哩哔哩 section of a search, or in 为你推荐. The listener opens its sheet (⋯ or long-press; the sheet header correctly shows the named copy) and taps the heart. 收藏 now lists it under the raw video title (e.g. 【4K60帧】周深《大鱼》现场 纯享版), with the video thumbnail and a title-parsed artist, while 歌曲 lists 大鱼 — 周深. Nothing reconciles the two until the next 编辑信息 save or a matcher generation bump rewrites all copies.
findings.fix: Pass `_latest()` to toggleFavorite. More robustly, let DatabaseService substitute its own downloaded copy by id whenever it inserts a track into a playlist (toggleFavorite, addTrackToPlaylist, addTracksToPlaylist).

findings.title: Artwork of downloaded songs is missing offline: the cover cache only hits on the exact pixel size, and a failed load is never retried
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/cached_cover_image.dart:176-177 `final fetchUrl = CachedCoverImage.sizedUrl(widget.url, _targetW, _targetH);` and 187-188 `final md5Key = md5.convert(utf8.encode(fetchUrl)).toString(); final file = File('${cacheDir.path}/img_$md5Key.img');` -- the cache key is the size-specific URL; there is no lookup of other cached sizes of the same cover.
:209-211 `} catch (_) { _settle(token, null); }` and :254-256 `} catch (_) { return null; }` -> `_CoverStatus.failed`; the only reload trigger is :131 `if (oldWidget.url != widget.url) {`.
Sizes requested for one cover: lib/widgets/song_tile.dart:35 `static const double artSize = 48;`; lib/widgets/mini_player.dart `static const double _art = 52;`; lib/widgets/artwork_backdrop.dart:44-45 `width: 64, height: 64`; lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:622-624 `url: track.coverUrl, width: size, height: size` (full-width artwork); also 104, 112 and 176 pt elsewhere.
findings.failure_scenario: On Wi-Fi the listener downloads a batch of songs from search results; only the 48-pt row thumbnails are fetched and cached. Offline (flight, subway) they play them: the mini player (52 pt), the blurred backdrop (64 pt) and the player artwork each ask for a different `@{w}w_{h}h` URL, miss the cache, fail the request and show the music-note placeholder -- for fully downloaded songs whose cover is already on disk at another size. When the connection returns, a widget that already failed (the player artwork or mini player for the current song) stays on the placeholder until the track changes or the page is reopened.
findings.fix: Name cache files by source URL plus size (e.g. `img_<md5(url)>_<w>.img`) and, when the wanted size is absent and the fetch fails, fall back to the largest cached variant of the same source; or store one canonical cover per song when it is downloaded. Reset a failed state on the next didChangeDependencies/rebuild after a delay so it retries.

findings.title: Cover-cache trim orders by access time, which Android and iOS do not update: it evicts the oldest-downloaded covers, not the least-recently-used
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/cached_cover_image.dart:55-57 doc `Once per launch, when it has outgrown [maxBytes], the covers unused longest go until it is back under three quarters of that.` and :73 `files.sort((a, b) => a.$2.accessed.compareTo(b.$2.accessed));`
Cache hit path, :190-193 `if (await file.exists() && await file.length() > 0) { _settle(token, file); return; }` -- nothing touches the file on use.
test/cover_cache_test.dart:15 sets the timestamp by hand (`await file.setLastAccessed(now.subtract(Duration(days: 10 - i)));`), so the test passes regardless of mount options. Android userdata (f2fs/ext4) and the iOS data volume are mounted noatime, so st_atime stays at creation time; this is platform knowledge, not verified on a device.
findings.failure_scenario: A library of roughly a thousand played songs: each leaves a ~1000-px player cover (100-250 KB) plus several thumbnails, so the cache passes 200 MB. At the next launch trimCache removes files by oldest `accessed` down to 150 MB. With noatime that is the order the files were first downloaded, so the covers thrown away belong to the longest-held library songs however often they are played, while thumbnails of search results seen once last week survive. Online they are re-fetched (and the churn repeats each launch); offline those songs show the placeholder.
findings.fix: Record use explicitly: on a cache hit call `file.setLastModified(DateTime.now())` (only when the stamp is older than, say, a day, to avoid a write per row) and sort by `stat.modified`; adjust the test to set modified times.

findings.title: Lyrics store rewrites, fsyncs and reads back its whole multi-megabyte file on the UI isolate for every new song and every calibration nudge
findings.evidence:
lib/services/lyrics_store.dart:40 `static const int _maxAutomatic = 300;`; :137 `await _persist();` (every putAutomatic); :99 `return _persistIfCurrent(trackId, revision);` (every pin); :155-158 `static Future<void> _persist() => DatabaseService.writeStoreFile(_file, _entries.map((id, lyrics) => MapEntry(id, lyrics.toMap())),);`
lib/services/database_service.dart:355 `final payload = jsonEncode(data);` (calling isolate), :359 `await tmp.writeAsString(payload, flush: true);`, :378 `if (await File(path).readAsString() == payload) return;`, all under the single `_writeLock` (:349-352).
lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:176 `unawaited(_lyrics.setOffset(track, offset)...` -> LyricsController.setOffset -> choose -> LyricsStore.pin, once per calibration action.
findings.failure_scenario: After a few weeks of listening the store holds 300 automatic entries plus pins: about 60 lines x ~75 bytes each, i.e. 1.5-3 MB of JSON. The first play of any new song, and each tap while calibrating lyric timing, builds ~20k line maps, encodes the whole file on the UI isolate, fsyncs it, then reads all of it back, decodes it and compares the strings. That is tens of milliseconds of UI-isolate work per event (dropped frames during the track-change animation and while dragging to calibrate) and megabytes of flash writes per song; session and playlist saves queue behind it on the shared write lock. Figures are estimates from the code, not measured.
findings.fix: Store lyrics one file per track (`bilibeat_lyrics/<id>.json`) with a small index for eviction, so a save touches a few KB. Failing that, encode large payloads with compute/Isolate.run and skip the read-back comparison for this store.

findings.title: Every cold start re-reads each song's metadata file and stats three files per song sequentially before the library can load
findings.evidence:
lib/services/database_service.dart:118-119 `await _loadTracks('$dir/bilibeat_downloaded.json', _downloadedTracks); await _discoverAudioFiles(dir);` (inside _load, which every getter awaits through _ensureLoaded).
:228-235 per `.ready` file: `if (await audioFile.exists() && (await audioFile.length()) > 0 && await metaFile.exists()) { ... final metaContent = await metaFile.readAsString(); final trackMap = Map<String, dynamic>.from(jsonDecode(metaContent)); final track = Track.fromMap(trackMap);` -- done even when the track is already in bilibeat_downloaded.json.
:251 `if (!_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id)) {` (linear scan per file: quadratic overall).
:272-278 prune loop: `exists = await ready.exists() && await audio.exists() && await audio.length() > 0;` per track, although :218 `final entities = await audioDir.list().toList();` already holds every file name.
lib/screens/home_page.dart:112 `child: !_library.loaded ? const SizedBox(height: 120)`.
findings.failure_scenario: With 2,000 downloads each launch performs about 14,000 awaited file operations one after another, parses 2,000 JSON files whose result is discarded, and runs a 2,000 x 2,000 id comparison, all before _ensureLoaded completes. Until then the home page is blank, restoreSession cannot rebuild the queue, and a media-button cold start (handler.play -> restoreSession) waits. Roughly 1-2 s on a phone by estimate, growing with the library; at a few hundred songs it is a few hundred milliseconds.
findings.fix: Build a Set of file names from the listing already fetched and decide ready/audio presence from it; keep a Set of downloaded ids and read a metadata file only for keys not in it (the recovery case).

findings.title: TrackCredit's cache is emptied wholesale at 2,000 entries, so a larger unnamed library re-parses every title on each library update
findings.evidence:
lib/services/track_credit.dart:18 `if (track.isNamed) return track.uploader.trim();` (only unnamed tracks use the cache), :22-25 `final parsed = LyricsEngine.cleanTitle(track.rawTitle, defaultArtist: track.uploader,)['artist'];`, :29 `if (_cache.length > 2000) _cache.clear();`
Callers that walk the whole library: lib/state/library_controller.dart:106-111 (artist sort comparator calls `artistOf(a)`/`artistOf(b)` per comparison), :146-147 (`for (final track in _downloaded) { for (final name in artistNamesOf(track)) {`), lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:252 `queue.add(List<MediaItem>.unmodifiable(tracks.map(_mediaItemFor)));` with :388 `artist: TrackCredit.artistOf(track),`.
lib/state/library_controller.dart:197 `_downloaded = List.unmodifiable(results[0] as List<Track>);` -- a new list identity on every reload, so the sorted/artists caches (:97, :142) are recomputed after any library event.
findings.failure_scenario: 自动匹配歌曲信息 is switched off (nothing is ever named), or the matcher could not name them, and the library passes 2,000 songs. One pass over the library needs more than 2,000 distinct cache entries, so the cache is cleared mid-pass and can never serve the next one. Each favourite toggle, finished download or loudness backfill triggers reload; the 歌手 lens, 歌手 sort (N log N comparator calls, two lookups each) and every queue publish then run the regex-heavy LyricsEngine.cleanTitle thousands of times on the UI isolate, giving a visible hitch per library change.
findings.fix: Evict instead of clearing (drop the oldest entries of the insertion-ordered map), or compute credits once per reload into a map keyed by track id and let the sort, the artists view and SongTile read from that.

findings.title: Covers referenced by a set-aside store are kept for one launch only; the next launch's sweep deletes them
findings.evidence:
lib/services/database_service.dart:124-125 `// With a store set aside, what it referenced is unknown: keep it all.` / `if (!_setAsideAny) unawaited(_sweepCovers(dir));`
:430-431 `/// Whether a file was set aside in this launch (see [_setAside]).` / `static bool _setAsideAny = false;` -- a process-lifetime flag, set only at :438 inside _setAside.
:179-191 the sweep keeps only paths referenced by the stores as loaded now: `final used = <String>{ for (final t in _downloadedTracks) local(t.coverUrl), ... }; ... if (entity is! File || used.contains(entity.path)) continue; if ((await entity.lastModified()).isAfter(cutoff)) continue; await entity.delete();`
findings.failure_scenario: bilibeat_playlists.json cannot be read (damaged tail, or written by a newer build on iOS/macOS where an older build can be installed over it) and is renamed to bilibeat_playlists.json.unreadable; the sweep is skipped in that launch. On the following launch the flag is false again, the playlist store is the fresh empty one, and every picked playlist cover (and track covers referenced only from playlists) older than a day is unreferenced and deleted. When the set-aside file is later repaired or restored, its coverUrl paths point at files that no longer exist.
findings.fix: Skip the sweep whenever any `*.unreadable` file is present in the documents directory (one directory listing), rather than relying on the in-memory flag.

findings.title: On iOS the downloaded audio sits in Documents with no backup exclusion, unlike Android where all app data is excluded
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:67-68 `final docs = await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory(); final path = '${docs.path}/bilibeat_audio';`
android/app/src/main/res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml: `Nothing in BiliBeat is worth restoring: downloads are re-downloaded and playlists re-created by hand. Opt everything out so no cached audio or credentials ever leak through a device-to-device migration.` with every domain excluded for cloud-backup and device-transfer.
A search for `isExcludedFromBackup` / `ExcludedFromBackup` across ios/, macos/ and lib/ returns nothing. iOS backs up an app's Documents directory by default (platform behaviour, not verified on a device).
findings.failure_scenario: On an iPhone with iCloud Backup on, a multi-gigabyte bilibeat_audio folder is included in every device backup and counts against the iCloud quota (a 5 GB plan fills and backups start failing), and it travels in device-to-device transfers -- the opposite of what the Android configuration states the app intends.
findings.fix: Set `isExcludedFromBackup` (URLResourceValues) on Documents/bilibeat_audio once at startup from the iOS runner, or keep audio under Application Support with that flag set.

find:persistence a475ad.notes:
Read-only audit; nothing was run, built or modified, and no network requests were made. Performance figures in the findings are estimates from the code, not measurements; the noatime and iOS-backup claims are platform knowledge not verified on a device.

Checked and found sound:
- Atomic write (_writeJsonAtomically): one FIFO lock, unique temp name, fsync before rename, POSIX rename-over-existing, temp cleanup on failure, lock released in finally. Snapshots are taken in call order, so queued persists of one file cannot lose an update. Dart's JSON encoder escapes lone surrogates, so the read-back comparison cannot spuriously fail on odd titles.
- Unreadable files: downloaded, recently played, playlists, search history, prefs and lyrics are all set aside on a parse error or a newer schema_version; a set-aside downloaded.json is rebuilt from the per-track metadata files, which updateTrackMetadata and setTrackLoudness keep current. The session file is overwritten rather than set aside, which is acceptable for ephemeral state.
- Read-modify-write: every mutator awaits _ensureLoaded and then mutates synchronously; a double-tap on favourite resolves sequentially; the concurrent prefs load / set-aside race is handled.
- Track.fromMap / Playlist.fromMap / PlaybackSession.fromMap tolerate missing, extra and wrongly typed fields; named, matcher and rawUploader round-trip; equality and hashCode are by id; TrackNotifier notifies on identity.
- LyricsStore: pins made before the file loads survive the merge, clears before load are honoured, pinned entries are never evicted or replaced by putAutomatic, revision checks hold.
- LibraryController: the sorted and artists caches are keyed on list identity and cannot go stale; reload ordering and the first-load guard against a naming sweep are correct.
- Picked covers: paths are rebased for all three stores and for rediscovered tracks before use; the network cover cache and the picked-cover folder are different directories on Android, iOS and macOS; cover URLs are normalised to https.
- Playlist reorder, swipe-remove and batch add/remove use consistent indices against the store.

Smaller observations not raised as findings:
- Nothing sweeps `*.tmp` files left if the process is killed between the temp write and the rename (unique names, so each such kill leaves one file; the window is a few milliseconds).
- Nothing in the app ever reads a `.unreadable` file back. Today schemaVersion is 1, so only damaged files are affected.
- Any read or isolate failure in a loader is treated as corruption and sets the file aside; I could not construct a realistic transient failure on these platforms.
- main.dart silences debugPrint in release only on the root isolate; the parse helpers run under compute, where a skipped malformed entry would still be logged with its contents. This only fires on malformed entries.
- pickCoverImage takes the extension as `image.path.split('.').last`; a picked file with no extension (possible on macOS) yields a path with slashes, the copy fails and the pick is silently dropped.
- Persist failures (for example disk full) are swallowed for the library files; in-memory state diverges from disk until the next successful write of that file.
- LyricsStore.putAutomatic removes an existing automatic entry when the new lookup is empty, and an offline lookup is indistinguishable from "not found"; this only bites when the stored lyrics no longer match the track's name. Left for the lyrics reviewer.
- When downloaded.json is rebuilt by discovery, the "most recently downloaded first" order is replaced by directory order.

Not determined: actual startup and encode timings on a device; behaviour of the cover trim on a device mounted relatime.

findings.title: One failed network lookup marks a song as having no lyrics for the rest of the process lifetime
findings.evidence:
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:46-48 `/// Songs the databases had nothing for, this session: no network request on every replay.` / `final Set<String> _misses = {};`
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:178-181 `if (_misses.contains(track.id)) { publish(Lyrics.none); return; }`
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:184-189 `final fresh = await LyricsEngine.autoFetchLyrics(...);` / `if (fresh.isEmpty) _misses.add(track.id);`
autoFetchLyrics cannot tell failure from absence: `_httpGet` swallows every error and returns null (lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:50-53 `catch (e) { debugPrint('Lyrics HTTP error: $e'); } return null;`), fetchFromNetEase just skips a null body (lyrics_engine.dart:1910 `if (searchBody != null) {`), fetchFromLRCLIB likewise (1843), and the orchestrator ends with `return Lyrics(source: 'none', ...)` (2165-2166).
The only removals from `_misses` are choose (83), rematch (104) and a rename of the playing track (134); nothing clears it when connectivity returns. The naming half already makes this distinction (lyrics_engine.dart:562-564 "or null when the request itself failed — which is not the same answer as 'nothing found'"; commit 6319e4f "A lookup that could not reach NetEase leaves the song unnamed for a retry"), the lyric half does not.
findings.failure_scenario: Offline or on a stalled connection (the normal case for an app that plays local files), play a downloaded song whose lyrics are not in the 300-entry cache. Both providers fail, the song is added to `_misses`, the pane shows 暂无歌词. Back online, play the same song again in the same process (the background audio service keeps the process alive for hours or days): no request is made and it still shows 暂无歌词. Only a force-stop, a manual 重新匹配, or a rename brings lyrics back. A single 10 s timeout has the same effect.
findings.fix: Let autoFetchLyrics report that a provider request failed (return null, or a flag set whenever `_httpGet` returned null) and add to `_misses` only when every provider actually answered with nothing.

findings.title: Cached automatic lyrics are rejected on every later play when the provider's title carries a subtitle; offline they are deleted
findings.evidence:
Acceptance at fetch time strips the provider's parenthesised subtitle and tries query suffixes: lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:1679-1680 `final cleanName = songName.replaceAll(parenSubtitle, '').trim(); if (isTitleMatching(cleanName, title)) return true;` (used at 1922).
What is stored is the unstripped name: lyrics_engine.dart:1995, 2000-2002 `final songName = (chosenSong['name'] ?? '') as String; ... return Lyrics(source: 'netease', title: songName, ...)`.
Cache validation compares that raw name with plain isTitleMatching: lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:148-154 `return LyricsEngine.isTitleMatching(storedTitle, parsed) || LyricsEngine.isTitleMatching(storedTitle, track.title);`, gating use of the cache at 172-177 `(stored.pinned || _matches(stored, track))`.
isTitleMatching (lyrics_engine.dart:1739-1754) normalises "问 (Live)" to "问live"; against "问" it is not equal and `if (cand.length < minLen || target.length < minLen) return false;` (1748) rejects it. Against a multi-word title ("大鱼live" vs "大鱼好听哭了") neither string contains the other (1753).
On mismatch the controller refetches (184) and then calls putAutomatic with whatever came back; an empty result removes the existing entry and rewrites the file: lib/services/lyrics_store.dart:131-137 `_entries.remove(trackId); if (lyrics.isNotEmpty) {...} ... await _persist();`.
findings.failure_scenario: Track named 问 / 周深; NetEase's recording is named "问 (Live)". First play: matchesSongQuery("问 (Live)", "周深 问") accepts it via the stripped name, lyrics are shown and stored with title "问 (Live)". Every later play: `_matches` is false ("问live" vs "问", target shorter than minLen), so the cache is ignored, the pane shows the loading shimmer and the search + lyric requests run again. Played offline: the refetch fails, putAutomatic(none) deletes the cached entry from bilibeat_lyrics.json, the song goes into `_misses` and shows 暂无歌词 although its lyrics were on disk. Same for any single-character CJK or under-4-letter Latin title with a subtitle ("SOS (Live)"), and for unnamed or part tracks whose parsed title has extra words ("大鱼 好听哭了" vs stored "大鱼 (Live)"; "<concert> - P3: 大鱼" vs "大鱼 (Live)").
findings.fix: Validate the cache the way the match was accepted: in `_matches` use `LyricsEngine.matchesSongQuery(storedTitle, parsed)` / `matchesSongQuery(storedTitle, track.title)` (or store the paren-stripped name). Separately, do not let putAutomatic drop an existing entry when the lookup failed rather than answered.

findings.title: _httpGet timeouts abandon the request/response without aborting it, permanently leaking pooled connections (4 per host)
findings.evidence:
lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:40-44 `final req = await _client.getUrl(Uri.parse(urlStr)).timeout(_timeout);` ... `final res = await req.close().timeout(_timeout);` ... `return await res.transform(utf8.decoder).join().timeout(_timeout);` — Future.timeout only stops waiting; nothing calls req.abort() or drains a late response. The client is one static pool (line 33 `static final HttpClient _client = biliHttpClient();`) with `maxConnectionsPerHost = 4` (lib/services/bili_http.dart:17,22). The code already knows undrained responses pin connections (lines 46-48 comment) but only handles the non-200 case.
dart:io source (~/flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/lib/_http):
- late response: http_parser.dart:1227 `_bodyPaused = true;` in _createIncoming — the body is not parsed until someone listens; the connection is returned only from `incoming.dataDone.then(...)` (http_impl.dart:2356-2374). A response whose headers arrive after the 10 s timeout is never listened to, so its connection stays in `_active` for good.
- queued request: http_impl.dart:2665-2673 `if (... _active.length + _connecting >= maxConnectionsPerHost) { ... _pending.add(() { completer.complete(connect(...)); }); return completer.future; }` — the pending closure is not removed when the caller's timeout fires; when a slot frees, `_checkPending()` (2603-2607) runs it, `send()` creates a request and pauses the parser (2286 `_subscription!.pause();`), and nobody ever closes that request.
Bursts above 4 are normal on this client: identify() issues up to ~10 parallel NetEase searches (lyrics_engine.dart:918-923) and searchCandidates fetches 6 lyrics in parallel (2075).
findings.failure_scenario: On a slow or briefly stalled mobile link (tunnel, lift, weak signal) a new song starts: identify() fires ~8 NetEase searches, 4 go out and 4 queue. The first four take longer than 10 s overall and then complete; the queued four have already timed out. As each connection is returned, a stale pending closure takes it and parks an unclosed request on it: all 4 music.163.com slots are now held forever. Any response that arrives after its own 10 s timeout leaks its slot the same way. From then until the app process is killed every NetEase request waits 10 s in the queue and fails: automatic lyrics take 30 s to give up (3 queries) and, with the first finding, each song played is recorded as having no lyrics; matching stops naming songs; the manual lyric search shows skeletons for 10 s. The same can happen to the lrclib.net pool.
findings.fix: On timeout release the connection: keep the getUrl future and, if it completes late, `abort()` the request; on a response timeout call `req.abort()` and, if a response still arrives, cancel/drain it (`res.listen(null).cancel()`); cancel the body subscription on a body timeout. Also bound `res.drain()` at line 49, which currently has no timeout. The same getUrl/close timeout pattern is repeated in bilibili_sdk.dart, wbi_signer.dart, fingerprint_service.dart and cached_cover_image.dart.

findings.title: Saving from the lyric editor turns every translation into a separate lyric line, and the unstable sort reverses some original/translation pairs
findings.evidence:
Export writes a translation as a second line with the same tag: lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:1822-1825 `sb.writeln('$tag${line.text}'); if (line.translation != null && line.translation!.isNotEmpty) { sb.writeln('$tag${line.translation}'); }`.
Import makes every tagged line its own LyricLine and never fills `translation`: 1788-1791 `result.add(LyricLine(time: ..., text: text));`, then 1795 `result.sort((a, b) => a.time.compareTo(b.time));`.
The editor round trip is toLrc -> parseAny: lib/widgets/lyrics_sheet.dart:107-114 `initial: ... LyricsEngine.toLrc(current.lines, offset: current.offset)` ... `final lines = LyricsEngine.parseAny(text);` and the result is pinned as source 'user' (117-125). 保存 returns the text whether or not it changed (lyrics_sheet.dart:409-412 `final text = _text.text.trim(); Navigator.of(context).pop(text.isEmpty ? null : text);`).
List.sort is not stable above 32 elements (dart-sdk/lib/internal/sort.dart:18 `_INSERTION_SORT_THRESHOLD = 32`, 61-65 dual-pivot quicksort otherwise). A line-for-line port of that file run on 17 to 65 equal-timestamp pairs returned 1 to 4 pairs with the second line first.
The view highlights only the last line whose time has passed (lib/widgets/lyrics_view.dart:109-111), so of two lines with the same time only one is ever bright.
findings.failure_scenario: A foreign-language song gets NetEase lyrics with translations (text + smaller translation under it). The listener opens 歌词选项 -> 编辑 to fix one word (or just looks) and taps 保存. The lyrics are now pinned with twice as many lines: each translation is a full-size line of its own, only one line of each pair lights up, and with more than 33 lines one or more pairs come out with the translation above the original. Because the result is pinned it is never corrected automatically. Pasting a bilingual .lrc (same timestamp twice per line, a common export format) is reordered the same way.
findings.fix: In parseLrc, when two consecutive source lines carry the same single timestamp, fold the second into `translation` of the first (the inverse of toLrc), and make the ordering stable (sort by time then original index, or mergeSort from package:collection). Optionally make 保存 a no-op when the text is unchanged.

findings.title: Songs whose titles are entirely kana, hangul or other non-CJK/non-ASCII script can never match automatic lyrics
findings.evidence:
lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:1722-1727 `_normalize` keeps only `[一-龥a-zA-Z0-9·]` — kana (U+3040–30FF), hangul, Cyrillic and accented Latin are deleted.
lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:1740-1742 `final cand = _normalize(candidateName); final target = _normalize(targetTitle); if (cand.isEmpty || target.isEmpty) return false;`
Every automatic acceptance goes through it: NetEase at 1922 `if (!matchesSongQuery(songName, query)) continue;` (matchesSongQuery calls isTitleMatching for the whole query and each suffix, 1680-1685) and LRCLIB at 1847 `if (!isTitleMatching(trackName, title)) continue;`.
Japanese titles are an intended input: test/library_features_test.dart:110-114 parses 'YOASOBI「夜に駆ける」Official Music Video' to song 夜に駆ける, and the LRCLIB step is commented "global coverage, e.g. Western/Japanese" (2155). 夜に駆ける only works because two kanji survive normalisation ("夜駆", which also equals スピッツ's 夜を駆ける).
findings.failure_scenario: Download "YOASOBI「アイドル」Official Music Video". cleanTitle gives song アイドル, artist YOASOBI. NetEase returns the song named アイドル; matchesSongQuery("アイドル", "YOASOBI アイドル") normalises the name to an empty string and returns false for the full query and for the suffix; the same happens for the other two queries and for every LRCLIB item. Result: 暂无歌词 (and the song enters `_misses`) although both providers have synced lyrics, which the manual search in the sheet lists immediately. Same for ドライフラワー, マリーゴールド, hangul-only and Cyrillic titles.
findings.fix: In isTitleMatching, when either normalised string is empty fall back to comparing the trimmed, lower-cased raw strings with whitespace and punctuation removed (equality / containment), or widen the kept ranges for this comparison to kana and hangul. Changing `_normalize` globally would need the matching corpus re-checked, so keep the change local to the lyric matcher.

findings.title: 重新匹配 deletes the song's pinned lyrics from disk before the new lookup, with no confirmation; a failed lookup leaves nothing
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/lyrics_sheet.dart:128-132 `void _rematch() { Haptics.light(); Navigator.pop(context); unawaited(_save(() => _lyrics.rematch(widget.track))); }` — one tap on a 48 pt footer button directly beside 编辑 (183-192), no confirmAction.
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:103-110 `_misses.remove(track.id); final cleared = LyricsStore.clear(track.id); if (_isCurrent(track.id)) { ... unawaited(_load(track, generation)); }`
