lib/services/lyrics_store.dart:103-108 clear(): `_entries.remove(trackId); ... return _persistIfCurrent(trackId, revision);` — pinned entries included ("Forgets a track's lyrics (pinned or not)"), written to disk immediately.
The following _load then goes through autoFetchLyrics; on failure it publishes none and records a miss (lyrics_controller.dart:189). The editor asks before discarding unsaved text (lyrics_sheet.dart:384-386 '放弃修改？') but saved, hand-made lyrics get no such guard, although the store calls them "the listener's work" (lyrics_store.dart:76).
findings.failure_scenario: The listener pasted lyrics for a song the databases do not have and calibrated them. Later they tap 重新匹配 (to see whether a match exists now, or by mis-tap next to 编辑), or do so while offline. The pasted, calibrated lyrics are removed from bilibeat_lyrics.json at once; the automatic lookup finds nothing (or cannot reach the network); the song shows 暂无歌词 and there is no undo.
findings.fix: Keep the existing entry until the new lookup returns something (replace on success, restore on an empty/failed result), or ask for confirmation when the current lyrics are pinned.

findings.title: Renaming a song does not refresh its automatic lyrics: the reload re-publishes the entry cached under the old name
findings.evidence:
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:130-135 `// Same song, edited metadata. A better name deserves a fresh lookup — unless the listener already settled the lyrics themselves.` ... `_misses.remove(track.id);` then a new `_load`.
`_load` first consults the cache: 170-177 `final stored = await LyricsStore.get(track.id); ... if (stored != null && stored.isNotEmpty && (stored.pinned || _matches(stored, track))) { publish(stored); return; }`
`_matches` (148-154) accepts the entry if its title matches the raw video title's parse OR track.title; the artist is never compared. So an artist-only edit always hits the cache, and so does a title edit whenever the cached lyrics were found from the raw-title parse (the normal case for a song first played before it was named, since the lyric lookup and auto-naming start together on the same nowPlaying notification: track_naming.dart:42-45).
findings.failure_scenario: An unnamed download titled "光 现场" gets the first NetEase song called 光, which is another artist's. The listener opens 编辑信息 and sets the artist to 陈粒 expecting the lyrics to follow. The controller shows the loading state, finds the cached entry titled 光, `_matches` is true, and the same wrong lyrics come back; no "陈粒 光" search is made. Likewise when auto-matching renames a song a few seconds after its first lyric lookup.
findings.fix: On the same-id rename path bypass the cache for unpinned entries (go straight to autoFetchLyrics and keep the old entry only if the new lookup returns nothing), or record the song/artist the lookup was made with on the stored entry and treat a different pair as stale.

findings.title: NetEase lyrics without timestamps are discarded in both the automatic lookup and the manual picker
findings.evidence:
Automatic: lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:1935 `final lines = parseLrc(rawLrc);` and 1962 `if (lines.isNotEmpty) {` — parseLrc drops every line without a `[mm:ss]` tag (1774-1775 `if (matches.isEmpty) continue;`), so plain-text lyrics yield no lines and the song is skipped with no fallback.
Manual: 2035 `final lines = parseLrc((json['lrc']?['lyric'] ?? '') as String);` in _netEaseLines, and candidates with no lines are filtered out (2089-2092 `if (l.isNotEmpty) l`).
LRCLIB's untimed text is kept on both paths (1877-1884 `lines: plainLines(rawLrc)`; 2110 `final lines = parseAny(raw);`), the view has a plain-page mode (lyrics_view.dart:22) and the picker a 无时间轴 badge (lyrics_sheet.dart:302-306). CHANGELOG 6.0.0 lists "无时间轴纯文本展示" as a feature.
findings.failure_scenario: A less common Chinese song whose NetEase entry only has unsynced text (lyric body without time tags, which NetEase serves for many user-uploaded tracks). Automatic lookup: 暂无歌词. Manual search in the sheet: the song is not listed, or 没有找到歌词. The text exists at the provider the app queried; the listener has to find and paste it by hand.
findings.fix: Use parseAny for the NetEase body in both places (as the LRCLIB paths do), preferring a synced candidate when one exists.

findings.title: With a calibration offset, tapping a line often highlights the previous line (float round-trip between seek target and active-line test)
findings.evidence:
Seek target: lib/widgets/lyrics_view.dart:172-173 `final seconds = (line.time + widget.lyrics.offset).clamp(0.0, 86400.0); widget.onSeek?.call(Duration(milliseconds: (seconds * 1000).round()));`
Active-line test: 103 `final at = position.inMilliseconds / 1000.0 - widget.lyrics.offset;` and 109 `if (_lines[mid].time <= at) {`.
The two are not inverse in IEEE doubles: (t + o) rounded to ms, divided by 1000, minus o can land one ulp below t. Reproducing exactly this arithmetic over random mm:ss.mmm line times gave `t <= at` false for 14–20% of lines with offsets such as -5.2, +0.35, +1.27, -0.83 (and 0.1% with offset 0). Offsets come from calibration rounded to centiseconds (165-168).
findings.failure_scenario: Lyrics calibrated to -0.83 s. While paused, tap a line to jump to it: the player seeks to that line's time, but for roughly one line in six `_indexAt` returns the line before it, so the previous line is highlighted and centred until playback is resumed. While playing, the same lines flash the previous line for one position tick before correcting.
findings.fix: Compare in integer milliseconds (precompute each line's displayed time as `((time + offset) * 1000).round()` and test against `position.inMilliseconds`), or add a half-millisecond tolerance to the comparison.

findings.title: The lyric sheet's default search ignores the part name of a multi-part video
findings.evidence:
Automatic lookup uses the part's own name: lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:61-64 `track.isNamed ? (song: track.title, artist: track.uploader) : (song: track.partTitle, artist: null);`
The sheet's pre-filled query does not: 67-73 `if (track.isNamed) {...} final parsed = LyricsEngine.cleanTitle(track.rawTitle); return '${parsed['artist'] ?? ''} ${parsed['songTitle'] ?? ''}'.trim();` — rawTitle is the whole video's title (lib/models/track.dart:67-78: parts are titled "<video> - P3: <part>").
The sheet searches that query as soon as it opens (lib/widgets/lyrics_sheet.dart:47-48, 57).
findings.failure_scenario: An album or concert uploaded as one multi-part video, e.g. part "周深演唱会全场 - P3: 大鱼" that auto-matching did not name. The automatic lookup searches 大鱼. Opening 歌词选项 searches the video title instead, so the candidate list is empty or unrelated and the listener has to retype the song name for every part.
findings.fix: In defaultQuery use `track.partTitle` as the song when it is non-null (with the artist parsed from rawTitle), mirroring `_namedBy`.

findings.title: macOS: scrolling the lyrics with a mouse wheel never enters browsing mode, so the view snaps back at the next line
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/lyrics_view.dart:151-154 `if (notification is ScrollStartNotification && notification.dragDetails != null) { _resumeTimer?.cancel(); if (!_browsing) setState(() => _browsing = true); }` — browsing is only recognised for drag-initiated scrolls.
Pointer-signal scrolling does not produce drag details: flutter/lib/src/widgets/scroll_position_with_single_context.dart:224-234 pointerScroll() does `goIdle(); ... forcePixels(targetPixels); didStartScroll(); ... didEndScroll();`, and the idle activity's start notification is `ScrollStartNotification(metrics: metrics, context: context)` (scroll_activity.dart:99-101) with no dragDetails; only DragScrollActivity sets them (scroll_activity.dart:484-491).
While `_browsing` is false every active-line change calls `_follow()` (lyrics_view.dart:123).
findings.failure_scenario: macOS build, wheel mouse: the listener scrolls down to read ahead. `_browsing` stays false, no 回到当前 button appears, and as soon as the sung line changes (a few seconds) the list animates back to it. "Scrolling by hand takes over" holds for touch and trackpad only.
findings.fix: Also enter browsing on a UserScrollNotification, or on a ScrollUpdateNotification that arrives while no programmatic follow is in flight (set a flag around `_follow`).

find:lyrics a0a674.notes:
Method: read-only. Nothing in the repo was modified and no flutter/dart/network command was run. Two claims were checked numerically with small Python scripts in the scratchpad (a line-for-line port of dart-sdk/lib/internal/sort.dart for the sort-stability claim; the seek/active-line float arithmetic). The connection-leak finding is derived from reading dart:io source (http_impl.dart, http_parser.dart), not from a run, hence its lower confidence. Provider data shapes (NetEase unsynced lyric bodies, "(Live)" naming) are from knowledge of the APIs, not from requests.

Also read in part (not listed in filesRead): lib/services/database_service.dart (write lock, envelope, set-aside, store-file helpers), lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart (nowPlaying/_publish/_announce, holdAutoAdvance, updateTrackMetadata), test/widget_test.dart and test/library_features_test.dart (LRC tests).

Checked and found sound:
- Pin semantics, every write path in LyricsStore: pin and clear bump the revision synchronously; putAutomatic re-checks revision and `pinned` both before and after its await; the file merge in _load keeps session entries over file entries and honours clears made before load; _evict skips pinned entries; calibration (setOffset -> choose -> pin) pins. I found no path by which an automatic result overwrites a pinned entry.
- Stale results: _load's owns() (generation + current track id + store revision) is re-checked after every await and in the catch; A->B->A, dispose, choose and rematch all invalidate in-flight work. The sheet's search token and mounted checks are correct; choose/paste/rematch act on the track the sheet was opened for.
- Calibration maths: offset is absolute, sign and the 0.20 s reaction correction are right, lines are not rewritten, the offset round-trips through toMap/fromMap and is baked into toLrc.
- parseLrc: mm:ss, mm:ss.x/.xx/.xxx, mm:ss:xx, several tags per line, CRLF and BOM (String.trim strips U+FEFF), metadata tags ([ar:], [length:03:45]) and blank timed lines behave as intended; fraction digits are read by position.
- LyricsView: listeners and the resume timer are removed in dispose and on lyric change; drag-initiated browsing, the 4 s grace and tap-to-resume work for touch; binary search handles equal times and offsets; _follow guards unmounted/empty states.
- JSON handling in the provider code: all decoding and casts sit inside try/catch or .catchError; a malformed response degrades to "no result" rather than throwing into the controller.

Smaller observations not raised as findings:
- The LRC `[offset:±ms]` tag is ignored (the line is skipped as metadata), so a pasted file that relies on it is off by that amount until calibrated.
- LyricsStore._persist rewrites the whole file (up to 300 cached songs, roughly 1 MB, jsonEncode and a read-back compare on the UI isolate) on every automatic result, including misses where nothing changed, and on every calibration tap. Not measured.
- fetchFromLRCLIB returns the first title-matching record even when it only has plainLyrics and a later record is synced; could not confirm result ordering without the network.
- `res.drain()` at lyrics_engine.dart:49 has no timeout; a stalled non-200 body would hold the lyrics pane in the loading state and block TrackNaming's serial queue.
- rematch() and _load() use the sheet's captured Track instance; if auto-naming renames the song while the sheet is open, a rematch searches with the old name.
- In calibration mode the list still snaps back to the (mis-timed) active line 4 s after a manual scroll, which works against hunting for the line being heard.

findings.title: Explicit download failures are silent: DownloadManager.errors lost its only listener in the 5.0.0 shell rewrite
findings.evidence: lib/services/download_manager.dart:69-72 `/// Emits a human-readable message when a user-initiated download fails — without this a failure was indistinguishable from a success (the ring simply disappeared).` / `Stream<String> get errors => _errorController.stream;` and :141 `if (!_errorController.isClosed) _errorController.add('$e');`. Nothing in lib/ subscribes to it (grep for `.errors` finds only the definition). The shell's only toast source is lib/app/app_shell.dart:51 `_messagesSub = _services.handler.messages.listen(_showMessage);` (playback-path messages). `git log -S"DownloadManager.instance.errors"` shows the listener (`showAppSnackBar(... message: '下载未完成，请重试' ...)`) was deleted from main.dart in 9f47aea and never re-added. The remaining indicator is the red icon in `_DownloadsButton` (app_shell.dart:271-272), but app_shell.dart:211-218 renders `if (_searchActive) TextButton(onPressed: _exitSearch, child: const Text('取消' ...)) else ...[const _DownloadsButton(), ...]`, so it is not on screen in search, where downloads are started. lib/widgets/track_download_button.dart:146-153 simply falls back to the idle download glyph once the task is removed.
findings.failure_scenario: In search, tap the download arrow on a Bilibili result (or 下载 in the song sheet) while the CDN link fails / Bilibili is rate-limiting / the network drops. The ring disappears and the arrow comes back; no toast, no error state on the row, and the top-bar warning icon is replaced by 取消 for as long as search is open. The listener only finds out after leaving search and noticing the red icon. The same failure through 下载并播放 does toast (handler.messages), so the two paths disagree.
findings.fix: In _AppShellState.initState add a second subscription, e.g. `_downloadErrorsSub = DownloadManager.instance.errors.listen((_) => _showMessage('下载未完成，请重试'));` and cancel it in dispose (never show the raw exception string).

findings.title: Mini player does nothing on any page opened from the player (static NowPlayingPage._open latch)
findings.evidence: lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:44-49 `static bool _open = false;` ... `if (_open || AppServices.instance.handler.currentTrack == null) return;` / `_open = true;` and :76-78 `} finally { _open = false; }` — reset only when the pushed player route completes. The player's own sheet navigates away while that route is still in the stack: now_playing_page.dart:363-364 `TrackSheet.show(context, track, forPlayer: true)`, and lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:191-203 (not gated on forPlayer) `for (final artist in artists.take(2)) if (_library.artistNamed(artist) != null) SheetAction(... onTap: () { final parent = _dismiss(); ArtistPage.open(parent, artist); })`. The pushed page carries lib/screens/artist_page.dart:101 `const DockedPlayer(),` whose tap is lib/widgets/docked_player.dart:27 `unawaited(NowPlayingPage.open(context, from: rect));`.
findings.failure_scenario: Open the player, tap ⋯, tap the artist row (e.g. 周深). The artist page is pushed above the player with a docked mini player at the bottom. Tap a song there (it plays), then tap the mini player: nothing happens, because `_open` is still true. The same holds for the playlist page reached from that artist page via 存为歌单. The only way back to the player is the system/back arrow.
findings.fix: Remember the player's route instead of a bool (`static Route<void>? _route`), and when it is already in the stack make `open` return to it: `Navigator.of(context).popUntil((r) => r == _route)`; clear it in the `finally`.

findings.title: Batch add to a playlist reverses the order of the selection (two of the three callers miss the compensation)
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:703 `playlist.tracks.insertAll(0, toAdd.reversed.toList());` (doc at :684-687: 'the batch's last item ends up first'). lib/screens/artist_page.dart:34-36 knows this and compensates: `// Inserted front-first, so reverse to keep the page's order.` / `await DatabaseService.addTracksToPlaylist(playlist.id, group.tracks.reversed.toList());`. The other two callers pass display order unchanged: lib/screens/playlist_page.dart:407-409 `final picked = await _SongPicker.show(context, candidates); ... await DatabaseService.addTracksToPlaylist(playlist.id, picked);` (picked is built in picker order at :474-477), and lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:304 `await DatabaseService.addTracksToPlaylist(playlist.id, tracks);`, reached from playlist_page.dart:331-332 `PlaylistPicker.show(context, selectedTracks)` where selectedTracks is in playlist order (:311-314).
findings.failure_scenario: Playlist X holds A, B, C in that order. 编辑 → 全选 → 加入歌单 → 新建歌单 (or any other playlist): the target shows C, B, A. Likewise 添加歌曲: tick the first three rows of the picker and they land in the playlist in the opposite order to the one just shown.
findings.fix: Make the batch keep the caller's order (`playlist.tracks.insertAll(0, toAdd)`) and drop the `.reversed` in ArtistPage._saveAsPlaylist; update the doc comment.

findings.title: Player top bar leaves only (width − 312) px for its centre: sleep badge overflows its pill and the calibration hint shrinks to ~5 px on 360 dp phones
findings.evidence: lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:286-291 `Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 12), child: Row(children: [SizedBox(width: 144, ...` and :324-325 `SizedBox(width: 144,` — the Expanded centre gets screenWidth − 24 − 288. The badge (:715-732) is `Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 12, vertical: 6), child: Row(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min, children: [const Icon(Icons.bedtime_rounded, size: 14, ...), const SizedBox(width: 6), Text(sleep.mode == SleepTimerMode.endOfTrack ? '播完本首' : formatDuration(sleep.remaining), ...` — the Text is not Flexible, so it needs 44 px + text (≈74 px for mm:ss, ≈92 px for 播完本首). The hint (:309-320) is `FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown, child: Text('点一下正在唱的那句', style: TextStyle(... fontSize: 14 ...` ≈126 px wide. Both side boxes stay 144 px even when they hold only 重置 / 完成.
findings.failure_scenario: On a 360 dp-wide Android phone the centre is 48 px: with any sleep timer running the pill is 48 px wide and its text runs 26–44 px past it (a RenderFlex overflow in debug); during 校准 the only instruction is scaled to 48/126 ≈ 0.38 → ~5 px glyphs. On 390–393 dp phones (the width the goldens render at, without a timer) 播完本首 still overflows by 11–14 px and the hint is ~9 px.
findings.fix: Give the centre the room it needs: e.g. lay the bar out as a Stack with the badge/hint centred over a Row of the two button groups sized to their content, or size the side boxes to their content while calibrating / when fewer than three buttons show; wrap the badge in a FittedBox(scaleDown) as a floor.

findings.title: Favouriting from a search/recommendation row stores Bilibili's raw copy instead of the library's named song
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:102-105 `Future<void> _toggleFavorite() async { Haptics.light(); await DatabaseService.toggleFavorite(widget.track); }` while the sheet itself knows better at :236-243 `/// The library's copy carries any edits made since the sheet's caller captured its [Track].` `Track _latest() {...}` (used for the header, 加入歌单 and 编辑信息 but not here). lib/services/database_service.dart:736 `favorites.tracks.insert(0, track);` stores that object verbatim. Search rows hand over Bilibili's own copy (lib/screens/search_view.dart:250 `_songs(_online.results)`; lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:616-625 `title: cleanTitle, rawTitle: cleanTitle, uploader: author, ...`, not named, no loudness).
findings.failure_scenario: A song is in the library as 大鱼 / 周深 (named). Search 周深, find the same video in the 哔哩哔哩 results (it shows ⋯ because it is downloaded), open the sheet — the header shows 大鱼 — and tap the heart. 收藏 now lists it as 【4K60帧】周深《大鱼》现场 纯享版 with the video thumbnail, and that copy is persisted in bilibeat_playlists.json until the next metadata edit of the song; the favourites cover on the home grid uses the thumbnail too.
findings.fix: `await DatabaseService.toggleFavorite(_latest());` (and likewise prefer the library copy inside DatabaseService.toggleFavorite when the id is downloaded).

findings.title: When the queue empties, the player pops whatever route is on top instead of itself, and can be left stale or blank
findings.evidence: lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:120-128 `if (track == null) { Future.microtask(() { if (!mounted) return; if (ModalRoute.of(context)?.isActive ?? false) { Navigator.of(context).maybePop(); } }); return; }` — `isActive` is true for any route still in the stack, `maybePop` pops the top-most route and honours the page's own PopScope (:195 `canPop: _calibrating == null`); no setState is made. A later rebuild hits :214 `child: track == null ? const SizedBox.shrink() : _player(track),` inside a non-positioned child of a Stack under the Scaffold's loose body constraints, so the Stack collapses to zero width (no artwork, no drag surface). Reachable because every row has lib/widgets/song_tile.dart:57 `onLongPress: () => TrackSheet.show(context, track, queue: queue)`, including queue rows (lib/widgets/playback_queue_sheet.dart:87), and lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:107-110 `final parent = _dismiss(); await DatabaseService.removeDownloadedTrack(track);` leads to lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:861-865 `if (_player.sequenceState.sequence.isEmpty) { await _player.stop(); _announce(null); _publish(); }`.
findings.failure_scenario: Play the single song of an artist (queue = 1), open the player, open 播放队列, long-press the row → 删除下载. The queue sheet is popped instead of the player; the player keeps showing the deleted song with dead transport controls. Tapping the artwork/歌词 (setState) turns the page into an empty dark screen with no controls — on iOS there is then no way to leave it. Same outcome when an artist/playlist page sits above the player (it gets popped), or while calibrating (PopScope swallows the pop and _endCalibration rebuilds to blank).
findings.fix: Remove this page's own route: `_endCalibration(); final route = ModalRoute.of(context); if (route != null && route.isActive) Navigator.of(context).removeRoute(route);` (or popUntil(route) then pop), instead of maybePop.

findings.title: 播放 from a queue row's long-press sheet replaces the queue with the whole library
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/playback_queue_sheet.dart:87-90 `child: SongTile(track: track, // Tapping the current song does not restart it.` `onTap: current ? null : () => _select(track.id),` — no `queue:` is passed. lib/widgets/song_tile.dart:57 `onLongPress: () => TrackSheet.show(context, track, queue: queue),` → lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:90-91 `unawaited(AppServices.instance.handler.playTrack(widget.track, queue: widget.queue));` → lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:643 `final base = (queue == null || queue.isEmpty) ? library.values : queue;`.
findings.failure_scenario: Start a 5-song playlist, open the player's 播放队列, long-press a row and tap 播放 in its sheet. Instead of jumping to that song inside the queue (what a tap does), the queue is reinstalled as every downloaded song in the library; the playlist context and its order are gone.
findings.fix: Pass the queue to the row (`SongTile(track: track, queue: snapshot.tracks, ...)`) so the sheet's 播放 stays within it.

findings.title: Song-info sheet reports 'no match' and 'save failed' with snack bars that render underneath the sheet
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:66-68 `if (found == null) { showAppSnackBar(ScaffoldMessenger.of(context), message: '没有匹配到这首歌'); return; }` and :107 `showAppSnackBar(ScaffoldMessenger.of(context), message: '保存失败，请重试');`. The sheet is a modal route with no Scaffold of its own (lib/widgets/sheet.dart:13 `return showModalBottomSheet<T>(`), so the root ScaffoldMessenger draws the bar in the page Scaffolds below the barrier; lib/utils/snack.dart:22-24 places it floating at the page's bottom edge (`margin: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 48, vertical: 12)`), exactly where the ~300 px sheet sits. Other sheets pop before showing a snack (e.g. settings_sheet.dart:107-110); this one stays open.
findings.failure_scenario: 编辑信息 → tap 匹配 on a video the catalogues do not know (or while offline). The spinner stops and nothing else changes: the message '没有匹配到这首歌' is drawn behind the sheet and has expired by the time the sheet closes. A failed save looks the same — the button re-enables with no explanation.
findings.fix: Show the outcome inside the sheet (e.g. a short inline line under the 匹配 row / above 保存 held in state), or wrap the sheet body in its own ScaffoldMessenger + transparent Scaffold.

findings.title: Scrolling local matches pages a hidden, stale Bilibili query in the background
findings.evidence: lib/screens/search_view.dart:77-81 `if (widget.query.value.trim().isEmpty) { _recs.loadMore(); } else if (_online.hasSearched && _online.results.isNotEmpty) { _online.loadMore(); }` — it never checks that the online results belong to what is typed, although the view itself does at :188 `final submitted = _online.query == query;` and only shows them when true. The controller keeps the old query until the field is emptied (lib/app/app_shell.dart:92 `if (text.trim().isEmpty) _services.onlineSearch.clear();`). The class doc promises (:22-23) 'Bilibili is only queried on submit ... so typing never fires network requests.'
findings.failure_scenario: Submit 周深 (Bilibili results load), then edit the field to 周. The view now shows only library matches for 周 plus the 在哔哩哔哩搜索 row. Scrolling that list to within 320 px of its end fires `BilibiliSdk.search('周深', page: 2)`, then page 3 on the next scroll, and so on — invisible requests against a service that rate-limits this app, and when the user returns to 周深 the list has silently grown by several pages.
findings.fix: Gate on the visible query: `else if (_online.query == widget.query.value.trim() && _online.results.isNotEmpty) _online.loadMore();`.

findings.title: The 重试 button for a failed results page is ignored for its first three seconds
findings.evidence: lib/state/online_search_controller.dart:96-101 `// A failed page gets a quiet retry window instead of re-firing on every scroll pixel.` `if (_loadMoreFailed && DateTime.now().difference(_lastFailure) < const Duration(seconds: 3)) { return; }` with :123-124 `_loadMoreFailed = true; _lastFailure = DateTime.now();`. The explicit button calls the very same method: lib/screens/search_view.dart:253-254 `else if (_online.loadMoreFailed) SliverToBoxAdapter(child: Center(child: _retry(_online.loadMore))),`.
findings.failure_scenario: Page 2 of a search fails (network blip). 重试 appears at that instant; tapping it within three seconds does nothing — no spinner, no request — so it looks broken. It only works on a later tap.
findings.fix: Let a deliberate retry bypass the window: `Future<void> loadMore({bool force = false})` skipping the time check when forced, and wire the button to `() => _online.loadMore(force: true)`.

findings.title: Recommendations paging has no failure back-off: every scroll notification at the end re-fires all seed searches
findings.evidence: lib/state/recommendations_controller.dart:62 `if (_loading || _loadingMore || _reachedEnd || _tracks.isEmpty) return;` and :81-86 `} catch (e) { debugPrint('Load more recommendations error: $e'); if (pass != _pass) return; } _loadingMore = false; notifyListeners();` — a failure records nothing. lib/screens/search_view.dart:74-78 calls `_recs.loadMore()` on every vertical ScrollNotification within 320 px of the end. The sibling controller was fixed for exactly this (online_search_controller.dart:96-101 'instead of re-firing on every scroll pixel'). One attempt is one search per seed (lib/services/recommendation_engine.dart:186-198, up to 4 seeds), each of which tries the music zone and then the unfiltered endpoint (lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:494-501).
findings.failure_scenario: Recommendations are on screen and Bilibili starts refusing requests (risk control) or the network drops. Dragging at the bottom of the list starts a new batch of up to 4 seeds × several requests as soon as the previous batch fails, for as long as the finger moves; the spinner flickers in and out, there is no 重试 row, and the burst deepens the rate limit the changelog already works around.
findings.fix: Mirror OnlineSearchController: keep `_loadMoreFailed`/`_lastFailure`, return early inside a few-second window, expose the flag and render a 重试 row in SearchView._recommendations.

findings.title: Home loses its lens and scroll position every time search is entered
findings.evidence: lib/app/app_shell.dart:133-146 `child: AnimatedSwitcher(... child: _searchActive ? SearchView(key: const ValueKey('search'), ...) : HomePage(key: const ValueKey('home'), onSearch: _searchFocus.requestFocus),` — HomePage leaves the tree while search is active, so its State is disposed. The lens lives only in that State: lib/screens/home_page.dart:45 `_Lens _lens = _Lens.songs;`, and the CustomScrollView (home_page.dart:77) has no PageStorageKey, so its offset is not kept either. `_checkProtection()` (home_page.dart:53) also re-runs each time.
findings.failure_scenario: Browse 歌手 (or 歌单), or scroll far down 歌曲; tap the search bar — even by accident — and 取消. Home comes back on 歌曲 scrolled to the top. Since search is the only way to add music, this happens on every download round-trip; a protection hint the user just acted on with 开启 (but has not yet granted) reappears as well.
findings.fix: Keep HomePage mounted while searching (IndexedStack/Offstage with the fade applied on top), or lift `_lens` into _AppShellState and give the scroll view a PageStorageKey.

findings.title: Orientation is not locked, and the player and the song sheet do not survive landscape
findings.evidence: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml: the MainActivity element has no `android:screenOrientation`; ios/Runner/Info.plist:62-67 lists `UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft` / `LandscapeRight` for iPhone; lib/main.dart never calls `SystemChrome.setPreferredOrientations`. lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:548-556 assumes the artwork is width-bound: `final art = box.maxWidth - 2 * _NowPlayingPageState._gutter;` ... `final spare = box.maxHeight - _rows - text - art;` `final s = spare < 96 ? 96.0 : spare;` — in landscape the fixed rows (222) plus the minimum gaps (96) take almost the whole height. lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:126-231 is a `Column(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min, ...)` with no scroll view (header + primary button + up to six 52 px actions ≈ 480 px).
findings.failure_scenario: With auto-rotate on, turn a 412×915 phone sideways on the player: the safe box is ~364 px high, leaving ~86 px for the Expanded area and, after its 38 px padding, a ~48 px artwork; in lyrics mode the pane is shorter than one lyric line. On a 360×640 phone the artwork is 0–20 px. Opening ⋯ in landscape overflows the sheet so 编辑信息 / 删除下载 are cut off below the screen. (An artwork first loaded at that size also stays a tiny thumbnail after rotating back, since CachedCoverImage only reloads on a URL change.)
findings.fix: Lock to portrait: `await SystemChrome.setPreferredOrientations([DeviceOrientation.portraitUp]);` in main(), `android:screenOrientation="portrait"` on the activity, and drop the landscape entries from UISupportedInterfaceOrientations (iPhone).

findings.title: Artist splitter treats any name starting with 'feat' or 'ft' as a separator
findings.evidence: lib/state/library_controller.dart:122-123 `static final RegExp _artistSeparators = RegExp(r'\s*(?:[&、,，/／×]|\bfeat\.?|\bft\.?)\s*', caseSensitive: false);` — `\bfeat\.?` / `\bft\.?` have a leading word boundary but nothing after, so they match the first letters of a longer word. Used by :129-133 `artistNamesOf(track) => artistOf(track).split(_artistSeparators).map((name) => name.trim()).where((name) => name.isNotEmpty).toList();`, which feeds the 歌手 lens (:146-151), the artist rows in the song sheet (track_sheet.dart:124, 192-203) and `LyricsEngine.knownArtists` (:219-225). The rows themselves show the unsplit credit via `artistOf`.
findings.failure_scenario: A song credited to FTISLAND (named, or an untouched download whose UP主 is e.g. 'Feather羽毛') is split into ['', 'ISLAND'] / ['', 'her羽毛']: the 歌手 lens and the song sheet show an artist called ISLAND while the song row says FTISLAND, and 'ISLAND' is taught to the offline title parser as a known artist.
findings.fix: Require the token to end: `r'\s*(?:[&、,，/／×]|\bfeat(?:\.|\b)|\bft(?:\.|\b))\s*'` (a dot or a word boundary after feat/ft).

find:screens abef45.notes:
Read-only audit; nothing was built, run or modified, and no network requests were made. Plugin/SDK behaviour was checked from source (just_audio 0.10.6 positionStream/createPositionStream, rxdart 0.28.0 subject stream equality, Flutter scaffold.dart body constraints, routes.dart pointer-ignoring during pop, reorderable_list.dart onReorderItem semantics). Only parts of lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart, lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart, CHANGELOG.md and ios/Runner/Info.plist were read (grep/excerpts), so they are not in filesRead.

Checked and found sound:
- BuildContext/setState after await: every async path in the scoped screens either captures navigator/messenger first or checks mounted/context.mounted (home protection hint, playlist remove/reorder/rename/delete/add, artist save-as-playlist, settings, lyrics sheet hand-off, calibration error path).
- Disposal: AppShell (observer, messages sub, focus node, text controller, query notifier), NowPlayingPage (nowPlaying listener, position sub/notifier, auto-advance hold released on every path incl. dispose), SettingsSheet observer, LyricsView/MarqueeText timers and controllers. No listener is added twice.
- Index safety: all list builders index immutable snapshots (LibraryController hands out unmodifiable lists; PlaylistPage copies the live playlist list each build), so in-place DB mutation of Playlist.tracks cannot produce a RangeError. Reorder indices match DatabaseService._moveWithin under onReorderItem semantics; rapid consecutive reorders stay consistent because the DB list is mutated in place before the persist.
- Search bar state machine: focus -> active, 取消/Back -> exit, onDrag keyboard dismissal keeps search open, PopScope(canPop: !_searchActive) is correct, whitespace-only queries are treated as empty, request tokens prevent stale results after clear/exit.
- New playlist / save-as-playlist open the page only after the library reload has landed (stream delivery and reload are all microtasks after the write), so the 'deleted elsewhere' blank scaffold is not shown on open.
- Artist grouping and sort caches are invalidated correctly (identity of the downloaded list, TrackCredit.reset when the taught set changes).
- _Spacing in portrait: no negative sizes; the Expanded artwork absorbs any shortfall. Verified by hand for 320x568 and 360x640 at text scale 2.0 and for tablets; the text-scale term matches the real growth of the title/artist/time rows.
- Safe areas: search bar (top), DockedPlayer/MiniPlayer (bottom inset, also when hidden), edit bar, sheets (useSafeArea + viewInsets), player page.
- handler.playTrack/playCollection resolve every queued item to the library copy by id, so stale Track copies passed from lists do not reach the queue or now-playing display.

Observed but deliberately not reported as findings:
- 歌名/歌手 sort uses String.compareTo on lower-cased UTF-16 (CJK ordered by code point, not pinyin) and List.sort is not stable for equal keys; a limitation rather than a regression.
- SongTile's fixed 64 pt extent overflows only at text scale of roughly 1.7 and above; playlist/artist grid cells overflow by a few px into their spacing at 1.3 on 360 dp.
- 删除下载 in the song sheet has no confirmation (the same action in 下载管理 does); it has been that way since v4, so treated as intent, but a mis-tap permanently loses audio for videos since removed from Bilibili.
- promptForText disposes its TextEditingController while the dialog is still animating out (debug-only assertion risk, nothing in release).
- TrackInfoSheet._save does Navigator.pop(context) after the awaits guarded only by mounted; if the sheet is dismissed during the short save window it would pop the page beneath. Window is tens of ms.
- just_audio leaks one position pipeline each time the last positionStream listener goes away and comes back (AppShell removes DockedPlayer while the keyboard is open); cost is negligible.
- ArtistPage 存为歌单 has no re-entrancy guard (a fast double tap creates two playlists).
- A non-downloaded playlist song started via 下载并播放 is inserted at queue index 0 rather than at its playlist position (the queue captured for the sheet predates the download).
- There are no widget tests for AppShell, HomePage, SearchView, PlaylistPage or ArtistPage; NowPlayingPage is exercised only through the lyrics tests' harness, and render_screens.dart renders at 390 pt without a sleep timer, which is why the top-bar overflow is not visible in the goldens.

findings.title: After the 30-minute idle stop the Android service keeps its wake lock (and foreground state) while the activity still exists
findings.evidence:
lib/main.dart:50 `androidStopForegroundOnPause: false` with the comment at :48-49 "The handler stops the service itself after a long pause, so the notification does not linger." The handler does this at lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:335-337 (`_idleTimer = Timer(_idleStopAfter, () { if (!_player.playing) unawaited(stop()); })`) and :783 `await super.stop()`.

audio_service-0.18.19 AudioService.java: the wake lock is taken at :710 in enterPlayingState (`acquireWakeLock()`), and released in only two places: :721-723 exitForegroundState (reached only via :716 `if (config.androidStopForegroundOnPause)`), and :381 in onDestroy. The idle transition runs :355-358 `stop() { deactivateMediaSession(); stopSelf(); }` - no stopForeground, no releaseWakeLock. AudioServicePlugin.java connects a MediaBrowserCompat to the service in onAttachedToActivity (:321-322 `connect()`) and only disconnects in onDetachedFromActivity (:359), so while the Activity instance exists (app merely backgrounded / in recents) the service is bound and stopSelf() does not destroy it; onDestroy, the only remaining release site, does not run. Deduced from plugin source; not verified on a device.
findings.failure_scenario: Play a song, pause, press Home and leave the phone (app stays in recents, the normal case). After 30 minutes handler.stop() runs, but because the activity's MediaBrowser binding keeps AudioService alive, onDestroy never runs: the PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK acquired on first play stays held and the service stays in the foreground state (its notification cannot be cancelled by NotificationManager.cancel while foreground) until the task is swiped away or the process is killed. The CPU cannot deep-sleep overnight - exactly the lingering the idle stop was written to avoid.
findings.fix: Do not rely on stopSelf() for release. Either keep androidStopForegroundOnPause true and solve the Android 12 resume problem differently, or on the idle stop explicitly drop foreground/wake lock (e.g. a small native call from MainActivity's channel that calls stopForeground(STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE) on AudioService.instance and releases the lock), and verify with `adb shell dumpsys power | grep -i audioservice` after the idle stop.

findings.title: Error-skip of an unplayable file reports idle while still playing, which makes audio_service deactivate the media session for the rest of playback
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:68-70 `// A missing or corrupt file skips ahead instead of stalling. maxSkipsOnError: 3`. `_broadcastState` forwards the raw state: :359-366 `processingState: const { ja.ProcessingState.idle: AudioProcessingState.idle, ... }[_player.processingState]!, playing: playing`.

just_audio-0.10.6 AudioPlayer.java:947-954 sendError sets `processingState = ProcessingState.idle` and broadcasts; just_audio.dart:1593-1597 on idle calls `_setPlatformActive(false)` without touching `playing`; :417-424 the maxSkipsOnError listener then does `seekToNext()`, and seek (:1330-1331) re-activates because `playing && !_active`. So `playing` stays true across idle -> loading -> ready.

audio_service-0.18.19 AudioService.java:559-570: `if (!wasPlaying && playing) enterPlayingState(); ... if (oldProcessingState != idle && processingState == idle) { stop(); }` and :355-358 `stop() { deactivateMediaSession(); stopSelf(); }` (:746-751 sets the session inactive and cancels the notification). The Dart side also calls stopService on the same transition (audio_service.dart:1132-1134). Because `playing` never goes false->true again, enterPlayingState (:705-713, the only place that calls mediaSession.setActive(true)/startForeground) is not re-run.
findings.failure_scenario: A queued file is corrupt or missing (DB lists it as downloaded; restoreSession/_library never stat the file). Playback reaches it in the background: ExoPlayer errors, the handler broadcasts idle+playing, audio_service deactivates the MediaSession and cancels the notification, then just_audio skips to the next song and music continues. From then on the lock-screen/notification controls and headset buttons are gone (session inactive) while audio plays, until the user opens the app and toggles pause/play.
findings.fix: In _broadcastState, never publish AudioProcessingState.idle while `_player.playing` is true (map it to loading/buffering), so the transient idle of an error skip does not reach audio_service; only stop()/an emptied queue should produce idle.

findings.title: Deleting a download that sits before the playing song briefly announces the following song and records it in 最近播放
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:853-859 removeTracks calls `await _player.removeAudioSourceAt(i)`. just_audio-0.10.6 just_audio.dart:3088-3100 removeAt first mutates `children`, then `await player._broadcastSequence()` (which emits `sequenceState.copyWith(sequence: ...)`, :963-967, keeping the old currentIndex) and only then sends concatenatingRemoveRange to the platform; the corrected index arrives later via a playback event (:324-326, Java onTimelineChanged -> updateCurrentIndex, AudioPlayer.java:304-306). SequenceState.currentIndex (:2155-2156) only clamps to the last item, it does not shift.

The handler publishes on every sequence event (:187 `_player.sequenceStateStream.listen((_) => _publish())`), and :229-231 `if (current?.id != previous?.id) { _announce(current); }` -> :283 `if (_recordHistory) unawaited(DatabaseService.addRecentlyPlayed(track));` plus mediaItem.add and _applyLoudness for the wrong track. removeTracks has no test (no reference in test/playback_handler_test.dart).
findings.failure_scenario: Queue [A, B, C, D], C is playing (index 2). The user deletes A's download from a list (track_sheet.dart:110 / download_management_sheet.dart:101). Dart's sequence becomes [B, C, D] with index still 2, so _publish announces D: D is written to the recently-played history as if it had been played, the notification/now-playing title and loudness gain flip to D, and a moment later the native index (1) arrives and C is announced again. Net result: a song never heard appears in 最近播放 and the UI/volume flickers.
findings.fix: Hold publishing across the removal the way _install does (increment _installing around the removeAudioSourceAt loop and publish once afterwards, after the platform call has returned and the index event has been delivered), or in _publish ignore a current-track change whose previous track is still in the sequence at index-1 while a removal is in flight.

findings.title: play() during an in-flight restoreSession returns without playing (the cold-start case the comment says is handled)
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:689-692 `Future<void> restoreSession() async { if (_restoreStarted) return; _restoreStarted = true; ...` - a second caller gets an already-completed future, not the running restore. :750-756 `if (_player.audioSources.isEmpty) { // A media button can cold-start the service before the UI restores. await restoreSession(); if (_player.audioSources.isEmpty) return; }`. lib/main.dart:58 always starts the restore first: `unawaited(handler.restoreSession());` immediately after AudioService.init, so by the time any platform `play`/`click` message can be dispatched `_restoreStarted` is already true.
findings.failure_scenario: Process was killed; the app (or the service via a headset button) starts. main() kicks off restoreSession (reads bilibeat_session.json and the library, then loads the queue natively). A headset/Bluetooth play press delivered before that finishes calls play(): restoreSession() returns immediately, audioSources is still empty, play() returns - the press is silently dropped and the session is then restored paused. The window is the duration of the restore (file IO + native load), longer with a large library.
findings.fix: Memoize the restore future (`Future<void>? _restore; Future<void> restoreSession() => _restore ??= _doRestore();`) so play() actually awaits the running restore before checking audioSources.

find:playback ac30e4.notes:
Method: read all nine scope files in full plus the manifest, then traced the handler's calls into just_audio 0.10.6 (Dart + Android AudioPlayer.java), audio_service 0.18.19 (Dart + AudioService.java / AudioServicePlugin.java) and audio_session 0.2.4 from the pub cache. Nothing was run; the first two findings are deductions from plugin source and should be confirmed on a device (dumpsys power / media_session) before fixing. The test files were only grepped, not read in full.

Checked and found sound:
- Install/selection races: _selection token + _installing hold + PlayerInterruptedException handling; rapid taps, a superseded download (_ensureLocal/preparing), restore overtaken by a tap. just_audio's _load reshuffles around the initial index, so shuffle starts and restores put the current track first.
- Rapid Next (_navTarget), previous-restarts-after-3s, manual skip under repeat-one, end of a non-looping queue (parks paused at first), skipToQueueItem/selectQueueTrack index mapping under shuffle.
- Concurrent removeTracks calls: queue ids are de-duplicated and each event carries one id, and removeAt is serialized by just_audio's lock, so stale snapshots cannot remove a wrong item. SequenceState.currentIndex clamps, so removing the last/current item cannot throw in _publish.
- Loudness: gain clamp (-14..+8 dB), -11 LUFS assumption for unmeasured tracks, measured_i only accepted when < 0, Track.copyWith never clears loudness, enhancer units (just_audio converts dB to millibel), enhancer state re-sent on platform re-activation, volume re-applied on activation.
- Audio focus: handleInterruptions:false still activates the session in play(); audio_session's begin/end types (transient -> pause/pause, permanent -> unknown, duck) match the handler's resume logic; becoming-noisy clears the resume flag; user pause/stop/sleep timer clear it.
- Session persistence: saved on pause, every 20 s while playing and 2 s after queue changes; empty state never overwrites; corrupt/missing file -> null; ids missing from the library are dropped; missing current id falls back to index 0 at position zero. After _player.stop() just_audio's idle player keeps index and position, so resuming after the idle stop continues where it was.
- Sleep timer: both modes, cancel/replace, stop clears, 300 ms end-of-track window vs just_audio's <=200 ms position tick; native seek events arrive before the seek result so manual skips are not misread as auto-advance.
- Metadata edits: updateTrackMetadata -> _latest -> _publish updates nowPlaying (TrackNotifier), mediaItem and queue; TrackNaming re-reads the stored track before saving.
- Manifest: mediaPlayback FGS type and permission, WAKE_LOCK, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, MediaButtonReceiver all present; MainActivity channel methods match BackgroundProtection.

Minor things seen but not reported as findings: (1) just_audio re-randomises the shuffle order on every platform activation, so the shuffled queue order changes after the 30-minute idle stop; (2) after that idle stop, deleting the current song leaves the next song current at the deleted song's old position (the idle player keeps _position); (3) a failed install can emit two snackbar messages (the install failure and the errorStream one); (4) a first media-button press on a fully cold process is dropped by audio_service itself (listener null in onMediaButtonEvent) before Dart is up, independent of the restore race reported above; (5) seek() is a no-op in just_audio while processingState is loading, so a Next/queue tap in the few hundred ms of a queue install is ignored.

findings.title: A write error mid-download (disk full) makes the download hang forever instead of failing
findings.evidence:
audio_download_service.dart:534-543: `await for (final chunk in timeoutRes) { sink.add(chunk); received += chunk.length; ... } await sink.flush();` with `sink = part.openWrite(...)` (502/522). Nothing listens to `sink.done`.

Dart SDK io_sink.dart (`_StreamSinkImpl`, ~/flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/lib/io/io_sink.dart:233-272): the first `add` starts `_target.addStream(_controller.stream)`; when that fails while no flush is in progress (`_isBound == false`) the onError branch only calls `_completeDoneError` and neither completes nor clears `_controllerCompleter` / `_controllerInstance`. `flush()` (184-197) then does `var future = _controllerCompleter!.future; _controllerInstance!.close(); return future...` and that future is never completed. file_impl.dart:225-229 shows a failed `writeFrom` cancels the subscription and completes addStream with the error, i.e. exactly that branch.

So after ENOSPC on any chunk before the last, later `sink.add` calls are dropped silently, the loop keeps pulling the whole file off the network, and `await sink.flush()` never returns. `_transfer` never returns, so `ensureDownloaded`'s `finally { _inFlight.remove(id) }` (291-293) and `DownloadManager.startDownload`'s `finally { _tasks.remove(...) }` (download_manager.dart:142-145) never run. The handler's `_ensureLocal` (audio_player_handler.dart:608) awaits the same future with no timeout.
findings.failure_scenario: Storage fills up while a song downloads (or is already full when one starts: the .part is created, the first write fails). The ring runs to 100% and stays there; the row says 下载中 with its tap disabled, the track sheet shows a dead percentage button, and a song tapped for playback shows 正在准备「…」 indefinitely. No 下载失败 message is ever shown and no retry is offered. Every later attempt on that track in the session joins the hung `_inFlight` future, so it cannot be retried until the app process is restarted, and the same thing happens again while the disk is full. The whole file is also fetched over the network for nothing.
findings.fix: Surface the sink's error. For example, replace the IOSink with a RandomAccessFile and `await raf.writeFrom(chunk)` per chunk (this also gives backpressure), or keep the IOSink and race the loop against `sink.done`: attach `sink.done.catchError(...)` to record the error, check it after each `add`, and throw it instead of calling `flush()` once it is set.

findings.title: Timed-out requests are never aborted, so each one permanently occupies a pooled connection; `getUrl` in the download path then waits forever
findings.evidence:
audio_download_service.dart:432 `final req = await _client.getUrl(Uri.parse(url));` (no timeout) and 443-446 `final res = await req.close().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 15), onTimeout: () => throw TimeoutException('CDN close timeout'));`. `Future.timeout` only abandons the future: the request is not aborted (`req.abort()` is never called anywhere in lib), so the connection stays in the target's `_active` set until a response is fully consumed or the socket errors. If headers arrive after the 15 s, the `HttpClientResponse` has no listener, the parser pauses the socket, and the connection is never returned.

The client is built with `maxConnectionsPerHost = 4` (bili_http.dart:17, used at audio_download_service.dart:47-50). Dart SDK http_impl.dart:2664-2673: when `_active.length + _connecting >= maxConnectionsPerHost`, `connect` parks the caller in `_pending` and returns a completer with no timeout; `connectionTimeout` (2706-2708) covers only the socket connect.

Same pattern in bilibili_sdk.dart:34-47 (`getUrl(...).timeout(10s)`, `req.close().timeout(10s)`, `.join().timeout(10s)`), client limit 10 per host (bilibili_sdk.dart:26-28); the body timeout also leaves its subscription uncancelled.
findings.failure_scenario: On a slow or restricted route to Bilibili (the case the 0.1.2 notes mention), a CDN host takes more than 15 s to send response headers four times over the life of the process (the app can stay alive for days behind the playback service). Each attempt reports 下载失败 but leaves its connection counted as active. The fifth download from that host blocks inside `_client.getUrl` with no timeout: the ring sits at 0 forever, `_inFlight` and `DownloadManager._tasks` are never cleared, and the track cannot be retried until the app is restarted. For api.bilibili.com the same leak ten times over makes every `_httpGet` time out at `getUrl`: search fails to load and `fetchAudioStream` returns null (无法获取音源下载链接) for the rest of the session.
findings.fix: Abort on timeout: `req.close().timeout(d, onTimeout: () { req.abort(); throw TimeoutException(...); })`, and put a timeout on `_client.getUrl` in `_transfer`. In `_httpGet`, abort the request on the close timeout and read the body through a subscription that is cancelled on timeout (e.g. `res.timeout(...)` on the stream rather than `.join().timeout(...)`).

findings.title: Re-downloading a song stores the caller's un-named copy, and automatic matching then overwrites the listener's own naming in playlists
findings.evidence:
database_service.dart:767-771 `saveDownloadedTrack(Track track)`: `if (_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id)) return; _downloadedTracks.insert(0, track);` inserts whatever copy the download was started with (audio_download_service.dart:352 passes the `track` given to `ensureDownloaded`). `removeDownloadedTrack` (779-786) drops the index entry and, through `AudioDownloadService.delete` (audio_download_service.dart:229-235), the `audio_<id>.json` metadata, while its doc comment (775-778) promises that playlist membership and metadata stay.

library_controller.dart:201-203 `if (!known.contains(track.id)) TrackNaming.autoName(track);` runs for every id new to the downloaded list. track_naming.dart `_name` reads only the downloaded copy (`final before = await _stored(track.id); if (before == null || _settled(before)) return;`) and then `_save` -> `DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata`, which replaces the copy in every playlist and in recents (database_service.dart:532-544).
findings.failure_scenario: The listener names a song by hand in 编辑信息 (matcher 0) and keeps it in 收藏 or a playlist. They delete its download to free space, and later download it again from search results or a pasted BV number. The search-result Track (video title, UP主, not named) becomes the 本地 entry, so the song shows its video title again there and in playback (the queue uses the library copy). Being new to the library and not settled, it is auto-matched; the matcher's answer is then written over the hand-named copy in the playlist/收藏 and in recents. The listener's naming is lost, contrary to the rule that it is never overwritten automatically.
findings.fix: In `saveDownloadedTrack`, when the id is not in the downloaded list, prefer an existing stored copy of the same id (playlists, then recents) for title, uploader, cover, named, rawUploader and matcher, taking only loudness from the incoming track; write the metadata file from that merged copy.

findings.title: A failed download stays listed as 下载失败 after the same song is fetched successfully by playback
findings.evidence: download_manager.dart:148-157 `_onProgress`: `final task = _tasks[p.trackId]; if (task == null) { if (p.done) _notify(p.trackId); return; }` only relays the id; `_failed` is removed solely in `retryDownload` (94), `dismissFailed` (107) and after a new `startDownload` claims the slot (130). `startDownload` returns at 127 (`if (alreadyDownloaded) return;`) before reaching 130. download_management_sheet.dart:133-159 renders every `_failed` entry, and library_controller.dart reads `failedTasks.length` into `_failedCount`.
findings.failure_scenario: A download started with the row button fails (network drop). The listener taps the song to play it; the handler's `ensureDownloaded` resumes the .part and finishes. The song is now in 本地 and plays, but the 下载 sheet still shows it under 下载失败 with 重试/忽略 next to its downloaded row, and the failed count on the home page stays raised until the listener taps one of them or restarts the app.
findings.fix: In `_onProgress`, when `p.done` arrives for an id, also `_failed.remove(p.trackId)` before notifying; likewise clear `_failed` in `startDownload` when `alreadyDownloaded` is true.

findings.title: Partial downloads that are abandoned are never cleaned up and cannot be seen or removed in the app
findings.evidence: audio_download_service.dart:354-359 keeps `audio_<id>.m4a.part` and `.part.json` on any failure by design; 275 `await saveTrackMetadata(track)` creates `audio_<id>.json` before any byte is fetched. The only code that removes these files is `delete(track)` (229-235), reached only through `removeDownloadedTrack`, which the UI offers only for downloaded tracks (track_sheet.dart `if (downloaded) ... 删除下载`; download_management_sheet.dart:160-170). `DownloadManager.dismissFailed` (download_manager.dart:106-108) only drops the in-memory record. `storageBreakdown` (201) counts only `.m4a` files with a `.ready` marker, and `_discoverAudioFiles` (database_service.dart:221) looks only at `.ready` files, so nothing sweeps the leftovers.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener starts a long video by mistake (there is no cancel, so the way out is to close the app) or a download fails and is dismissed with 忽略. Tens of megabytes of `.part` stay in `bilibeat_audio/` for good unless that exact track is later downloaded to completion. They are not included in the 下载 sheet's size total and there is no in-app way to delete them short of clearing all app data, which would also delete the library.
findings.fix: Delete the track's `.part`, `.part.json` and (when no `.ready` exists) `.json` in `dismissFailed`, and sweep at startup in `_discoverAudioFiles`: remove `.part`/`.part.json` and marker-less metadata files older than a few days.

find:downloads a6d0e7.notes:
Nothing was run and no network request was made; SDK behaviour was checked from the Dart sources in ~/flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/lib (io/io_sink.dart, io/file_impl.dart, _http/http_impl.dart). The two test files named as context were not read. Excerpts only of audio_player_handler.dart, track_sheet.dart, track_naming.dart and library_controller.dart.

Checked and found sound:
- Resume logic in _transfer: If-Range with a strong ETag or Last-Modified; 206 accepted only when Content-Range start, total and validator agree; 200 after a Range request replaces the part; 416 accepted only when the recorded total equals the bytes on disk; a part with no note is discarded; truncated bodies are caught by the total check and the part is kept for resume.
- Chunk stall timeout (30 s) cancels the response subscription, which destroys the socket; non-200/206 and text/JSON bodies are drained.
- Two downloads of one track: _inFlight is claimed synchronously before any await; DownloadManager's _tasks and _pendingIsDownloadedCheck guard double taps; a tracked download joining a playback-path one still gets progress by id.
- File naming: ids are restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80} before becoming a path; multi-part ids (bvid_p<page>) give distinct files.
- Index vs disk: startup discovery re-adds .ready files from their metadata and prunes index entries whose files are gone; delete removes the .ready marker first and resets the memo.
- Track.audioUrl is persisted but never set anywhere in lib, so an expired stored link cannot be reused; every attempt asks for a fresh link.
- No batch-download caller exists, so there is no unbounded download concurrency.
- TrackDownloadButton state transitions (mounted mid-download, completion with no intermediate event, row recycling) and the management sheet's membership comparison.

Smaller observations not reported as findings:
- The 416 "already complete" path skips the `received < 1024` sanity check; it would need a server that repeatedly serves the same sub-1 KB non-text body, which I could not ground.
- If creating the .ready marker fails (error swallowed at audio_download_service.dart:345), the track is still memoised and indexed as downloaded for the session, then pruned on next launch with the .m4a left behind; I could not establish a realistic trigger.
- There is no backpressure between the socket and the file sink (chunks are buffered in memory if the network outpaces storage); not a practical problem at audio sizes.
- Could not determine without the network: whether playurl with fnval=16 actually returns durl, how AVPlayer handles a DASH audio segment saved as .m4a, and whether Android freezes a download started with nothing playing when the app is backgrounded.

findings.title: Re-downloading a song from search discards the listener's own name/cover kept in 收藏/playlists, and auto-matching then overwrites those copies too
findings.evidence: database_service.dart:767-772 `saveDownloadedTrack`: `if (_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id)) return; _downloadedTracks.insert(0, track);` - it inserts whatever copy the caller holds and never looks at the copies the collection still has. database_service.dart:775-778 documents that removal 'preserves the user's collection: playlist membership, Favorites, metadata and history all stay', while audio_download_service.dart:229-235 deletes the per-track meta JSON, so the playlist/recent copies are the ONLY place the edit survives. Search rows hand their own raw Track to the download (track_sheet.dart:99 `DownloadManager.instance.startDownload(widget.track)`, :90 `playTrack(widget.track)`), built in bilibili_sdk.dart with `rawTitle: title` and named=false. Then library_controller.dart:202-204 calls `TrackNaming.autoName(track)` for the new id; track_naming.dart:121-122 reads the downloaded copy (unnamed, so not settled) and track_naming.dart:188-196 -> :115 `DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata(track)`, which at database_service.dart:532-537 and :540-543 replaces every playlist and recent copy with the matcher's answer (matcher = 4, catalogue cover).
findings.failure_scenario: The listener names a song by hand in 编辑信息 (matcher 0, custom cover) and favourites it. Later they delete the download to free space (收藏 still shows their name and cover, as designed). Weeks later they find the video in search and tap 下载. The library entry is created from the search copy with the raw video title and UP主; 收藏 and 本地 now show two different names for the same id. As soon as the automatic matcher finds a song, updateTrackMetadata overwrites the 收藏/playlist/history copies as well: the hand-entered title, artist and picked cover are gone (and the picked cover file is deleted by _sweepCovers a day later). A listener-named track (matcher 0) is supposed never to be revisited by the matcher.
findings.fix: In saveDownloadedTrack, when the id is not in _downloadedTracks, look for an existing copy in _playlists / _recentlyPlayed and, if one isNamed (or has matcher == 0), insert that copy (keeping the new audioUrl/loudness via copyWith) instead of the caller's; also force-write its meta JSON.

findings.title: 收藏 from a track sheet stores the caller's stale Track instead of the library's copy
findings.evidence: track_sheet.dart:102-105 `await DatabaseService.toggleFavorite(widget.track);` while the same sheet deliberately resolves the fresh copy for everything else: track_sheet.dart:236-243 `_latest()` ('The library's copy carries any edits made since the sheet's caller captured its [Track]') is used for display (:121), 加入歌单 (:188 `PlaylistPicker.show(parent, [track])`) and 编辑信息 (:210). database_service.dart:736 `favorites.tracks.insert(0, track);` persists that object verbatim, and playlist_page.dart:73-75 / song_tile.dart:98 render the playlist's own copy (`track.title`).
findings.failure_scenario: A song is downloaded and named 大鱼 / 周深 (by matching or by hand, possibly with a picked cover). The listener later meets the same video in search results, long-presses the row and taps the heart. The sheet header shows 大鱼 (from _latest), but 收藏 receives the search-result Track: title = the full video title, uploader = the UP主, the video thumbnail, named = false. The 收藏 page shows the raw video title for that row permanently, since the library copy is already settled and nothing calls updateTrackMetadata for it again; the same song shows two names in 本地 and 收藏.
findings.fix: Use `_latest()` in `_toggleFavorite` (as the other actions do), or have DatabaseService.toggleFavorite/addTracksToPlaylist prefer the `_downloadedTracks` entry with the same id over the passed object.

findings.title: Cover cache eviction sorts by file access time, which Android/iOS app storage does not maintain - it evicts the oldest-downloaded (library) covers, not the least used
findings.evidence: cached_cover_image.dart:55-57 'the covers unused longest go'; :73 `files.sort((a, b) => a.$2.accessed.compareTo(b.$2.accessed));` then :74-78 deletes from the front until under 3/4 of 200 MB. Nothing in the read path touches the file's atime explicitly (:190-193 just `_settle(token, file)`), so the order depends on the filesystem updating atime on read. Android's /data (and iOS app containers) are mounted noatime, so `accessed` stays at creation time. The only test (test/cover_cache_test.dart:15) sets atime by hand with setLastAccessed, so it cannot see this. The cache is the only local copy of every cover (:181-182), and it is filled by search/recommendation browsing as well as the library.
findings.failure_scenario: After months of browsing search results the cache passes 200 MB. On the next launch trimCache deletes ~50 MB of the files with the oldest atime - on Android those are the first covers ever fetched, i.e. the listener's long-standing library songs shown every day - while keeping thumbnails of search results seen once last week. Offline (the app is meant to play from local files without a connection) those library rows and the player page show the placeholder note icon until the device is online again; online they are silently re-downloaded and the cycle repeats.
findings.fix: Touch the file on a cache hit (e.g. `file.setLastAccessed(DateTime.now())` or setLastModified, throttled to once per launch per file) and sort by that timestamp, or exempt covers whose source URL belongs to a library/playlist track from eviction.

findings.title: Every launch re-reads and re-parses every track's meta JSON and does ~7 sequential file round-trips per song before any library data is available
findings.evidence: database_service.dart:118-119: `_discoverAudioFiles(dir)` is awaited inside `_load`, which every getter awaits through `_ensureLoaded`. For EVERY `.ready` file (i.e. every downloaded song, not just unknown ones) :228-235 does `audioFile.exists()`, `audioFile.length()`, `metaFile.exists()`, `metaFile.readAsString()`, `jsonDecode` and `Track.fromMap` on the UI isolate, and only then checks :251 `if (!_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id))` - a linear scan per file, so O(n^2) id comparisons. The prune loop :265-289 then does three more awaited stats per track (`ready.exists()`, `audio.exists()`, `audio.length()`). The id needed for the membership test is already in the file name (:241-245 computes `fileKey`), so the read/parse is wasted for known tracks.
findings.failure_scenario: With a library of ~3,000 songs each cold start performs roughly 21,000 awaited filesystem calls plus 3,000 JSON parses and ~4.5 million id comparisons before `_ensureLoaded` completes. Until then LibraryController.reload, restoreSession (audio_player_handler.dart:698 `_library()`) and a media-button cold start (`play()` -> restoreSession) are all blocked: the home screen stays empty and the first press of play does nothing for a second or more, growing linearly-to-quadratically with the library. The compute() isolate added for parsing downloaded.json does not help, because this work runs on the main isolate.
findings.fix: Build a Set of known ids once; derive the id from the file name and only read/parse the meta JSON when that id is not in the set. Replace the per-track stats in the prune loop with one directory listing into a Set of names (the listing is already in `entities`).

findings.title: updateTrackMetadata rewrites (and reads back) the whole playlists file on every call, even when no playlist contains the track
findings.evidence: database_service.dart:532-538: the loop only assigns when `idx != -1`, but `await _persistPlaylists();` is unconditional (contrast setTrackLoudness :566-570, which tracks `playlistsChanged`). _persistPlaylists (:473-487) serialises every playlist with a full copy of every track, and _writeJsonAtomically (:359, :378) writes it with flush and then reads the whole file back to compare. The call also follows `_persistDownloaded()` (:526) and `_persistRecentlyPlayed()` (:543), each a full rewrite + read-back, plus the meta JSON. Callers: every automatic naming (track_naming.dart:115, reached from the nowPlaying listener at :42-45 for every not-yet-settled song that starts playing, including the `noBetter` branch :179-183 that only stamps the matcher version) and every manual edit.
findings.failure_scenario: After TrackNaming.matcher is raised (as CLAUDE.md prescribes when matching improves), every previously auto-named song is re-checked the first time it plays. With a few thousand downloads and large playlists, each track change then encodes on the UI isolate, writes, fsyncs and re-reads downloaded.json, playlists.json and recently_played.json (several MB in total) - even though the track is in no playlist - while playback and scrolling are in progress, producing visible jank at each song change during that period.
findings.fix: Track whether any playlist entry was replaced and only then call _persistPlaylists; otherwise emit the library update directly. (Optionally drop the read-back verification for files other than the first write after launch.)

findings.title: A set-aside store is never read again, and from the second launch on the cover sweep deletes the picked covers it references
findings.evidence: database_service.dart:124-125 `// With a store set aside, what it referenced is unknown: keep it all.` / `if (!_setAsideAny) unawaited(_sweepCovers(dir));` - but `_setAsideAny` (:431) is an in-memory flag set only in the launch that performs the rename (:438). On the next launch the fresh, empty file parses fine, the flag is false, and _sweepCovers (:173-192) deletes every file in bilibeat_covers older than a day that the new stores do not mention. Separately, nothing in lib ever opens a `*.unreadable` file (grep: only the rename at :442-446 and comments), so the 'kept' data has no way back even when it becomes readable.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener sideloads a build with a newer schemaVersion, then goes back to the previous build (or playlists.json is read during a transient IO error). Launch 1 of the old build renames bilibeat_playlists.json to .unreadable and shows empty playlists; the sweep is skipped. Launch 2 (a day later): the sweep runs and deletes every custom playlist cover and every picked song cover that only the set-aside playlists referenced. When the newer build is installed again it loads the fresh empty bilibeat_playlists.json; the .unreadable file with all the playlists is still on disk but is never offered or merged, and its cover images are already gone. On a sideloaded Android build the user cannot reach the app's private documents folder to recover it by hand.
findings.fix: Skip the sweep whenever any `*.unreadable` file exists in the documents directory (a directory check, not a per-launch flag), and on load try `<name>.unreadable` when the primary file is missing/empty and the aside file parses under the current schema.

find:persistence a99d2d.notes:
Read-only audit; nothing was run or modified, no network requests made. Of the context tests I read store_safety_test.dart and cover_cache_test.dart in full; serialization_test.dart, library_features_test.dart and track_test.dart were NOT read. Partially read for tracing: audio_player_handler.dart (history, loudness, session, _library/_resolve), track_info_sheet.dart (1-130), playlist_page.dart, song_tile.dart, lyrics_controller.dart (_load), download_manager.dart, track_credit.dart, playback_actions.dart.

Checked and found sound:
- Atomic write protocol (_writeJsonAtomically): single FIFO async lock that is always released in finally; unique temp name per attempt; flush before rename; target only deleted first on Windows; every DatabaseService persist plus LyricsStore go through it; payload snapshots for the track/playlist/lyrics stores are materialised at call time so writes land in call order. The only bypass is AudioDownloadService._atomicWriteString (per-track meta JSON), which uses its own unique temp + rename and is safe.
- Set-aside on unreadable/newer-schema files covers downloaded, recently_played, playlists, search_history, prefs and lyrics. Downloaded.json being set aside is recovered by discovery from the per-track meta files.
- Track.fromMap / Playlist.fromMap / PlaybackSession.fromMap tolerate missing, extra and wrongly typed fields; bare legacy payloads and the versioned envelope are both accepted; per-item failures are skipped rather than failing the file.
- Track equality/hashCode by id; TrackNotifier notifies on non-identical assignment; copyWith preserves named/matcher/rawUploader (it cannot clear them to null, but no caller needs to).
- TrackNaming re-reads the stored copy before and after its lookup, so it does not write from a stale Track; concurrent updateTrackMetadata calls resolve in call order.
- LyricsStore revision/pin logic, load-merge with entries registered before load, eviction of automatic entries only.
- LibraryController caches are keyed on list identity and invalidate on every reload; playlist reorder indices stay consistent with the in-memory list because mutations are applied synchronously.
- rebaseCover / _rebaseCovers for iOS container moves, and _sweepCovers path comparison (both sides use the current documents path); the cover cache (Application Support) and picked covers (Documents) are different directories on Android, iOS and macOS.
- Cover download de-duplication and .part + rename.

Minor things noticed but not reported as findings (could not build a strong enough scenario): (1) a temp file `<name>.<micros>.tmp` left by a process kill between write and rename is never cleaned up; (2) bilibeat_session.json is not set aside when unreadable or written by a newer schema - it is simply ignored and overwritten (transient data); a prefs file whose payload is valid JSON but not a map is likewise overwritten; (3) pickCoverImage derives the extension with `image.path.split('.').last`, which yields a path fragment containing '/' for an extensionless picked file, making the copy fail and the pick silently do nothing; picked temp files from image_picker are not deleted; (4) TrackInfoSheet saves from the Track captured when the sheet opened, so a loudness backfill that lands while the sheet is open is overwritten until the next launch; (5) all persist helpers swallow write errors (e.g. disk full), so a change can exist only in memory with no message; (6) iOS: if the app were ever launched before first unlock, an unreadable-but-present playlists file would be set aside rather than retried - I could not establish that such a launch can happen for this app.

findings.title: Search treats every non-zero Bilibili API code as "no results" (no fallback, no error, pagination ends)
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:538-542 only discards the signed answer when `isRiskControlled(primary)`; isRiskControlled (637-651) recognises only `code == -352 || code == 412` or a v_voucher. bilibili_sdk.dart:571-582 then reads `final data = json['data']; final dynamic rawResult = data is Map ? data['result'] : null;` and 630 `return [];` - `json['code']` is never inspected. So a body such as {"code":-403,...} (bad/stale w_rid), {"code":-412,...} (note: Bilibili's JSON code is negative, the check is for +412), -799/-509 (rate limit) or -400 returns [] from _searchOnce. search() 500-501 then runs the unfiltered attempt, which gets the same code and also returns []. Callers: online_search_controller.dart:82 `_reachedEnd = results.isEmpty;` and :119 `if (results.isEmpty) _reachedEnd = true;`. This contradicts the contract stated at 456-459 and the comment at 558-559. WbiSigner makes the -403 case reachable: after one failed /nav fetch it signs with the static `_fallbackKeys` for 2 minutes (wbi_signer.dart:138-141, 180-181) and live keys are cached 12 h with no invalidation when a signed request is rejected (131-136).
findings.failure_scenario: The nav request times out once on a flaky connection (or the cached keys rotate while the app stays alive). For the next 2 minutes (or up to 12 h) every signed search comes back code -403 with HTTP 200. The plain fallback URL at 545-550 is never tried because the body is non-null and not 'risk controlled'; the user sees '没有找到，换个关键词或粘贴 BV 号试试' instead of the retry state, for a song that exists. During scrolling, a single rate-limited page (-799) returns [] and sets _reachedEnd permanently, so the result list silently stops. Same path makes RecommendationEngine count the seed as a success with zero tracks.
findings.fix: In _searchOnce, after decoding, treat `json['code'] != 0` as a failure: for the signed primary fall through to the plain fallback URL, and if the final body still has code != 0 throw BiliApiException. On -403 from a signed endpoint also clear WbiSigner's cached keys/_cacheTime so the next call refetches.

findings.title: Search-result titles and uploader names keep HTML entities (& " ') and are stored that way
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:591-593 `final rawTitle = item['title'] as String? ?? ''; final cleanTitle = rawTitle.replaceAll(_htmlTagRegex, ''); final author = item['author'] as String? ?? 'UP主';` and 620-622 `title: cleanTitle, rawTitle: cleanTitle, uploader: author`. Only the <em> highlight tags are removed; the search API returns HTML-escaped text. The only entity decoding in lib/ is inside LyricsEngine._preprocess (lyrics_engine.dart:166-170), which is used for parsing, not for display or storage (grep for '&' / unescape over lib finds nothing else). The repo's own fixtures show such titles reaching the app: test/zhoushen_test.dart:171 '王菲&窦靖童合唱《誓言》', :371 '【姚贝娜&单依纯 心火】…'. The view API (_tracksOfView, 198) returns the unescaped title, so the same video has two different rawTitle values depending on how it was found.
