findings.failure_scenario: Search '誓言 王菲'; the row reads '王菲&窦靖童合唱《誓言》'. Tap to download: the Track is saved with title/rawTitle containing '&' (rawTitle 'never changes' per CLAUDE.md), so the library row, notification and lock screen show the entity until the song is auto-named or hand-edited; if matching is off or finds nothing it stays forever. LocalSearch over rawTitle and TasteProfile.tokenize also see 'amp' as a token (recommendation_engine.dart:61 adds [a-zA-Z0-9]{2,} runs, so 'amp'/'quot' become taste terms and potential seed queries).
findings.fix: Decode entities (& < > " ' and numeric &#NN;) on title and author in _searchOnce after stripping tags, sharing one helper with LyricsEngine._preprocess.

findings.title: 换一批 (refresh recommendations) re-requests page 1 with no exclusions and shows the same list
findings.evidence: recommendations_controller.dart:35-50: refresh() calls `RecommendationEngine.recommend()` with default `page = 1` and `excludeIds = const {}`, then `_seen..clear()..addAll(...)`, `_page = 1`. recommendation_engine.dart:160-214 is deterministic for fixed local data: same profile -> same `seedQueries()` -> `BilibiliSdk.search(seed, page: 1)` with order=totalrank -> same candidates -> same score sort -> `take(limit)`. Nothing random or rotating is involved. The engine's own doc (156-159) says 'each refresh asks every seed for its next Bilibili page ... guaranteeing a refresh never repeats an earlier one', which the controller does not do. search_view.dart:144-146 wires the '换一批' button to `_recs.refresh`.
findings.failure_scenario: Open search with a non-empty library, see 20 recommendations, tap 换一批 ('another batch'): after a skeleton flash and 4-16 network requests the identical 20 tracks in the identical order come back (only scrolling position/extra pages are lost). The button never produces a different batch unless favourites/history/search history changed in between.
findings.fix: Make refresh advance: keep a rotating page counter (e.g. recommend(page: ++_refreshPage, excludeIds: previously shown ids), wrapping to 1 when a pass comes back empty), and only clear _seen on wrap.

findings.title: Paging past the end of the music-zone results silently continues with unfiltered (non-music) results from the same page number
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:494-501: `musical = await _searchOnce(query, musicOnly: true, page: page); ... if (musical != null && musical.isNotEmpty) return musical; return _searchOnce(query, musicOnly: false, page: page);`. The empty->unfiltered fallback is justified in the comment (489-493) for 'no matches there', i.e. page 1, but it is applied to every page. online_search_controller.dart:109 calls `BilibiliSdk.search(_query, page: page)` for each further page and ends only when the returned page is empty (119). A transient exception on the music attempt (496-499) has the same effect for that one page.
findings.failure_scenario: Search a niche title that has 25 hits in the 音乐 zone. Pages 1-2 are music. Scrolling requests page 3: the music zone returns [] (its real end), so the unfiltered search's page 3 (ranks 41-60 of the all-zones ranking: gameplay, lectures, reaction videos) is appended, then page 4, 5 ... up to Bilibili's cap. The list never ends where the music ends, the unfiltered pages 1-2 are skipped, and every further page costs two searches (up to four HTTP requests).
findings.fix: Decide the mode once per query: only fall back to unfiltered when page == 1 (and let the controller remember which mode page 1 used and pass it for later pages); for page > 1 an empty music page is the end.

findings.title: BV/av/short-link queries ignore `page`: loadMore re-fetches the same video on every scroll at the end of a multi-part list and never reaches the end
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:467-471: `final directId = extractBvOrAvId(query); if (directId != null) { final direct = await fetchVideoInfo(directId); if (direct.isNotEmpty) return direct; }` and 474-483 for short links - both return the full part list regardless of `page`. online_search_controller.dart:109-119: `final results = await BilibiliSdk.search(_query, page: page); ... for (final t in results) if (_seen.add(t.id)) t ... // Only an empty page proves the end; a page of duplicates does not. if (results.isEmpty) _reachedEnd = true;` - the page is all duplicates, never empty, so _reachedEnd stays false and _loadMoreFailed is false (no 3 s window). search_view.dart:72-81 calls `_online.loadMore()` on every ScrollNotification within 320 px of the end when results are non-empty.
findings.failure_scenario: Paste the BV number (or b23.tv link) of a 30-part album video. The 30 parts list is scrollable; on reaching the bottom each scroll notification, serialised only by _loadingMore, fires another view request (for a short link: a b23.tv resolve plus a view request), the spinner flickers in and out under the list, and this continues for as long as the user scrolls or overscrolls near the end - dozens of identical requests per minute against an API that risk-controls bursts (the plain view then 412s and each attempt becomes 2 requests).
findings.fix: In BilibiliSdk.search return [] for page > 1 when the query resolves to a direct id / short link (or have the controller set _reachedEnd when a page adds no new ids for a direct-id query).

findings.title: Recommendation loadMore has no failure back-off: each scroll tick re-fires all seeds while Bilibili is refusing
findings.evidence: recommendations_controller.dart:61-86: the guard is `if (_loading || _loadingMore || _reachedEnd || _tracks.isEmpty) return;`; the catch block (81-84) only logs, then `_loadingMore = false; notifyListeners();` - no failure flag or timestamp, unlike OnlineSearchController.loadMore (online_search_controller.dart:98-101, 'A failed page gets a quiet retry window instead of re-firing on every scroll pixel'). search_view.dart:77-78 calls `_recs.loadMore()` on every scroll notification near the end. One recommend() call (recommendation_engine.dart:186-195) runs up to 4 seeds, each BilibiliSdk.search = music + unfiltered attempt, each attempt = signed + fallback request.
findings.failure_scenario: Risk control starts answering -352/412 (or the phone goes offline) while the user is at the bottom of 为你推荐. Every scroll movement there starts a new pass of up to 16 HTTP requests the moment the previous one fails (fast when refused), for as long as the finger moves - which extends the risk-control ban that also blocks search and downloads. There is also no visible failure/retry affordance: only a flickering spinner.
findings.fix: Mirror the search controller: record _loadMoreFailed + _lastFailure and skip loadMore for a few seconds after a failure (and surface a retry row).

findings.title: Recommendations recommend songs the user already downloaded (knownIds covers only favourites and the last 30 plays)
findings.evidence: recommendation_engine.dart:20 '/// Tracks the user already has; never recommend these back.'; knownIds is filled only in absorb() (84-86), called for `favourites` (94-96) and `history.take(30)` (98-100). recommend() loads only `getFavoritesPlaylist()`, `getRecentlyPlayed()` and `getSearchHistory()` (165-167); `DatabaseService.getDownloadedTracks()` (database_service.dart:788) is never consulted, and line 202 filters solely on `profile.knownIds`.
findings.failure_scenario: Library of 200 downloaded 周深 songs, few favourited. The top seed is '周深'; Bilibili's page-1 hits for it are the most popular uploads - exactly the ones already downloaded and not among the last 30 plays. 为你推荐 ('to download') is then largely made of songs already in the library, and since ranking prefers title-token overlap with the profile, already-owned songs score highest.
findings.fix: Add the downloaded track ids to the exclusion set in recommend() (knownIds ∪ downloaded ids), without letting them add taste weight if that is not wanted.

findings.title: buvid refresh failure is never backed off, and concurrent callers each fetch their own identity / WBI keys
findings.evidence: fingerprint_service.dart:26-30 returns the cache only while `now.difference(_cacheTime!).inHours < 1`. On a failed refresh, 63-68 `if (_buvid3.isEmpty) { ...; _cacheTime = now; }` updates _cacheTime only when there was no previous value; with an existing buvid3 the old value is returned but _cacheTime stays stale, so the next call fetches again. WbiSigner has a `_retryAfter` for exactly this reason (wbi_signer.dart:83-87); FingerprintService has none. Neither service shares an in-flight future: getBuvid (24-71) and _getWbiKeys (130-182) start a new request per caller. RecommendationEngine fires up to 4 searches concurrently (recommendation_engine.dart:186), each calling getCookieString then signParams (bilibili_sdk.dart:512, 529).
findings.failure_scenario: (a) App alive > 1 h (normal for a music player) and the spi endpoint is slow or refused while the rest of api.bilibili.com answers: every search, view fallback and recognised-music lookup first waits on a new spi attempt (up to 10 s connect + 10 s headers + 10 s body) before doing its real request, indefinitely. (b) Cold start with search open: the 4 seed searches issue 4 spi and 4 nav requests at once and are sent with 4 different freshly minted buvid3 cookies (last writer wins in the statics) - a burst pattern from unactivated device ids that invites -352.
findings.fix: Set a retry-after timestamp on refresh failure (keep serving the old buvid), and memoise the in-flight Future in both getBuvid and _getWbiKeys so concurrent callers share one request.

findings.title: Timeouts abandon requests without aborting them; stalled sockets keep their slot in the per-host pool
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:34-47: `await _httpClient.getUrl(...).timeout(10s)`, `await req.close().timeout(10s)`, `res.transform(utf8.decoder).join().timeout(10s)`. Future.timeout only stops waiting: the HttpClientRequest is never `abort()`ed and the response subscription is never cancelled, so the connection stays in `_active`. Same pattern at 104-115, wbi_signer.dart:144-157 and fingerprint_service.dart:33-46. The clients are static, never closed, with `maxConnectionsPerHost` 10 / 4 (bili_http.dart:17, bilibili_sdk.dart:26-28). Dart's pool queues when full (sky_engine _http/http_impl.dart:2664-2672: `if (_active.length + _connecting >= maxConnectionsPerHost) { ... _pending.add(...)`), and idleTimeout applies only to idle connections; no TCP keepalive is set.
findings.failure_scenario: Wi-Fi to cellular hand-over (or a captive/black-holing network) while 为你推荐 is loading: the 4 seeds have ~8-10 requests in flight on api.bilibili.com whose sockets go half-open (request already ACKed, no response ever arrives). All time out in Dart after 10 s but remain active. The pool for that host is now full: every later getUrl is queued and itself times out after 10 s, so search, video info and audio-stream lookups (downloads) all fail on a working network until the OS finally kills the dead sockets or the app is restarted.
findings.fix: On timeout call `req.abort()` (and cancel the body subscription / `res.detachSocket` is unnecessary - abort suffices), e.g. wrap each request in a helper that aborts in the timeout handler; alternatively recreate the client with close(force: true) after repeated timeouts.

findings.title: Short-link resolver validates the host by substring, keeps http://, and follows redirects anywhere
findings.evidence: bilibili_sdk.dart:474-476 enters the resolver when `query.contains('b23.tv')` (anywhere in the text). 87-91 falls back to `RegExp(r'https?://[^\s]+').firstMatch(input)` - the first URL of any host - and 97-101 accept it when `urlStr.contains('b23.tv')` (path, query or a look-alike host such as b23.tv.example.com all pass; `Uri.host` is never checked). 94 `if (!urlStr.startsWith('http')) urlStr = 'https://$urlStr';` leaves an explicit http:// link as cleartext. 104-109 use the default HttpClient redirect following (no followRedirects/maxRedirects set anywhere in lib), so even a genuine short link is followed to whatever host it redirects to, and 122-123 trusts any BV number found in the final page body.
findings.failure_scenario: The user pastes share text from a chat such as '好听 https://b23.tv.evil.example/a' or 'https://evil.example/x?from=b23.tv': the app issues a GET (with the Bilibili Referer and spoofed UA, revealing the device IP) to that host, follows its redirects, and if the returned HTML contains any BV number shows and offers to download that video as 'the' result for the pasted link. With 'http://b23.tv/xxxx' the resolve request goes out in cleartext, where an on-path party can answer with a body naming a different BV.
findings.fix: Parse with Uri and require `uri.host` to equal (or be a subdomain of) b23.tv / bili2233.cn / acg.tv, force the scheme to https, set `req.followRedirects = false`, read the Location header yourself and only accept a location whose host ends with bilibili.com (or one of the short-link hosts).

findings.title: A nav answer whose wbi_img URLs are empty/short makes every signed request throw, and search then skips its plain fallback
findings.evidence: wbi_signer.dart:160-169: with `wbi_img` present, `imgUrl = wbiImg['img_url'] as String? ?? ''` and `_cachedImgKey = imgUrl.split('/').last.split('.').first;` are stored and returned without checking length; `_cacheTime` is set and `_retryAfter = null`. _getMixinKey (94-96) does `mixinKeyEncTab.map((n) => orig[n])` with indices up to 63, so a combined key shorter than 64 chars throws RangeError from signParams. Because the cache check (131-136) requires non-empty keys, the nav request is repeated on every call with no back-off. In bilibili_sdk.dart:510-554 signParams is inside the same try as both the primary and the fallback request, so the throw becomes `BiliApiException('search request failed')` and the unsigned fallback at 545-550 is never attempted; fetchAudioStream (389, 442-446) returns null.
findings.failure_scenario: Bilibili changes or blanks the wbi_img fields (e.g. returns relative/empty URLs for anonymous clients): every search shows '无法连接哔哩哔哩' and every download fails to get a stream, each after an extra nav round-trip, even though the unsigned search endpoint and static fallback keys would still have worked.
findings.fix: Validate that both keys are 32 chars before caching; otherwise fall through to the fallback-keys path (with _retryAfter). In _searchOnce, catch a signing failure separately and still try the plain fallback URL.

find:network aee1ec.notes:
Read-only audit; nothing was run or modified and no network requests were made. Behaviour of Bilibili's endpoints (exact error codes for a bad w_rid, HTML-escaped search titles) is from knowledge of the API, not verified live; confidence values reflect that.

Checked and found sound:
- WBI: mixin table matches the published 64-entry table; parameters are sorted, the filtered characters !'()* are removed from both the signed and the sent values (covered by test), Uri.encodeComponent gives %20 and upper-case hex as required; wts is added before signing; callers re-encode with the same function.
- TLS: no badCertificateCallback anywhere; all Bilibili endpoints are https constants; cover/stream URLs are upgraded http:->https:; Android manifest has usesCleartextTraffic=false (the only cleartext path found is an explicitly pasted http:// short link, reported).
- Every request has connect/header/body timeouts (their not aborting the socket is reported separately); non-200 responses are drained; non-UTF-8 or HTML bodies end as null / parse failure rather than a crash.
- Response parsing: _tracksOfView casts are wrapped and converted to BiliApiException; fetchVideoHints/_dataOf/_recognisedMusic type-check before use; fetchAudioStream is fully inside try/catch; search item loop type-checks bvid.
- BV/av extraction boundaries (tests cover the false-positive words); ids are query-encoded in the view URLs.
- Stale-result tokens in OnlineSearchController (search/loadMore/clear/history) and the pass counter in RecommendationsController are consistent; I found no path where an older response overwrites a newer query or leaves loading flags stuck.
- Identifiers: only buvid3/buvid4 (in memory, never persisted) and a fixed desktop UA are sent; no account cookies exist. Search history (max 12, includes pasted links) is stored locally only.
- LocalSearch: normalisation, AND-of-terms scoring and stable ordering behave as documented; the SearchView cache is keyed on the identity of LibraryController.downloaded, which is replaced (List.unmodifiable) on reload.

Not determined: whether the static fallback WBI keys are still the live pair (if they are, the -403 scenario in finding 1 needs a real key rotation or rate-limit code instead); whether dart:io on current Flutter enforces Android's cleartext policy for the http:// short-link case.

findings.title: Re-checking a named part of a multi-part video asks about the whole video: the part's own name is lost once the track is named
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:81-88 `final part = track.partTitle; if (part != null) return (title: part, context: track.rawTitle); return (title: track.rawTitle.isEmpty ? track.title : track.rawTitle, context: '');`
track.dart:71-78 partTitle is derived from `title` only: `if (rawTitle.isEmpty || !title.startsWith(rawTitle)) return null;`
track_naming.dart:188-196 naming overwrites `title` with the song name (`title: found.title, ... named: true, matcher: matcher`), so afterwards title no longer starts with rawTitle and partTitle is null for good; nothing else stores the part name (bilibili_sdk.dart:231 only bakes it into `title`).
track_naming.dart:95-96 `_settled` is false for a track named by an older generation, and `matcher` has been raised in three separate commits (54c7758, 3fbbd22, 6319e4f; now 4), so `_name` re-runs `_ask(before, ...)` -> `_question(before)` with the video title and no context. The same happens in the edit sheet: track_info_sheet.dart:63 `TrackNaming.identify(widget.track)`.
findings.failure_scenario: A two-part video "周深《大鱼》+《光亮》" was downloaded and its parts auto-named 大鱼 and 光亮 by matcher 3 (question = the part name, context = video title). After updating to the build with matcher = 4, playing P1 triggers the re-check: _question now returns the whole video title for both parts, identical except for duration. identify() scores the two bracketed songs (later 《》 pairs get +0.1*bookIdx, line 1068) and returns one answer; whenever it differs from the stored name, lines 188-196 overwrite the correct part name/artist/cover with the other song's. The same wrong question is asked every time the listener taps 智能识别 on an already-named part. This repeats on every future matcher bump.
findings.fix: Keep the part name on the Track when it is first named (e.g. a persisted `partName` field set from `partTitle` in `_name` and in the edit sheet's save) and have `_question` use `track.partTitle ?? track.partName` so a named part is still asked by its own name with rawTitle as context.

findings.title: Latin noise keywords (ED, OP, OST, HQ, SQ, LRC, Audio) are matched as substrings, so English song/artist names containing them are discarded
findings.evidence:
lyrics_engine.dart:57-64 noiseKeywords: `...|主题曲|片尾曲|片头曲|插曲|推广曲|印象曲|角色曲|宣传曲|ED|OP|OST|` with `caseSensitive: false` and no word boundary (only MV and Live are `\b`-anchored). The glueNoise comment at 70-72 shows this class of bug was fixed there only: "The ASCII glue words are word-anchored so they cannot eat real words out of a token (Alive, Discovery, Deliver must survive)".
Consumers: line 452 in _generateCandidates.add `if (tokenNoise.hasMatch(s)) return;`; line 219 in _noisyClean `if (tokenNoise.hasMatch(sub)) continue;`; line 740 tags filter `!tokenNoise.hasMatch(t)`; line 87-88 showMarker has the same unanchored `ED|OP|OST`.
Fixture title (test/fixtures/zhoushen_videos.json, BV1oN4y1q7md): "周深《Unstoppable》神级回眸惊艳全场【2023最美的夜】" - "unstOPpable" matches `OP`. The only test for it (test/recognised_music_test.dart:83-89) passes because it supplies musicTitle 'Unstoppable' and so takes the recognised-music path at line 811, which bypasses candidates.
findings.failure_scenario: Same video, but Bilibili's recognition is unavailable (fetchVideoHints returns hints without music when the player request fails, bilibili_sdk.dart "Half an answer ... is used") or simply did not recognise the song. identify(): _generateCandidates calls add('Unstoppable', '', 0, ...) for the 《》 pair; line 452 rejects it because tokenNoise matches "op". No bookIdx candidate exists, hasUnmarkedBook is false, the remaining candidates are "2023最美的夜" and "周深", and a tag "Unstoppable" would be dropped at line 740 too - the bracketed song is never searched and the track is not named (or is named after whatever the 周深 catalogue query matches). Offline display is hit as well: cleanTitle('Ed Sheeran - Perfect') -> _noisyClean drops the token "Ed" (line 219), leaving "Sheeran - Perfect", so TrackCredit.artistOf shows artist "Sheeran"; likewise "Post Malone" (OST) -> "Malone", "Red Velvet" -> "Velvet", and 《Lost Stars》/《Faded》/《Hope》 are never candidates.
findings.fix: Word-anchor the ASCII alternatives in noiseKeywords and showMarker the way glueNoise already does: `\bED\b|\bOP\b|\bOST\b|\bHQ\b|\bSQ\b|\bLRC\b|\bAudio\b` (Dart's \b is ASCII-word based, so it still fires next to CJK text such as "动漫OST").

findings.title: _netEaseArtistExists reports a failed request as "not an artist" and never marks the answer incomplete, so a transient failure can be persisted as a wrong name
findings.evidence:
lyrics_engine.dart:1643-1668: `final body = await _httpGet(...); if (body != null) { ... return exists; } ... return false;` - a timeout/non-200 returns false (unlike _netEaseSinger at 1514 which returns null and sets `unasked`, and _netEaseSearch at 572 which returns null and sets `incomplete` at 926).
Decision points that trust it: line 759-762 `titleNamesSinger = ... await _netEaseArtistExists(titleArtist)`; line 763-768 `if (!isCover && !titleNamesSinger) { normCredits += tags... }`; line 773 tagArtist; line 858-863 `if (known[0] != known[1]) { settledSong = known[0] ? right : left; settledArtist = known[0] ? left : right; }`; line 1168 singerInTags; line 1571 _singerInTitle.
None of these sets `incomplete`, so line 1236 `if (incomplete && !bestExact) return null;` does not protect, the result is memoised (1244) and TrackNaming._name writes it with `matcher: matcher` (track_naming.dart:188-196), after which _settled() never looks again.
findings.failure_scenario: Title "周深-大鱼" (no 《》). Line 858 asks NetEase whether 周深 and 大鱼 are artists; both normally exist so nothing is settled. If the request for 周深 times out (10 s timeout, 4 connections per host shared with other lookups) while 大鱼 succeeds, known = [false, true]: settledSong = '周深', settledArtist = '大鱼'. Every candidate other than a song literally named 周深 is skipped at line 870-874/972, and `settledSong != null` counts as corroboration (line 1007). The outcome is either a song titled "周深" credited to "大鱼" or a remembered null; nothing flags the answer as retryable. Similarly for the comment's own example (line 757) "【单依纯】大鱼" tagged 周深: a failed artist check makes titleNamesSinger false, the tags join normCredits, 周深's 大鱼 scores as credited+exact and the track is saved as 大鱼 / 周深 with 周深's artwork, permanently.
findings.fix: Make _netEaseArtistExists return bool? (null when body == null or parsing threw), set `incomplete = true` in identify wherever a null comes back (treating it as false for the decision), and return null without _remember when incomplete - as is already done for searches and for _netEaseSinger.

findings.title: A failed Bilibili hints fetch is treated as "no hints" and the title-only answer is persisted as this generation's final word
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:124-125 `final hints = await BilibiliSdk.fetchVideoHints(before.bvid, cid: before.cid);` - the only emptiness check is inside the legacy branch (134). bilibili_sdk.dart:249-296: "Never throws: offline (or refused) is [VideoHints.none]" and "Half an answer (one request failed) is used but not kept" - not memoised, but TrackNaming keeps what is derived from it: lines 188-196 save with `matcher: matcher`, so _settled (95-96) never revisits.
In identify the hints decide cover-ness: lyrics_engine.dart:745-756 isCover/isRendition come from `hints.zone`, `hints.tags`, `hints.description` when the title has no marker; 1102 `if (hints.musicTitle.isNotEmpty && !bestApart)` (the backing-track guard) and 811 (recognised song) depend on musicTitle.
findings.failure_scenario: An amateur cover titled "《大鱼》周深" filed in the 翻唱 zone / tagged 翻唱, 20 s shorter than the release. With hints: isCover and isRendition are true (747-754), line 1125-1129 sets bestExact = false (only the song's own artist is credited and the length differs), and the artist falls through to the UP主. If Bilibili refuses the view/tag requests (risk control, which the code elsewhere expects) while NetEase answers, hints == VideoHints.none: isCover is false, 周深 is credited from the title, the result is exact, and the track is saved as 大鱼 / 周深 with the official release artwork and matcher 4 - a wrong credit that is not re-examined until the matcher constant is next raised. The same applies when only the recognition request fails: the line-1102 guard is skipped because musicTitle is empty.
findings.fix: Have fetchVideoHints expose completeness (e.g. a `complete` flag, false when view/tags/recognition could not be asked) and in _name, when hints are incomplete, do not save: `_attempted.remove(track.id); return;` (as the legacy branch already does for an empty owner).

findings.title: The `echo` penalty in identify can never apply: its condition is self-contradictory
findings.evidence: lyrics_engine.dart:986-990 `// Search-farm uploads are named like the query itself ("遥遥 周深"). final echo = artists.isNotEmpty && inTitle.isEmpty && normRaw.length > nameNorm.length && nameNorm == normRaw;` - `nameNorm == normRaw` implies equal lengths, so `normRaw.length > nameNorm.length` is always false alongside it; `echo` is constantly false and line 1064 `if (echo) score -= 5.0;` is dead. (fetchFromNetEase has a working version of the same idea at 1969-1973.)
findings.failure_scenario: Video titled "遥遥 周深"; NetEase returns a search-farm track whose name is "遥遥 周深" by an unrelated account, the same length as the real song. nameNorm "遥遥周深" equals normRaw, so inRaw is true; gap <= 2 corroborates it (line 1005) and adds +4.0. The intended -5.0 never applies, so whenever the genuine recording is absent from the result pages (or its length differs), the farm track wins and the song is saved with the title "遥遥 周深".
findings.fix: Express the intended test, e.g. `final echo = artists.isNotEmpty && inTitle.isEmpty && nameNorm == normRaw && nameNorm.length > candNorm.length;` (the song's name is the whole video title rather than the candidate that was searched).

findings.title: Legacy branch writes back the pre-lookup copy of the track without re-reading it, discarding an edit made during the hints fetch
findings.evidence: track_naming.dart:121 `final before = await _stored(track.id);` ... 124-125 `await BilibiliSdk.fetchVideoHints(...)` (network, up to several 10 s timeouts) ... 139-141 `if (before.uploader.trim() != owner.trim()) { await _save(before.copyWith(rawUploader: owner, matcher: 0)); return; }`. The re-read that protects against concurrent edits ("The listener may have edited (or deleted) it while the lookup ran", 161-169) comes only after this early return. _save -> DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata replaces the stored track wholesale (database_service.dart:523-526) and force-writes the on-disk metadata.
findings.failure_scenario: A song named in an older version (named, matcher == null, artist != UP主) starts playing; _name begins and waits on fetchVideoHints over a slow connection. Meanwhile the listener opens 编辑信息 on it, corrects the title and saves (track_info_sheet.dart:88-100, matcher 0). When the hints arrive, line 140 saves `before` - the pre-edit title, artist and cover - over the listener's edit, and also pushes it to the player. The edit is silently lost. It also re-creates the entry if the listener deleted the download in that window is not possible (updateTrackMetadata only replaces), but playlists/recents copies are overwritten too.
findings.fix: Re-read before writing in the legacy branch: `final stored = await _stored(track.id); if (stored == null || stored.title != before.title || stored.uploader != before.uploader || stored.matcher != before.matcher || stored.named != before.named) return; await _save(stored.copyWith(rawUploader: owner, matcher: 0));`

findings.title: Lookups that end with no usable search are never marked settled, so the track is looked up again on every play
findings.evidence:
lyrics_engine.dart:916 `if (queries.isEmpty) return null;` (no _remember) and 1093-1097 `if (best == null) { if (anyResponse && !incomplete) _remember(memoKey, null); return null; }` where anyResponse is only set by `if (songs.isNotEmpty) anyResponse = true;` (950) - successful searches that all return zero songs look the same as being offline.
track_naming.dart:155-159 `if (found == null && !settled) { _attempted.remove(track.id); return; }` and 42-45 the nowPlaying listener calls autoName on every track start.
_normalize (1722-1727) keeps only 一-龥, a-z, 0-9 and ·, and _generateCandidates.add drops empty norms (451), so a kana/hangul-only title produces no candidates.
findings.failure_scenario: A download titled only in kana or hangul, e.g. "아이유 - 좋은 날": every candidate normalises to '' and is dropped, tags normalise below 2 chars (738), the parsed artist is not a bare name so no catalogue query is added -> queries is empty -> null without a memo. Or any title for which NetEase's searches all return empty lists. _name then removes the id from _attempted, so each time the song starts (including on repeat-one or every pass of a looped playlist) the whole lookup runs again - hints fetch (three Bilibili requests whenever the recognition request did not complete, since such hints are not memoised) plus up to nine NetEase searches - for a question whose answer cannot change this session.
findings.fix: Distinguish "asked and nothing came back" from "could not ask": at 916 `_remember(memoKey, null)` before returning, and at 1095 remember null whenever `!incomplete` (every search returned a list), keeping the retry only for null (failed) searches.

findings.title: Turning 自动匹配歌曲信息 off does not stop lookups already queued or in flight from renaming songs
findings.evidence: track_naming.dart:100-107 `if (!enabled || _settled(track) || !_attempted.add(track.id)) return; _queue = _queue.then((_) => _name(track))...` - `enabled` is read only when the work is enqueued. _name (119-197) never reads it again before `_save` at 188. setEnabled (48-51) only flips the flag and the pref. Lookups are serialised on `_queue` and each can take many seconds (hints + ~10 NetEase requests with 10 s timeouts), so several can be pending after skipping through tracks or after a batch of downloads arrives (library_controller.dart:201-204 enqueues every new download).
findings.failure_scenario: The listener downloads a 20-track playlist; LibraryController.reload enqueues 20 lookups. Seeing the first songs being renamed in a way they dislike, they open 设置 and switch 自动匹配歌曲信息 off. The remaining queued lookups still run and still rewrite title, artist and artwork of the other tracks (each stamped matcher 4), despite the switch being off.
findings.fix: Re-check the flag where the write happens: at the top of _name `if (!enabled) { _attempted.remove(track.id); return; }` and again just before each `_save`.

find:matching ad4624.notes:
Read in full: lyrics_engine.dart (all 2168 lines), track_naming.dart, track_credit.dart, video_hints.dart, track.dart, title_parser_test.dart, recognition_live_test.dart. Read in part: recognised_music_test.dart, track_test.dart, bilibili_sdk.dart (track construction, fetchVideoHints), database_service.updateTrackMetadata, library_controller (_teachArtists, reload), track_info_sheet (_identify/_save), audio_player_handler (nowPlaying assignment). Fixtures were sampled with scripts (structure, titles hitting specific rules), not read in full. No build/test/network commands were run.

Checked and found sound:
- Compilation / duration guards (lines 707-716) run before the recognised-music path, so 【合集】/歌单 brackets, 串烧/盘点/reaction and >15 min are never named, including via recognition. (The category words are only looked for inside 【】/[]; an un-bracketed 合集 under 15 min relies on the other evidence rules - I could not build a certain wrong answer from fixture titles, so not reported.)
- Listener-named tracks: the edit sheet always saves matcher 0, _settled() short-circuits on it in both autoName and _name, and the post-lookup re-read (161-169) compares title/uploader/matcher/named, so a normal-path result is not applied over an edit made meanwhile (the legacy early-return is the exception, reported).
- Same track named twice: _attempted plus the single serial _queue prevent concurrent naming of one id; _save -> handler.updateTrackMetadata -> nowPlaying listener does not loop because the saved track is settled.
- Matcher re-check does not storm: one track per play, serialised; hints, artist and singer lookups are memoised per session. The only repeat-forever cases are the unsettled-null ones reported as low.
- Regexes: no catastrophic backtracking found. listeningPhrase, _describedSinger and the _preprocess patterns use bounded or negated-class quantifiers; the unbounded `在.*大声听` and `.*打卡.*` only run on title-length strings/tags.
- Recognised music the video does not name is ignored (_recognisedSong requires a bracket match, a substring of the normalised title, or an equal tag), and line 1102 refuses un-set-apart title words when Bilibili heard something else. Note that a 2-character CJK recognised title only needs to be a substring of the title; that is the documented design, not reported.
- Cover handling in _performers/covered() was traced against the fixture titles containing 翻唱/cover/原唱/演绎/挑战 (e.g. \"《Cheap Thrills》原唱一句，周深一句\", \"【AI Cover】INVU-周深（原唱：金泰妍）\"); the branches agree with the hand-checked expectations.
- partTitle: correct for the normal \"<video> - P3: <part>\" shape. An empty/whitespace-only part name makes the regex fail, so such a track reads as isNamed (legacy) - I could not confirm Bilibili ever returns an empty part name, so not reported.

Could not determine without network (not reported as findings):
- credited() (line 797-806) has no minimum length for the catalogue artist's normalised name, unlike isOwn/specific; a one-letter NetEase artist name would be \"credited\" by almost any title. Whether such recordings surface in real result pages is unverified.
- _netEaseArtistExists (no mvSize filter, unlike _netEaseSinger) is still what decides tagArtist, titleNamesSinger, the A-B settle and _singerInTitle; the comment at 1500-1502 says nearly any word is some account's artist name. The live fixture test reportedly passes, so impact is unknown.
- _originalArtists returns null when cloudsearch answers with code != 200; if that endpoint is persistently refused, every non-exact cover returns an unsettled null and is retried on each play.
- The description cover test (`翻唱|cover` without word boundary, lines 749/755) also matches words like \"Discover\" and sentences such as \"无数优秀的歌手翻唱过这首歌曲\" (present in the fixture); in the cases traced _performers still produced the expected artist.

findings.title: Marquee keeps scrolling the new title during its 'dwell' and then snaps back to the start when the track changes
findings.evidence:
lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:409-412 builds `MarqueeText(text: track.title, ...)` with no key, so one State (and one AnimationController) lives across track changes.
lib/widgets/marquee_text.dart:267-292: `if (_syncedRun == shouldRun && _syncedCycle == cycle) return;` ... `if (_dwelledText != widget.text) { WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) { ... _dwellTimer = Timer(widget.dwell, () { ... _dwelledText = widget.text; _syncController(shouldRun: true, cycle: _syncedCycle ?? Duration.zero); }); }); return; }` - nothing stops or resets the controller when the dwell begins.
The reset only happens after the timer, in :140-145 `if (_controller.duration != cycle) { _controller.duration = cycle; _controller.stop(); _controller.value = 0; } if (!_controller.isAnimating) _controller.repeat();`.
Meanwhile build keeps painting from the still-running controller, :214-216 `final progress = (_controller.value + widget.phase) % 1.0; return Transform.translate(offset: Offset(-progress * _travel, 0), ...)`.
test/marquee_dwell_test.dart only covers the first text a widget ever shows.
findings.failure_scenario: Player page open, song A has a title too wide for the row (the norm for un-named Bilibili video titles at 22 pt) and is scrolling. The song ends or the listener skips to song B, whose title also overflows. B's title appears already shifted to wherever A's scroll was and keeps scrolling for 1.4 s (the supposed reading pause), then jumps back to offset 0 and immediately scrolls again with no pause. If B's title has the same measured width as A's (two CJK titles of equal length give an identical cycle), the early return at :268 fires: no dwell and no reset at all, B simply continues from A's mid-scroll offset.
findings.fix: Treat the text as part of the sync key and reset at the start of the dwell: track `_syncedText` in the early-return comparison, and when `_dwelledText != widget.text` do `_controller.stop(); _controller.value = 0;` in the post-frame callback before starting the dwell timer.

findings.title: Snackbars raised while a sheet stays open are drawn underneath the sheet and never seen
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:66-68 `if (found == null) { showAppSnackBar(ScaffoldMessenger.of(context), message: '没有匹配到这首歌'); return; }` and :107 `showAppSnackBar(ScaffoldMessenger.of(context), message: '保存失败，请重试');` - the sheet is not popped in either path.
lib/widgets/playback_queue_sheet.dart:48-53 `final messenger = ScaffoldMessenger.of(context); ... showAppSnackBar(messenger, message: '暂时无法切换，请重试');` - same, the queue sheet (82% of the screen) stays open.
lib/widgets/sheet.dart:13 `return showModalBottomSheet<T>(` - a modal route with no Scaffold of its own, so the root ScaffoldMessenger shows the bar in the page Scaffold below the barrier; lib/utils/snack.dart:22-24 makes it a floating pill at that page's bottom edge with a 2 s duration, i.e. exactly where the sheet is. (Flutter scaffold.dart:614-616 starts the dismissal timer regardless, because the root messenger has no ModalRoute.) Also noted by an earlier unverified pass (docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md) for the edit sheet; the queue sheet has the same defect.
findings.failure_scenario: 编辑信息 -> tap 匹配 on a video the matcher cannot identify (or while offline): the spinner stops and nothing else happens; the message expires behind the sheet. A failed save re-enables 保存 with no explanation. In the queue sheet a failed jump likewise looks like the tap was ignored.
findings.fix: Show these messages inside the sheet (an inline caption/error line in the sheet's own state), or wrap the builder in showAppSheet with a transparent Scaffold + ScaffoldMessenger so sheet-raised snackbars render above it.

findings.title: Releasing a seek-bar drag after the track changed seeks the new song to the old drag position
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/player_seek_bar.dart:34 `double? _drag;` and :82-88 `onChangeStart: (v) => setState(() => _drag = v), onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _drag = v), onChangeEnd: (v) { Haptics.light(); widget.onSeek(seconds(v)); setState(() => _drag = null); }`. Nothing clears `_drag` or cancels the gesture when `widget.duration` / the track changes; :53-54 only clamps the held value to the new max.
lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:264-269 creates `PlayerSeekBar(...)` without a per-track key, so the State and the in-progress Slider drag survive `_onTrackChanged`'s setState. Playback continues while the thumb is held (seek happens only on release).
findings.failure_scenario: The listener grabs the thumb in the last seconds of a song and holds it (or scrubs slowly near the end). The song finishes underneath and the next one starts; on release `onSeek` runs against the new song with the held value, e.g. 3:40 into a 3:45 song, so the new song plays a few seconds and ends too - two songs are skipped from one scrub. With a shorter next song the value clamps to its full length and it completes immediately.
findings.fix: Drop the drag when the song changes: give the bar `key: ValueKey(track.id)` in now_playing_page.dart, or in the State remember the duration/track at onChangeStart and ignore onChangeEnd (just clear `_drag`) if it differs.

findings.title: Artist marquee rests 35% into its text, so an overflowing artist line never shows its beginning during the reading pause
findings.evidence:
lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:414-416 `MarqueeText(text: LibraryController.artistOf(track), phase: 0.35, ...`.
lib/widgets/marquee_text.dart:214-216 `final progress = (_controller.value + widget.phase) % 1.0; return Transform.translate(offset: Offset(-progress * _travel, 0), child: child);` - with the controller at 0 (the whole dwell, and each restart at :143 `_controller.value = 0`) the offset is `-0.35 * (textWidth + gap)`, not 0. The doc at :8 says motion 'holds the static start for [dwell] first'.
findings.failure_scenario: A song credited to several performers (or an un-named track with a long UP主 name) whose artist line is wider than the title column: on opening the player the line is shown starting about a third of the way through, with its leading characters scrolled off and faded, held there for 1.4 s, and the first name only comes into view after ~65% of a full cycle.
findings.fix: Apply the phase only once scrolling has begun (e.g. start the controller with `_controller.forward(from: phase)`/`repeat` after the dwell and paint `-_controller.value * _travel`), or drop `phase: 0.35` at the single call site since the two lines already start at different times.

findings.title: Content-sized sheets cannot scroll: showAppSheet lays the builder out with unbounded height, so TrackInfoSheet's scroll view is inert and TrackSheet overflows on short viewports
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/sheet.dart:19-25 `final body = Column(mainAxisSize: expand ? MainAxisSize.max : MainAxisSize.min, ... children: [const _Handle(), if (expand) Expanded(child: builder(context)) else builder(context)],);` - a non-flex Column child gets an unbounded max height.
lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:114-116 `return SingleChildScrollView(padding: ..., child: Column(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min, ...` therefore always takes its full content height (about 285 px with the handle) and never scrolls; the outer Column overflows instead.
lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:126-231 is a plain `Column(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min` (header + primary button + up to six 52 px SheetActions, roughly 380-470 px).
Orientation is not locked (AndroidManifest MainActivity has no screenOrientation; ios/Runner/Info.plist:62-67 lists both landscape orientations).
findings.failure_scenario: Phone in landscape (about 340-390 px usable height) or an Android split-screen window: long-press a downloaded song - the sheet overflows and 删除下载 / 编辑信息 are cut off below the screen with no way to scroll to them. 编辑信息 with the keyboard up in landscape leaves about 140-190 px for a 285 px form: the 保存 button and the 匹配 row are clipped until the keyboard is dismissed. (Landscape was also raised by an earlier unverified pass as an orientation issue; the root cause in this file is the unbounded slot.)
findings.fix: In showAppSheet's non-expand branch wrap the builder in `Flexible(child: SingleChildScrollView(child: builder(context)))` (keeping MainAxisSize.min) so content is height-bounded and scrolls when it does not fit; then remove TrackInfoSheet's own scroll view.

findings.title: Mini player's 'open player' semantics node has no tap action, so a screen reader cannot open the player
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/mini_player.dart:146-160 `child: Semantics(button: true, label: '打开播放器：${track.title}，$artist', child: ExcludeSemantics(child: GestureDetector(onHorizontalDragEnd: ..., child: InkWell(onTap: onTap,` - the Semantics widget declares a button but no `onTap`, and ExcludeSemantics removes the InkWell's tap action (and the text) from the tree. Compare lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:123-127 and now_playing_page.dart:582-586, where the GestureDetector is not excluded and its tap action merges into the labelled node.
findings.failure_scenario: With TalkBack or VoiceOver on, focus the docked card: it is announced as a button, but double-tap does nothing because the node exposes no tap action. The full player (lyrics, queue, seek, sleep timer) is unreachable by assistive activation; only 播放/暂停 and 下一首 work.
findings.fix: Add `onTap: onTap` to the Semantics widget (keep ExcludeSemantics for the inner text), or drop ExcludeSemantics and use MergeSemantics so the InkWell's action is retained.

findings.title: SongTile is a fixed 64 px while its two text lines scale with the system font; rows overflow from about 1.7x
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/song_tile.dart:59-60 `child: SizedBox(height: extent,` with `static const double extent = 64;` and the text column at :88-111: title `AppTypography.body.copyWith(... height: 1.25)` (15 pt -> 18.75 px), `SizedBox(height: 3)`, second line `AppTypography.caption.copyWith(fontSize: 13)` (height 1.3 -> 16.9 px) = 38.65 px at 1.0x, i.e. 35.65*s + 3 > 64 once s > 1.71. playback_queue_sheet.dart:78 additionally pins `itemExtent: SongTile.extent`. The mini player was given exactly this allowance (mini_player.dart:50-52 `// Text can grow with the system font size; the card grows with it.`) but the row was not.
findings.failure_scenario: Android 14+ font size set to 180-200%: every song row in the library, search, playlists and queue needs about 67-74 px for its text; the centred Column overflows the 64 px row and, since Flex does not clip, the title and artist lines paint into the neighbouring rows (and report RenderFlex overflow in debug).
findings.fix: Grow the row with the text scaler as the mini player does (compute `extent + max(0, scaler.scale(15)-15)*1.25 + max(0, scaler.scale(13)-13)*1.3`, and use the same value for the queue's itemExtent), or cap the text scale for these two lines with `MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling`.

findings.title: Three icon-only controls are below the project's 48 pt minimum touch target
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/lyrics_view.dart:327-331 `child: const Tooltip(message: '回到当前', child: SizedBox(width: 44, height: 44,` (the InkWell is sized by this box: 44x44).
lib/widgets/download_management_sheet.dart:184-187 `return SizedBox(width: 44, height: 48, child: IconButton(tooltip: tooltip, padding: EdgeInsets.zero,` - used for 重试 / 忽略 / 删除下载, with 重试 and 忽略 side by side at :138-157.
CLAUDE.md UI conventions: 'Touch targets are at least 48 pt'.
findings.failure_scenario: In the downloads sheet a failed row shows 重试 and 忽略 as two adjacent 44 px-wide targets with 21 px glyphs; a slightly off tap on 重试 lands on 忽略 and removes the failed entry (and with it the only retry affordance for that song). The lyrics 回到当前 button is 44x44 at the pane's right edge.
findings.fix: Use 48x48 for `_icon` in download_management_sheet.dart and for `_ResumeButton` in lyrics_view.dart.

find:widgets a91c90.notes:
Nothing was executed (read-only); all findings are derived from source. An earlier unverified pass exists in docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md with no widgets finder among its sources; two of my findings overlap it (snackbar behind the edit sheet; landscape sheet overflow) and are reported here with the widget-level root cause and additional sites.

Checked and found sound:
- ExpandFromCard: CurvedAnimation is rebuilt/disposed correctly on animation change; the `t >= 1.0` branch changes tree depth but the page survives because ModalRoute wraps it in a GlobalKey'd RepaintBoundary (state is reparented, not rebuilt). Reversal mid-open can jump because of forward/reverse curves, but only inside a 420 ms window; not reported.
- CachedCoverImage: token guard against stale settles, in-flight dedupe, .part + rename, timeouts, decode sizing via ResizeImage(policy: fit), errorBuilder fallback, cache key includes the sized URL so sizes do not collide; custom-cover paths are rebased and swept in DatabaseService (rebaseCover/_sweepCovers). Cover URLs are upgraded to https in BilibiliSdk. Not reported: a cover first loaded at one size is not refetched when only width/height change (rotation only).
- PlayerSeekBar: zero/unknown duration falls back to track.duration then max=1.0 with value clamped; dragging past the ends is clamped; position updates during a drag are masked by `_drag`. Slider horizontal drag vs the page's vertical pull-down are different axes; lyrics scroll wins the arena over the page's vertical drag.
- MiniPlayer: horizontal swipe (velocity threshold 300) vs InkWell tap do not conflict; buttons are 52x56 with tooltips; progress line guards total <= 0; card grows with text scale.
- MarqueeText: size is stable from the first layout, ticker and dwell timer are disposed, unbounded width and reduced-motion paths are handled, the duplicate copy is excluded from semantics.
- LyricsView: listener moved on position change, keys regenerated with lines, timers cancelled, binary search correct for index -1. LyricsSheet: search token guards stale results; sheet pops before async saves.
- TrackDownloadButton: stale-row guard in _refresh, subscriptions cancelled; a tap on a disabled (downloading) button falls through to the row, which only opens the song sheet.
- TrackSheet/PlaylistPicker: `_dismiss()` returns the navigator context and checks `mounted` before use; promptForText disposes its controller right after the dialog future completes (debug-only risk during the exit animation, harmless in release; not reported).
- Shimmer respects reduced motion and disposes its controller; Haptics are plain platform-channel calls that are no-ops on platforms without them; formatDuration/formatBytes handle zero; theme colours: only mask gradients (Colors.white/transparent), ArtworkBackdrop's alpha variants of the background colour and ProgressRing's default track colour are hard-coded, none visible as a wrong colour.

Could not determine without running: exact pixel overflow thresholds (SongTile at large font scale, sheet heights in landscape) are computed from style metrics, not measured.

findings.title: Engine started headless by the media service treats the missing permissions channel as "not protected": stale battery hint shown, notification prompt skipped
findings.evidence:
The `bilibeats/permissions` handler exists only while a MainActivity has configured the engine: android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/bilibeats/app/MainActivity.kt:18-23 `override fun configureFlutterEngine(...) { ... MethodChannel(flutterEngine.dartExecutor.binaryMessenger, "bilibeats/permissions").setMethodCallHandler {...}`.
But the same shared engine is also created, and Dart main() run, by the service with no activity: audio_service-0.18.19 AudioService.java:345 `flutterEngine = AudioServicePlugin.getFlutterEngine(this);` -> AudioServicePlugin.java:110 `executeDartEntrypoint(DartEntrypoint.createDefault())`. The service is exported with a MediaBrowserService filter and a MEDIA_BUTTON receiver (AndroidManifest.xml:45-58), so a headset/Bluetooth button or SystemUI media resumption can start it in a dead process.
In that engine: lib/services/background_protection.dart:22-29 `try { return await _channel.invokeMethod<bool>('isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations') ?? false; } catch (_) { return false; }` (MissingPluginException -> false), consumed by lib/screens/home_page.dart:61-62 `final enabled = await BackgroundProtection.isEnabled(); if (mounted && !enabled) setState(() => _showProtectionHint = true);` which runs once in initState. And lib/main.dart:62-66 fires `requestNotifications` once with `.catchError((Object _) {})`. When the activity later attaches to the cached engine, main() and HomePage.initState do not run again.
findings.failure_scenario: User has already granted the battery exemption (not dismissed the hint). The process is killed; they press play on a Bluetooth headset (or SystemUI binds the MediaBrowserService after reboot). AudioService.onCreate starts the engine headless; HomePage is built, isEnabled() throws MissingPluginException and is read as "not exempt". The user then opens the app: the activity attaches to the existing engine and the home screen shows the "enable background protection" hint although the exemption is already granted. On a first run started this way the POST_NOTIFICATIONS request is also silently dropped for that process lifetime. (Relies on the headless engine building the widget tree in its warm-up frame, which is how audio_service's shared-engine design normally behaves.)
findings.fix: Do not map a channel error to `false`: return null/unknown on MissingPluginException and leave the hint hidden; re-run the check (and the notification request) on AppLifecycleState.resumed, as settings_sheet.dart already does for its own row.

findings.title: Missing key.properties silently produces a debug-signed "release" APK with exit code 0
findings.evidence:
android/app/build.gradle:59-66 `signingConfig = hasReleaseKey ? signingConfigs.release : signingConfigs.debug` followed only by `logger.warn("WARNING: android/key.properties not found — signing this release with the DEBUG key...")`.
tool/build_release.sh:80-85 likewise only echoes a WARNING when `android/key.properties` is absent, then continues to `flutter build apk --release` and copies the result to `bilibeats-${SHORT_VERSION}-arm64-v8a.apk` (line 98-99), the same name a properly signed build gets. key.properties and the .jks are gitignored (android/.gitignore:11-13), so any fresh clone / new machine is in this state. AndroidManifest.xml:19-21 disables all backup, so app data cannot survive an uninstall.
findings.failure_scenario: On a fresh checkout (or after key.properties is lost) `tool/build_release.sh` succeeds and yields bilibeats-0.1.x-arm64-v8a.apk signed with that machine's debug key; the warning scrolls past in Gradle output. Installed over the real install it fails with a signature mismatch; installed clean (new phone, or after uninstalling to "fix" the mismatch) it works, but every later properly-signed build can no longer update it, and the only way forward is an uninstall that wipes the whole downloaded library and playlists (no backup by design).
findings.fix: Make the release script fail (exit 1) when android/key.properties is missing unless an explicit opt-in such as ALLOW_DEBUG_SIGNING=1 is set; optionally throw a GradleException for assembleRelease/bundleRelease in the same case, or suffix the artifact name with `-DEBUGSIGNED`.

findings.title: Android launch/normal themes are light when the system is in light mode, so the dark-only app cold-starts on a white screen
findings.evidence: android/app/src/main/res/values/styles.xml:4 `<style name="LaunchTheme" parent="@android:style/Theme.Light.NoTitleBar">` with `windowBackground` = `@drawable/launch_background`; drawable-v21/launch_background.xml: `<item android:drawable="?android:colorBackground" />` (white under Theme.Light); drawable/launch_background.xml: `@android:color/white`. styles.xml:15-16 NormalTheme is also `Theme.Light.NoTitleBar` with `?android:colorBackground`. Only values-night/styles.xml uses Theme.Black. The app is dark only (CLAUDE.md) and the first Flutter frame is delayed until after `await AudioService.init(...)` (lib/main.dart:39-51) because runApp is called at the end of main().
findings.failure_scenario: Phone set to the light system theme (default on many devices, or daytime auto-schedule). Every cold start shows a full white screen until AudioService.init completes and Flutter draws its first #08080A frame; the white NormalTheme window background can also show through behind the Flutter surface during resizes/transitions. With the system in dark mode the problem does not appear, which is why it is easy to miss.
findings.fix: Make both values/ and values-night/ themes dark: parent `@android:style/Theme.Black.NoTitleBar` and a fixed dark colour (the app background, #08080A) for `windowBackground` in LaunchTheme and NormalTheme / launch_background.xml.

findings.title: Orientation is not restricted on any platform although the UI is laid out for portrait only
findings.evidence: ios/Runner/Info.plist:62-67 lists `UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft` and `UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight` for iPhone; android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:22-30 declares MainActivity with no `android:screenOrientation`; `grep -rn "orientation\|Orientation" lib` returns nothing (no SystemChrome.setPreferredOrientations). The player page budget assumes a tall box: lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:545 `static const double _rows = 48 + 52 + 46 + _PlayButton.size;` and :553-556 `final spare = box.maxHeight - _rows - text - art; final s = spare < 96 ? 96.0 : spare;` - fixed rows plus at least 96 pt of gaps, with the artwork taking whatever is left.
findings.failure_scenario: With auto-rotate on, the user tilts the phone while the player page is open. The viewport becomes roughly 800x360 pt: fixed rows (~220 pt) + minimum gaps (96 pt) + status/navigation insets leave about 20 pt or less for the cover, which collapses to a sliver (or the column overflows on shorter devices); the home grid and mini player are likewise stretched. Nothing in the app was designed or golden-tested for landscape (test renders are portrait).
findings.fix: Lock to portrait: `android:screenOrientation="portrait"` on MainActivity (or `SystemChrome.setPreferredOrientations([DeviceOrientation.portraitUp])` in main()) and remove the two landscape entries from the iPhone `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` array.

findings.title: web/, linux/ and windows/ are checked-in scaffolding for targets that cannot run
findings.evidence: linux/flutter/generated_plugins.cmake:5-7 `list(APPEND FLUTTER_PLUGIN_LIST file_selector_linux )` - no audio plugin is registered; just_audio-0.10.6/pubspec.yaml:44-55 declares platforms android, ios, macos, web only, and audio_service has no Linux/Windows implementation either. lib/main.dart:39 `final handler = await AudioService.init(...)` runs before `runApp` (line 68). For web, persistence and playback go through dart:io (`File`, `Platform`, `HttpClient` in database_service.dart, audio_download_service.dart, bili_http.dart), which is unsupported in the browser. Yet web/index.html and web/manifest.json are branded ("BiliBeats — 在手机上听 B 站音乐...") and linux/windows CMake files carry the renamed binary/application id, and lib still has `Platform.isWindows` branches (audio_download_service.dart:109, database_service.dart:365).
findings.failure_scenario: `flutter run -d linux` / `-d windows` builds and opens a window, then AudioService.init / the first AudioPlayer call throws MissingPluginException before runApp, leaving a blank window; `flutter run -d chrome` fails at the first file-system call. The directories look like maintained targets (they were kept in sync during the package rename) but none of them can start, and CLAUDE.md lists only Android, iOS and macOS.
findings.fix: Delete web/, linux/ and windows/ (and the two `Platform.isWindows` branches), or state in CLAUDE.md that they are unsupported scaffolding; if desktop is ever wanted, add just_audio_media_kit/just_audio_windows and guard AudioService.init.

find:native aa4a5a.notes:
Read-only; no builds or network requests were run.

Not read in full (so not listed in filesRead): macos/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj (target, build-phase, build-configuration and SPM sections read; file-reference/group header and warning-flag lines skipped), tool/make_keystore.sh, lib/main.dart, home_page.dart, settings_sheet.dart, now_playing_page.dart, and the audio_service plugin sources (relevant sections only).

Checked and found sound:
- audio_service manifest requirements: service with foregroundServiceType=mediaPlayback, MediaBrowserService filter, MEDIA_BUTTON receiver, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK, WAKE_LOCK and POST_NOTIFICATIONS are all present; every component has an explicit android:exported; MainActivity extends AudioServiceActivity, so the shared engine is used. The plugin's PendingIntents are FLAG_IMMUTABLE.
- usesCleartextTraffic=false, and no ATS exception is needed on iOS: all endpoints are https, and Bilibili/NetEase cover and stream URLs are rewritten from http to https (bilibili_sdk.dart:199/409/434/595, lyrics_engine.dart:1618).

- SDK levels: compileSdk 36, targetSdk 36, minSdk 24 (Flutter 3.44 defaults) satisfy image_picker_android (minSdk 24), jni (compileSdk 35) and sqflite_android. MainActivity's API guards are correct (TIRAMISU check for POST_NOTIFICATIONS; the battery APIs are API 23+).
- Battery-exemption intent: package: URI for the app's own package, guarded by try/catch with a fallback to the settings list; REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS is declared; settings_sheet re-reads the state on resume.
- Predictive back: the app uses PopScope throughout, no WillPopScope.
- R8 rules keep the Flutter embedding, media3 and com.ryanheise.audioservice (over-broad, but not harmful).
- Signing: key.properties (storeFile=bilibeats-release.jks, keyAlias=bilibeats) matches the renamed keystore; both are gitignored and untracked; make_keystore.sh refuses to overwrite an existing keystore.

- iOS: UIBackgroundModes audio and NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription are present (the picker is gallery-only, so no camera string is needed); deployment target 13.0 meets every plugin's Package.swift minimum (image_picker_ios 13.0, others 12.0); SPM local package reference is present and there is no Podfile; Runner.app naming matches build_release.sh.
- macOS: Release.entitlements has network.client and files.user-selected.read-write (file_selector_macos backs image_picker); Debug only adds JIT and network.server; deployment target 10.15 meets file_selector_macos 10.15.

Minor, not reported as findings:
- The macOS project still references the product as "bilibeat.app" (pbxproj lines 68/227, TEST_HOST at 401/415/429, Runner.xcscheme BuildableName) while PRODUCT_NAME is BiliBeats. The app build is unaffected, but the macOS RunnerTests target's TEST_HOST points at a non-existent bundle.
- home_page hides the protection hint as soon as request() returns, even if the user declines in the system dialog; it reappears on the next launch.
- AudioService is exported with an onGetRoot that accepts any client (plugin default), so any installed app can bind and send transport commands; this is inherent to audio_service.

Could not determine without running:
- How the Kotlin plugin gets applied: app/build.gradle does not apply kotlin-android and gradle.properties sets android.builtInKotlin=false. Presumed to be handled by the Flutter Gradle plugin, since a release APK dated after the last Gradle change exists in build/.
- Whether a headless engine really builds HomePage before an activity attaches (the premise of the first finding).

findings.title: release.sh with an explicit X.Y.Z resets the build number to 1, lowering Android versionCode below the installed build
findings.evidence: tool/release.sh:79-82 `*) NEW_SHORT="$BUMP"; NEW_BUILD=1 ;;` while every other branch does `NEW_BUILD=$((BUILD + 1))` (lines 67, 72, 77). pubspec.yaml:4 is `version: 0.1.3+4`; android/app/build.gradle:39 `versionCode = flutter.versionCode`; the merged release manifest in build/ shows versionCode="4". The script's own header (lines 20-21) says: "Android uses it as versionCode; forgetting it makes installs reject updates." The usage line (27) advertises the X.Y.Z form. This path was last used for 0.1.0 (`git show v0.1.0:pubspec.yaml` -> 0.1.0+1, after 6.0.0+53), which was harmless only because the application id changed in the same release.
findings.failure_scenario: `tool/release.sh 0.2.0 "note"` on the current tree writes `version: 0.2.0+1`, commits and tags v0.2.0. build_release.sh then produces an APK with versionCode 1. On the phone that has 0.1.3 (versionCode 4) the install is refused as a downgrade (INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE); the only way to install that APK is to uninstall first, which deletes the downloaded audio and the library JSON. The bad number is already committed and tagged by then.
findings.fix: In the explicit-version branch use `NEW_BUILD=$((BUILD + 1))` like the others (the build number must be monotonic regardless of the version name). Optionally also reject an explicit version that is not greater than the current one and one that contains `+` or `-` (the glob `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*` accepts `1.2.3+9`, producing `1.2.3+9+1`).

findings.title: build_release.sh succeeds and emits the publishable APK name when signing fell back to the debug key
findings.evidence: tool/build_release.sh:79-84 only prints `WARNING: android/key.properties not found — this build will be signed with the DEBUG key and must not be published.` and continues; lines 97-98 then copy the result to `bilibeats-${SHORT_VERSION}-arm64-v8a.apk`, the exact asset name the README tells users to download, and the script exits 0. android/app/build.gradle:59-61 `signingConfig = hasReleaseKey ? signingConfigs.release : signingConfigs.debug`. The warning is printed before several minutes of Gradle output and is not repeated in the closing summary. Commit 3e6c2b9's message records that v1.0.0 through v2.2.0 shipped debug-signed this way.
findings.failure_scenario: On a fresh clone or a second machine where the .jks was restored but key.properties was not (both are gitignored), `tool/build_release.sh all` finishes normally and leaves bilibeats-0.1.4-arm64-v8a.apk ready to attach. Installed over the existing app it is rejected for a signature mismatch; if it is attached to the GitHub release, anyone who installs it can never update to a properly signed build without uninstalling (losing downloads and playlists).
findings.fix: Make the missing key a hard error in build_release.sh (`exit 1` unless e.g. ALLOW_DEBUG_SIGNING=1 is set), and when the override is used name the copy `...-DEBUG-SIGNED.apk`. Optionally run `apksigner verify --print-certs` after the build and fail if the signer is CN=Android Debug.

findings.title: README states Android 6.0+ but the shipped APK has minSdkVersion 24 (Android 7.0)
findings.evidence: README.md:14 `在 Android 设备上打开下载的 .apk 文件（需 Android 6.0 及以上版本）。` android/app/build.gradle:37 `minSdk = flutter.minSdkVersion`; ~/flutter/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt:26 `val minSdkVersion: Int = 24` (Flutter 3.44.8, the version pinned in CI). build/app/intermediates/merged_manifests/release/processReleaseManifest/AndroidManifest.xml contains minSdkVersion="24" for the 0.1.3 build whose sha256 matches the published release asset.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone follows the README on an Android 6.0/6.0.1 device (API 23): the package installer refuses the APK with a parse/incompatible error although the README says the device is supported.
findings.fix: Change the README to Android 7.0 (API 24), or pin `minSdk` explicitly in android/app/build.gradle so a Flutter upgrade cannot move it silently and the README can state a fixed number.

findings.title: release.sh leaves a bumped, uncommitted, untagged tree when a step after the version edit fails
findings.evidence: tool/release.sh:94 rewrites pubspec.yaml in place; the CHANGELOG failure branch (124-128) removes only `CHANGELOG.md.new` and `/tmp/release_entry.md` and exits without restoring pubspec.yaml; lines 135-137 `git add` / `git commit` / `git tag` run under `set -e` with no trap, so a failing commit (pre-commit hook, signing, missing identity) exits with pubspec.yaml and CHANGELOG.md modified and staged and no tag. The preflight at line 42 then blocks the retry: `error: working tree is dirty`. The script also never checks the current branch (the repo has `redesign-v5` and `redesign-v6` next to `main`), and the origin check at line 49 only warns.
findings.failure_scenario: `git commit` fails inside `tool/release.sh patch "..."`: the version reads 0.1.4+5 in pubspec.yaml and the changelog has a 0.1.4 entry, but there is no commit and no tag. Re-running refuses with 'working tree is dirty'; running build_release.sh at this point builds an APK labelled 0.1.4 from an unreleased tree. Separately, running the script while a redesign branch is checked out commits and tags the release on that branch, not on main.
findings.fix: Add `trap 'git checkout -- pubspec.yaml CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null; git reset -q pubspec.yaml CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null' ERR` (cleared after the tag succeeds), and in preflight refuse unless `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` is `main`.

findings.title: Version numbers 1.0.0 through 6.0.0 are already tagged, so the restarted 0.x series cannot be released past 0.x
findings.evidence: tool/release.sh:86-89 `if git rev-parse "v$NEW_SHORT" ... echo "error: tag v$NEW_SHORT already exists"; exit 1`. `git tag -l` lists v1.0.0, v2.0.0 ... v6.0.0 (57 tags from the pre-rename series) alongside v0.1.0-v0.1.3, and CHANGELOG.md already has `## [1.0.0] - 2026-07-28` (line 366) through `## [6.0.0]` (line 48) below the 0.1.x entries. pubspec.yaml:4 is 0.1.3+4.
findings.failure_scenario: `tool/release.sh major "..."` computes 1.0.0 and stops with 'tag v1.0.0 already exists'. The same happens for any later bump that lands on a number used by the old series (2.0.0, 2.1.0, 3.0.0-3.13.0, 4.0.0, 5.0.0, 6.0.0). Working around it by deleting the old tag orphans that GitHub release and leaves two `## [1.0.0]` headings in CHANGELOG.md for different apps.
findings.fix: Decide the scheme now: either namespace the old series (retag as `legacy-vX.Y.Z` and mark those CHANGELOG sections as the pre-rename app `com.bilibeat.bilibeat`), or document that the new series must skip to 7.0.0 for its first major and make `major` do that.

findings.title: build_release.sh builds whatever is checked out under the pubspec version and overwrites that version's symbols
findings.evidence: tool/build_release.sh:55-58 `VERSION=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml ...)`, `SYMBOLS_DIR="symbols/$VERSION"`, `mkdir -p`; lines 91-94 write `--split-debug-info="$SYMBOLS_DIR"` unconditionally. There is no check that the tree is clean or that HEAD is the commit tagged `v$SHORT_VERSION`. Today HEAD (9e5b784) is two commits past v0.1.3 with pubspec still at 0.1.3+4, and build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/bilibeats-0.1.3-arm64-v8a.apk was rewritten at 23:11 on Oct 5, after the release assets were uploaded (22:03Z). Those two commits touched no Dart, so the bytes happen to match the published asset (sha256 951418a7...), but nothing enforces that.
findings.failure_scenario: After tagging 0.1.x the user fixes something in lib/ and runs `tool/build_release.sh` to try it on the phone before cutting the next release. The script produces a second, different `bilibeats-0.1.x-arm64-v8a.apk` with the same versionName/versionCode and replaces symbols/0.1.x+N/app.android-arm64.symbols. A crash trace from the published 0.1.x build now symbolizes against the wrong file (wrong or garbage frames), and two different binaries carry the same version.
findings.fix: In build_release.sh refuse (or require an explicit `--dev` flag that writes to `symbols/dev/` and names the artifact `-dev`) unless `git status --porcelain` is empty and `git describe --exact-match --tags HEAD` equals `v$SHORT_VERSION`.

findings.title: CI never compiles iOS or any release-mode build, so the configurations that are actually shipped are untested
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:49-55 matrix is only `flutter build apk --debug` (ubuntu) and `flutter build macos --debug`. The comment at 40-43 says the job exists to catch 'a bad SPM/CocoaPods file ... a native API gone in a plugin update', but there is no iOS entry although an unsigned .ipa is published for every release and `image_picker_ios` has no macOS counterpart. Release-only Android configuration is also never exercised: android/app/build.gradle:70-75 (`minifyEnabled`, `shrinkResources`, proguard-rules.pro), 95-101 (release-variant jniLibs excludes), the lintVital step that tool/build_release.sh:22-24 says needs JDK 21, and `--obfuscate`.
findings.failure_scenario: A dependency bump (e.g. the pending image_picker_ios 0.8.13+6 -> +9 or jni 1.0.2 -> 1.1.0 from `flutter pub outdated`) breaks the iOS SwiftPM build or needs a new R8 keep rule. CI stays green; the break is found only when `tool/build_release.sh all` runs after release.sh has already committed and tagged the version, or, for an R8 strip, at runtime on the phone.
findings.fix: Add matrix entries `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign` on macos-latest and `flutter build apk --release --target-platform android-arm64` on ubuntu with `actions/setup-java` (temurin 21); the debug-key fallback already lets the release APK build without secrets.

findings.title: make_keystore.sh writes an unverified password and cannot be re-run after a partial run
findings.evidence: tool/make_keystore.sh:50-51 `printf 'Re-enter the keystore password ...'; read -rs PASS` and 59-65 write it straight into key.properties with no check against the keystore keytool just created (41-47). `read` with default IFS also strips leading/trailing whitespace from the password. Lines 26-30 refuse to run when `$KEYSTORE` or `$PROPS` exists. tool/build_release.sh:82 tells the user to 'Run tool/make_keystore.sh first' whenever key.properties is missing.
findings.failure_scenario: The user mistypes the re-entered password (or presses Ctrl-C at that prompt). Case 1: key.properties holds a wrong password and the next release build fails in Gradle's signing task with a keystore error. Case 2: the .jks exists but key.properties does not, so build_release.sh warns, signs with the debug key and points at make_keystore.sh, which now exits with 'already exists. Refusing to overwrite'. Neither script says how to recover (hand-write key.properties).
findings.fix: After `read`, verify before writing: `KS_PASS="$PASS" keytool -list -keystore "$KEYSTORE" -alias "$ALIAS" -storepass:env KS_PASS >/dev/null` and loop on failure; use `IFS= read -rs PASS`. When the keystore exists but key.properties does not, offer to write only key.properties instead of refusing.

findings.title: README forbids commercial use while the project is licensed GPL-3.0, which does not permit that restriction
findings.evidence: README.md:136 `无破解与商业化：本项目严禁用于任何商业牟利行为` and README.md:141 `本项目基于 GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPL-3.0) 开源`; LICENSE is the GPLv3 text (added in 0550189, one commit after the disclaimer in 4f3e4e6). GPLv3 section 7 treats a field-of-use limit as a 'further restriction' that recipients may remove, and section 10 forbids imposing further restrictions on the rights granted.
findings.failure_scenario: The two statements contradict each other: under the LICENSE file anyone may use and redistribute the app commercially, so the README's prohibition is unenforceable and the project's actual terms are ambiguous to anyone reading the repository.
findings.fix: Reword the disclaimer line as a statement about the project itself (no ads, no paid tiers, not operated commercially by the author) rather than a prohibition on users, or choose a licence that actually carries a non-commercial term.

find:release aa6dad.notes:
Nothing in this area is worse than medium; the release pipeline as actually used (patch bumps, key present) is sound.

Checked and found sound:
- Secrets: no keystore, key.properties or literal password was ever committed (`git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only`, and `-S storePassword/keyPassword` only hits build.gradle's property lookups in 3e6c2b9). Both files are ignored by .gitignore and android/.gitignore. key.properties is mode 600 and its storeFile/keyAlias match the renamed keystore and alias. Passwords never reach argv. The .jks itself is mode 644 locally (the script's chmod 600 was lost in the rename); negligible on a single-user Mac.
- Published 0.1.3: the local bilibeats-0.1.3-arm64-v8a.apk has the same sha256 as the GitHub release asset, v0.1.3 is marked Latest (so README's releases/latest link is right despite v6.0.0 existing), and a symbols zip is attached to 0.1.0, 0.1.2 and 0.1.3. symbols/ holds all four platform files per 0.1.x version.
- CI: the last 8 runs are green, Flutter is pinned to 3.44.8 (matches the local SDK and README), permissions are contents: read, and both live test files carry @Tags(['live']). Actions are pinned by tag (actions/checkout@v4, subosito/flutter-action@v2), not SHA; with read-only permissions and no secrets I did not rate that a finding.
- Dependencies: OSV batch query for all 84 locked hosted packages returned no advisories. No discontinued packages and no outdated majors among direct dependencies (only image_picker 1.2.3 -> 1.2.4). Licences of the linked packages are MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0, all GPL-3.0 compatible. Only public package names and versions were sent to osv.dev.
- sdk constraint '>=3.0.0 <4.0.0': the lockfile already enforces dart >=3.12.0 / flutter >=3.44.0 through dependencies and analyze is clean at language version 3.0, so the loose bound is cosmetic.
- Android config: the Flutter Gradle plugin applies kotlin-android itself; jni and jni_flutter ship consumer R8 rules; no Android Studio JDK shadows the script's JAVA_HOME check on this machine.
- Apple config: SwiftPM is enabled by default on stable 3.44.8, every darwin plugin has a Package.swift at or below iOS 13.0 / macOS 10.15, and macOS Release.entitlements includes network.client. Product names match the paths build_release.sh expects (Runner.app, BiliBeats.app).
- release.sh: sed branches for BSD/GNU, the tag-exists check runs before any file is modified, changelog insertion handles a missing heading, and notes with $, backticks or backslashes are preserved.
- README/CLAUDE.md counts match (540 titles, 126 surveyed videos).

Minor, not reported as findings: build_release.sh's header and README omit the macos target that `all` builds; its closing `ls *-release.apk` does not list the renamed artifact; README says CI runs `flutter test` where it runs `--exclude-tags live`; make_brand_assets.py prints a hard-coded icon count.

Not determined: LICENSE was only spot-checked (head, tail, 674 lines) rather than read in full; the provenance and licence of tool/brand/app_icon_source.jpg cannot be established from the repository; whether an iOS or release build would pass on a GitHub runner today was not tested (no builds were run).

findings.title: 'a failed install does not switch the display' passes only because the fake's setAudioSources fails atomically; the real player has already replaced the queue and the handler publishes it
findings.evidence:
test/playback_handler_test.dart:147-150 `fake.failNextSource = true; await handler.playTrack(t[1], queue: t); expect(handler.currentTrack, t[0]); expect(fake.currentTag, t[0]);`.
