Fake, test/fake_audio_player.dart:190-194: `if (failNextSource) { failNextSource = false; throw ja.PlayerException(1, 'fake source failure', initialIndex); }` comes BEFORE `_children = audioSources.cast<...>().toList();` so a failed load leaves the old playlist, index and sequence untouched.
Real just_audio 0.10.6, lib/just_audio.dart:891 `await _playlist._init(audioSources, loadRequest.shuffleOrder);` runs before `duration = await load();` (895); _init (3165-3174) does `this.children.replaceRange(0, this.children.length, children);` and `await player._broadcastSequence();`. Nothing restores the old children when load() throws. SequenceState.currentIndex (2154-2155) is `sequence.isNotEmpty ? min(_currentIndex ?? 0, sequence.length - 1) : null`, so currentSource is always an item of the NEW list.
Handler, lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:569-580: the catch only records `failure`, then `if (_installing == 0) { _recordHistory = recordHistory; _publish(); ... }` runs unconditionally. _publish (216-231) reads `_player.sequenceState`, sees a different current id and calls `_announce(current)`, which sets nowPlaying, mediaItem and (283) `DatabaseService.addRecentlyPlayed(track)`. Only afterwards (584-587) is '无法播放「…」' emitted and false returned. There is no reinstall of the previous queue anywhere in the file.
findings.failure_scenario: Song A is playing from queue Q1. The listener taps song X whose local file cannot be opened (a truncated/non-audio body that passed the >=1024-byte check, or a file removed outside the app while the .ready marker and the downloaded memo remain). With the real player: Q1 is discarded before the load is attempted, the load throws, the handler publishes Q2 anyway - the player page, mini player, notification and queue sheet switch to a track of Q2, that track is written to 最近播放 although it never played, A stops, and the snack says 无法播放. The class doc's contract (and this test's name) says nothing changes. The test cannot see any of it because the fake models failure as a no-op. The '无法播放' message is asserted by no test either.
findings.fix: Make the fake mirror the real ordering (assign _children/_index and emit the sequence before the delay/throw) so the test exercises what happens on device; then make _install honour the contract, e.g. remember the previous sources/index/position and reinstall them (without recording history) when setAudioSources throws something other than PlayerInterruptedException, and assert the message.

findings.title: No test ever loads a valid persisted store from disk: the write-envelope / read-payload round trip for downloads, playlists, history, prefs and lyrics is unverified
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:99-109 `_loadFuture` is a process-wide static with no reset hook, so each test file loads exactly once, and every file starts from an empty temp directory (test/audio_test_harness.dart:160 `Directory.systemTemp.createTemp('bilibeat_$tag')`). The only files present at load time in the whole suite are the deliberately unreadable ones in test/store_safety_test.dart:43-47. After that every assertion reads in-memory lists: store_safety_test.dart:71 `DatabaseService.getRecentlyPlayed()`, download_management_test.dart:85 `getPlaylists()`, lyric_meta_test.dart:72 `getDownloadedTracks`, lyric_ownership_test.dart `LyricsStore.get/peek`. LyricsStore._load's merge branch (lib/services/lyrics_store.dart:64-73 `if (text != null) { final parsed = await compute(_parseLyricsFile, text); ... }`) never executes with a readable file. The only file read back is bilibeat_session.json (playback_handler_test.dart:214). The readers are lenient in a dangerous way: database_service.dart:19-20 `DatabaseService._readPayload(jsonDecode(json)) as List<dynamic>? ?? []` and 425 `return decoded['data'];` - a missing/renamed key yields an empty list, not an exception, so the file is not set aside. test/serialization_test.dart round-trips models only, never `_envelope`/`_readPayload`/`_parsePlaylistList`. The legacy bare-list format (documented at 405-407) is only exercised by render_screens.dart, which is not part of the suite.
findings.failure_scenario: A change to `_envelope` or `_readPayload` (renaming 'data', nesting the payload, a schema bump whose migration is wrong) or to `_parsePlaylistList` passes all 178 tests. On the next real launch every store reads as an empty list without error, so nothing is moved to .unreadable; the first toggleFavorite / addRecentlyPlayed / pin then rewrites bilibeat_playlists.json, bilibeat_recently_played.json or bilibeat_lyrics.json from the empty state. Playlists, favourites and pinned lyrics are gone for good (downloads alone come back through _discoverAudioFiles).
findings.fix: Add a restart test: write through the public API in one isolate-fresh file (or add a @visibleForTesting `DatabaseService.resetForTest()` / `LyricsStore.resetForTest()` that clears the static caches), then reload from the same directory and compare downloads, playlists with their tracks, favourites, history, prefs, search history and a pinned + an automatic lyric. Include one fixture in the bare pre-envelope format.

findings.title: The whole of zhoushen_test.dart is tagged live, so about 30 offline cleanTitle regression tests never run in CI
findings.evidence: test/zhoushen_test.dart:1-2 `@Tags(['live'])` / `library;` tags every test in the file. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `flutter test --exclude-tags live`, and the audit baseline (178 tests) was taken the same way. Of the 52 declared tests (plus 10 more generated by the forEach at 71-77), only 29 call `_skipIfOffline()` (22 directly, 7 through `check` at 142-148). The rest are pure, synchronous calls such as 36-43 `LyricsEngine.cleanTitle('周深-世界赠予我的 4k最高音质无损纯享 ...')`, 57-78 (studio-listening titles), 101-139 (knownArtists crediting), 451-482 (【show】 artist 《song》 regressions), 514-527 (English glue noise, standalone separator). The CI-visible parser tests are test/library_features_test.dart:89-121 (5 cases), test/widget_test.dart:274-294 (4 cases) and test/title_parser_test.dart:17-25, which only asserts `parsed['songTitle']` is non-null and non-empty for the 540-title corpus.
findings.failure_scenario: A change to LyricsEngine.cleanTitle that re-breaks a documented regression (e.g. '【声生不息3】 黄绮珊&周深 《岁月》' crediting 声生不息3 again, or '周深 - Alive' losing its title to the Live noise word) is pushed. CI is green because none of those cases is in an untagged file. cleanTitle feeds TrackCredit.artistOf for every unnamed song, so the wrong artist shows in every list and in the artist lens, and seeds the lyric and matching queries.
findings.fix: Move the tests that do not touch the network into an untagged file (e.g. test/title_rules_test.dart) and leave only the NetEase-backed ones under @Tags(['live']); or tag the individual live tests/groups with `tags: 'live'` instead of the library.

findings.title: _skipIfOffline marks the test skipped but lets the body run, so every NetEase-backed test fails when offline
findings.evidence: test/zhoushen_test.dart:13-15 claims 'every live-NetEase test starts with this so the suite stays green offline'. 16-33: `Future<void> _skipIfOffline() async { if (_networkChecked != null) { if (!_networkAvailable) markTestSkipped('requires music.163.com'); return; } ... catch (_) { markTestSkipped('requires music.163.com'); } }` returns void; callers do `await _skipIfOffline();` and carry on, e.g. 82-89 `final id = await LyricsEngine.identify(title, uploader: 'JLRS-LeoFM'); expect(id?.artist, '周深', reason: title);`. test_api-0.7.x lib/src/scaffolding/utils.dart:40-45: 'A skipped test may still fail if any exception is thrown ... If the entire test should be skipped `return` from the test body after marking it as skipped.' Offline, identify returns null (lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:689 'Returns null when nothing is confirmed (or the network is down)'). The sibling file does it correctly: test/recognition_live_test.dart:35-38 `markTestSkipped(...); return;`.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the documented `flutter test` (CLAUDE.md lists it without --exclude-tags) on a machine with no route to music.163.com, or behind a network where the TCP probe fails. The 29 tests that call _skipIfOffline are marked skipped and then fail on their expectations (`expect(id?.artist, '周深')` against null), so the run is red for a reason unrelated to the code - the opposite of what the helper promises. Only the two cases that expect null (175-182) pass.
findings.fix: Return a bool and bail out: `Future<bool> _online() async {...}` with `if (!await _online()) { markTestSkipped('requires music.163.com'); return; }` at each call site (and inside `check`).

findings.title: Every download test supplies Track.audioUrl, a field production never sets: the playurl lookup and stream selection that every real download depends on has no test
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:297-303 `var url = track.audioUrl; if (url == null || url.isEmpty) { final info = await BilibiliSdk.fetchAudioStream(track.bvid, track.cid); url = info?['url']; final loudness = double.tryParse(info?['loudness'] ?? ''); if (loudness != null) track = track.copyWith(loudness: loudness); }`. `grep -rn audioUrl lib` outside models/track.dart finds only that line: nothing in lib/ ever assigns audioUrl, so production always takes the fetchAudioStream branch. Tests always bypass it: test/audio_test_harness.dart:185 `audioUrl: server.urlFor(name)`, test/download_resume_test.dart:124 `audioUrl: server.url`. BilibiliSdk.fetchAudioStream (lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:366-447) does its JSON handling inline with the request (durl first, then dash audio sorted by `bandwidth`, baseUrl/base_url/backupUrl, `volume.measured_i`) inside a catch-all that returns null (443-447); there is no parse seam and no test references it. The follow-on `saveTrackMetadata(track, force: track.loudness != null)` (348) is likewise never reached with a loudness.
findings.failure_scenario: A refactor of the playurl parsing (a wrong cast on `bandwidth`, reading `durl.first['url']` from a changed shape, dropping the https rewrite) makes fetchAudioStream throw into its catch-all and return null. Every download and every 下载并播放 then fails with 无法获取音源下载链接 - the app can no longer add music - while analyze and all tests stay green. Equally, a regression that stops carrying `loudness` into the stored track silently disables levelling for new downloads.
findings.fix: Extract the body handling into a @visibleForTesting `parseAudioStream(Map json)` (as was done for parseRecognisedMusic / isRiskControlled) and test it with recorded durl-only, dash-only, backupUrl-only and volume-bearing answers; add one download test with audioUrl null and an injectable stream resolver to cover the loudness merge and forced metadata write.

findings.title: Startup discovery and pruning of the downloaded list (_discoverAudioFiles) is untested; it rewrites bilibeat_downloaded.json on every launch that finds a difference
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:214-306. Recovery half (220-259): each `audio_<id>.ready` with a non-empty .m4a and a .json is added when `!_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id)`. Prune half (261-296): for each stored track `exists = await ready.exists() && await audio.exists() && await audio.length() > 0;` built from `File('$dirPath/bilibeat_audio/audio_${t.id}.m4a')`; anything else goes to `prunedIds`, and `if (toKeep.length != beforePrune) { _downloadedTracks..clear()..addAll(toKeep); unawaited(_persistDownloaded()); }`. No test reaches either half with data: every suite file loads once from an empty directory (see audio_test_harness.dart:160 and the static `_loadFuture` at database_service.dart:99-109), so `_downloadedTracks` and bilibeat_audio are both empty when _load runs. The only place that seeds .ready/.m4a/.json before a load is test/render_screens.dart:108-113, which is not in the suite and asserts nothing about the list.
findings.failure_scenario: The path convention is duplicated here rather than taken from AudioDownloadService (`_audioPath`/`_readyPath`, audio_download_service.dart:94-100). If one side changes (a new extension, a sub-folder, a different marker), the prune loop sees every stored track as missing on the next launch, clears the in-memory list and persists the empty list; the library screen is empty and, if discovery is affected by the same change, stays empty although the audio is on disk. Conversely a break in the recovery half means a set-aside (damaged) bilibeat_downloaded.json no longer comes back from the per-track .json files. No test fails in either case.
findings.fix: Add a test that seeds a documents folder before first load with (a) a downloaded.json entry whose files exist, (b) one whose .m4a is missing, (c) a ready+m4a+json triple not listed, and asserts the loaded list and the rewritten file; have _discoverAudioFiles use AudioDownloadService's path helpers so the convention lives in one place.

findings.title: TrackNaming._name, the only code that renames songs without the listener asking, has no test; only the pure settled() predicate is covered
findings.evidence: lib/services/track_naming.dart:119-197. The guards that protect the listener's own naming are all in here: 122 `if (before == null || _settled(before)) return;`, the legacy branch 131-143 (`if (before.uploader.trim() != owner.trim()) { await _save(before.copyWith(rawUploader: owner, matcher: 0)); return; }`), the re-read 162-169 (`stored.title != before.title || stored.uploader != before.uploader || stored.matcher != before.matcher || stored.named != before.named`), and the offline retry 155-159. `_save` (114-117) goes to DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata, which overwrites the copy in downloads, every playlist and history (database_service.dart:521-544). The suite references TrackNaming only at test/track_test.dart:95-121 (`TrackNaming.matcher` and `TrackNaming.settled`). recognised_music_test / recognition_live_test call LyricsEngine.identify directly, never the apply step. BilibiliSdk.fetchVideoHints is called statically (125) with no injection point, which is why it cannot be driven from a hermetic test today.
findings.failure_scenario: A change that loosens one guard - for instance dropping the `stored.named != before.named` comparison, or treating `matcher == null` as re-checkable without the owner comparison - makes the next play of a song the listener renamed through 编辑信息 before 0.1.x (named, matcher null) replace their title, artist and cover with the catalogue's answer in the library, 收藏 and every playlist. All tests pass; CLAUDE.md's instruction to raise `matcher` to re-check old answers makes this path run across the whole library after such a release.
findings.fix: Give _name injectable lookups (hints fetcher and identify function, defaulting to the real ones) and test: listener-named (matcher 0) untouched; legacy-named with a different artist than the owner stamped matcher 0 and left alone; an edit made while the lookup is in flight is not overwritten; offline (found null, not settled) leaves the track retryable; a confirmed answer writes title/artist/cover/rawUploader/matcher.

findings.title: The cover sweep that deletes files from bilibeat_covers at launch is untested; only the pure rebaseCover string function is
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:123-125 `_rebaseCovers(dir); if (!_setAsideAny) unawaited(_sweepCovers(dir));` and 173-192: `used` is built from `local(t.coverUrl)` over downloads, history and playlists, then `await for (final entity in folder.list()) { if (entity is! File || used.contains(entity.path)) continue; if ((await entity.lastModified()).isAfter(cutoff)) continue; await entity.delete(); }`. Keeping a cover depends on an exact string match between `entity.path` (from listing `'$docs/bilibeat_covers'`) and the stored coverUrl after _rebaseCovers. test/store_safety_test.dart:87-116 tests `DatabaseService.rebaseCover(url, now)` only; no test creates a bilibeat_covers folder, and in store_safety_test `_setAsideAny` is true so the sweep is skipped altogether. The one-day cutoff additionally hides any mismatch from a quick manual check.
findings.failure_scenario: A change in how picked covers are stored (a `file://` prefix that `local` does not strip the same way, a trailing-slash or symlinked documents path, covers referenced from a new store such as artist portraits that is not added to `used`) makes `used.contains(entity.path)` false for covers still in use. Nothing happens for a day; from the next launch after that, every such cover is deleted and the affected songs and playlists show the placeholder permanently - the picked image was the only copy. No test notices.
findings.fix: Test _load against a seeded folder: a referenced cover older than a day (kept), an unreferenced old one (deleted), an unreferenced fresh one (kept), a cover referenced through a file:// URL and one stored under a previous container path (kept after rebase).

findings.title: The handler's recovery paths have no test and the fake cannot drive them: player errors, stop(), and play() on an empty queue
findings.evidence: test/fake_audio_player.dart:45-46 `// ignore: close_sinks` / `final _errors = StreamController<ja.PlayerException>.broadcast();` is exposed as errorStream (151) but nothing ever adds to it and there is no simulateError control, so lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:207-210 (`_messages.add('有歌曲无法播放，已跳过')`) and the real player's maxSkipsOnError behaviour (just_audio.dart:417-427: seekToNext, or pause after the limit) are unreachable from tests. `setSourceDelay` (fake 15, 189) is never set by any test, so overlapping installs - `_installing > 1` and the `on ja.PlayerInterruptedException` branch at handler 567-568 - are also unexercised; the fake would not throw that exception anyway (two overlapping calls both succeed and the slower, older one lands last, the reverse of the real player). No test in test/playback_handler_test.dart calls handler.stop(), handler.play(), togglePlayPause, onTaskRemoved, skipToQueueItem or selectQueueTrack; `removeTracks` is only tested for a non-current track (225-237), never for the playing one or for emptying the queue (handler 861-865).
findings.failure_scenario: Regressions that would pass the suite: play() from a media button after a cold start no longer restoring the saved session (handler 750-756) - the headset button does nothing until the app is opened; stop() no longer saving the session before releasing the player (780-781) - position lost after the 30-minute idle stop; deleting the song that is playing leaving nowPlaying pointing at a removed file; two quick taps on downloaded songs leaving `_installing` stuck above zero, after which _publish (214) returns early forever and the UI freezes on one song.
findings.fix: Add simulateError(index) and PlayerInterruptedException-on-overlap to the fake (interrupt the earlier pending setAudioSources when a newer one starts), then add tests for: error on the current item, two overlapping playTrack calls on downloaded songs, stop() followed by play(), play() on a fresh handler with a saved session, and removing the current / the only track.

find:tests a41ec6.notes:
Read-only; nothing was run and no network request was made. An untracked docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md from the earlier (interrupted) run exists; I looked at its headings only to avoid repeating other finders (their #20, #48/#77, #72, #73 touch tests I also looked at; not re-reported).

Checked and found sound:
- Hermetic HTTP. Every HttpClient in lib/ comes from biliHttpClient (bili_http.dart:19) and only getUrl is used (no postUrl/openUrl). useHermeticHttp's client (audio_test_harness.dart:38-43) lets 127.0.0.1/localhost through and throws SocketException otherwise. The three non-live files on useRealHttp (playback_handler_test, download_management_test, download_resume_test) cannot reach a third party: the handler is built with an injected player so loudnessLookup is null (audio_player_handler.dart:56-58), tracks carry a localhost audioUrl, and neither AppServices nor TrackNaming is initialised there. Files with no override and a Flutter binding get flutter_test's 400 mock; files with neither (track_test, title_parser_test, lyrics_matching_test, serialization_test) call only synchronous functions. testWidgetsWithHttp's `HttpOverrides.runZoned(() => body(tester))` passes no override and so just delegates to the global one - the comment above it is misleading but the behaviour is right.
- runAsync usage in lyric_fav/lyric_meta/lyric_paste: real IO is started or drained inside tester.runAsync (startPlaying, pumpUntil, settle); the library is loaded in real time before any fake-clock code depends on it.
- Fake vs real just_audio beyond the finding above: play() is never awaited by the handler (real play() completes only on pause/stop), shuffle-with-current-first matches DefaultShuffleOrder via _shuffle(initialIndex), completed -> pause -> seek(first) matches, playingStream distinctness matches. Divergences I judged immaterial to current tests: real seek() is a no-op while processingState is loading; real sequenceStateStream replays on listen; real currentIndex changes arrive by playback event after seek()/removeAudioSourceAt() return (the earlier playback finder already reported the removal case).
- Download resume tests (Range/If-Range/416/orphan .part/too-long .part) assert on bytes and on the Range headers seen by the server; they are meaningful. Unsafe-id test checks both the lookup and that no request was made.
- lyric_ownership_test and store_safety_test assert real outcomes (set-aside byte equality, revision rejection, pin-before-load visibility). The deliberately destructive last test in lyric_ownership_test is order-dependent by design and is last.
- contrast_test, marquee tests, LyricsView/MiniPlayer/LocalSearch/TasteProfile groups: assertions are real; no tautologies found. title_parser_test is only a does-not-throw / non-empty smoke test over the corpus (noted in the live-tag finding).
- No time-zone or wall-clock dependence found; waitFor/waitForTrue poll with generous deadlines; the one real timer (200 ms sleep timer) has a 10 s wait.

Minor, not reported as findings:
- stubDocs temp directories (and lyric_ownership's) are never deleted; each run leaves about seven bilibeat_* folders in the system temp directory.
- playback_handler_test 'each track plays at the volume...' writes normalizeVolume=false to the shared prefs and only restores it on the last line; a failure before that line cascades into the next test.
- AudioDownloadService/DatabaseService/LyricsStore/DownloadManager statics are shared by all tests in a file; the suite copes by using unique ids per test (documented in the files), so tests are order-tolerant but cannot be made to reload state - which is the root of the 'no valid store is ever loaded' gap.
- render_screens.dart: returns from main() with no tests when the macOS font path is missing (the tool then reports no tests rather than a skip); the boxed lens labels are because _LensLabel's AnimatedDefaultTextStyle replaces the themed style (no fontFamily), so they fall to the test font - a harness limitation as CLAUDE.md says, not an app bug. Recommendations in the render are whatever the 400-mock yields.

Could not determine: the exact native event sequence after a failed load on Android/iOS (which index is current, whether maxSkipsOnError then starts the next item). The Dart-side facts in the first finding (playlist replaced and broadcast before load, no rollback, handler publishes after failure) are from source; the on-device symptom should be confirmed with a deliberately corrupt audio file.

findings.title: Short-link resolver validates the host by substring, so a pasted look-alike link makes the app fetch (and follow redirects from) an arbitrary host, over cleartext if asked
findings.evidence:
lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:87-91 picks the URL: `RegExp(r'(?:https?://)?(?:www\.)?(?:b23\.tv|bili2233\.cn|acg\.tv)/[^\s]+').firstMatch(input) ?? RegExp(r'https?://[^\s]+').firstMatch(input);` -- the fallback takes ANY url in the text.
lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:97-101 is the only host check: `if (!urlStr.contains('b23.tv') && !urlStr.contains('bili2233.cn') && !urlStr.contains('acg.tv')) { return null; }` -- a substring of the whole URL, not the host.
lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:103-109: `final uri = Uri.parse(urlStr); final req = await _httpClient.getUrl(uri)... // Let HttpClient follow redirects automatically` and 111-115 reads the whole body with no size cap; 122-123 then trusts a BV number found anywhere in that body: `final bvInBody = _bvId.firstMatch(body); if (bvInBody != null) return 'BV${bvInBody.group(1)}';`.
Entry gate at 474-476 is the same substring test on the raw query. Scheme is not forced to https (line 94 only adds https when no scheme is present). `android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"` (AndroidManifest.xml:19) does not apply: the Dart SDK shipped with this Flutter (~/flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/lib/_http/http_impl.dart) has no cleartext policy check at all (no `isInsecureConnectionAllowed`), and dart:io follows up to 5 redirects to any host/scheme.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener pastes share text containing `https://b23.tv.evil.example/a` (or `http://192.168.1.1/apply.cgi?x=b23.tv`) into search. The first regex does not match (b23.tv is not followed by `/`), the fallback regex takes the whole URL, the substring check passes, and the app issues a GET to that host with redirects followed -- to an attacker server (IP disclosure, attacker-chosen BV returned from the body so a different video than the one advertised is listed as the result), to a cleartext http URL, or to a device on the home LAN (GET-triggered actions on a router/IoT admin page). A genuine `http://b23.tv/...` link is likewise fetched in cleartext and can be rewritten on path.
findings.fix: Parse the candidate with Uri.tryParse and require `uri.scheme == 'https'` (upgrade http) and `uri.host` to be exactly b23.tv / bili2233.cn / acg.tv (or a `.`-prefixed subdomain); drop the generic `https?://\S+` fallback. Set `req.followRedirects = false`, read the Location header yourself and only extract the BV from it (optionally follow one hop if its host ends with bilibili.com). Cap the body read.

findings.title: On iOS every downloaded song and the cover cache live in backed-up directories, contradicting the app's own 'nothing is backed up' policy
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:67-68: `final docs = await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory(); final path = '${docs.path}/bilibeat_audio';` -- all audio goes to Documents.
lib/widgets/cached_cover_image.dart:179-182: `// Application Support, not the temp dir ...` `final supportDir = await getApplicationSupportDirectory(); final cacheDir = Directory('${supportDir.path}/bilibeat_covers');` (up to 200 MB, line 61).
lib/services/database_service.dart:89 puts library, history, search history and lyrics JSON in Documents too.
Android explicitly opts out: android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:20-22 `android:allowBackup="false" android:fullBackupContent="false" android:dataExtractionRules=...` and data_extraction_rules.xml: `Nothing in BiliBeat is worth restoring: downloads are re-downloaded ... Opt everything out so no cached audio or credentials ever leak`.
Nothing in ios/, macos/ or lib/ sets the excluded-from-backup resource value (grep for `xcludedFromBackup` returns nothing), and on iOS both Documents and Library/Application Support are included in iCloud and Finder backups.
findings.failure_scenario: The iOS build is installed on a phone with iCloud Backup enabled and a few GB of songs downloaded. Every `audio_*.m4a`, the 200 MB cover cache, the play history and the search history are uploaded to iCloud with the device backup: the free 5 GB quota fills and device backups start failing, and data the Android build deliberately keeps off any backup (listening and search history) leaves the device.
findings.fix: On iOS/macOS store re-downloadable audio and the cover cache outside the backup set (e.g. `Library/Caches`-independent `Application Support/<dir>` with `URLResourceKey.isExcludedFromBackupKey = true` set on `bilibeat_audio` and `bilibeat_covers` via a small platform channel / the existing native side), or set the flag on the two directories after creating them.

findings.title: Lock-screen artwork path decodes the full-resolution cover on the Android main thread and re-downloads the original remote cover without resizing
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:391-397: `artUri: track.coverUrl.isEmpty ? null : Uri.tryParse(track.coverUrl.startsWith('/') ? 'file://${track.coverUrl}' : track.coverUrl)` -- the raw coverUrl, not the CDN-resized one CachedCoverImage uses (cached_cover_image.dart:52 `'$url@${w}w_${h}h_1e_1c.webp'`).
lib/main.dart:41-51 `AudioServiceConfig(...)` sets no `androidArtDownscaleSize`.
audio_service-0.18.19/lib/audio_service.dart:1058-1059 sends a file art path straight to the platform; for http(s) it fetches the URL with `cacheManager.getSingleFile(artUri.toString())` (a second, separate cover cache, no Referer, original size).
audio_service-0.18.19/android/.../AudioService.java:218-240: when `config.artDownscaleWidth == -1` it runs `bitmap = BitmapFactory.decodeFile(artUri.getPath());` with no sampling, inside setMetadata on the platform thread; the surrounding `catch (Exception e)` (line 244) does not catch OutOfMemoryError.
lib/utils/cover_picker.dart:11 `ImagePicker().pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery)` passes no maxWidth/imageQuality, and line 19 copies the original file.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener sets a camera photo (12-50 MP, or a 200 MP shot on recent phones) as a song's cover via 编辑信息. Each time that song becomes current (and again when the session is restored at launch) the service decodes the whole image -- 48 MB of pixels for 12 MP, ~200 MB for 50 MP, ~800 MB for 200 MP -- on the main thread, stalling the UI for hundreds of ms and, for the largest photos, throwing an uncaught OutOfMemoryError that kills the app on every start because the session restore replays the same item. Separately, every played track with a Bilibili cover downloads the original multi-megabyte image again through flutter_cache_manager although a resized copy is already in the app's own cover cache.
findings.fix: Pass `androidArtDownscaleSize: Size(512, 512)` (and `preloadArtwork: false`) in AudioServiceConfig; give `artUri` the CDN-resized URL (`CachedCoverImage.sizedUrl(coverUrl, 512, 512)`); and pick covers with `pickImage(source: ..., maxWidth: 1600, maxHeight: 1600, imageQuality: 90)`.

findings.title: Cover picker derives the extension with split('.').last, building a nested path when the picked file has no extension
findings.evidence:
lib/utils/cover_picker.dart:16-19: `final ext = image.path.split('.').last; final saved = File('${dir.path}/${prefix}_${DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}.$ext'); await File(image.path).copy(saved.path);` and 21-23 swallow the error: `catch (e) { debugPrint('Cover pick failed: $e'); return null; }`.
The split is on the whole path, not the basename. On Android the picked file is copied to `{cacheDir}/{uuid}/{fileName}` (image_picker_android-0.8.13+19 FileUtils.java: `File targetDirectory = new File(context.getCacheDir(), uuid)`), i.e. under `/data/user/0/com.bilibeats.app/cache/...`, and the extension is only rewritten when the MIME type is known (`else if (extension != null) fileName = getBaseName(fileName) + extension;`). On macOS the path is the user's own file path.
findings.failure_scenario: A picked image whose name has no extension (a document-provider file with unknown MIME type on Android; `~/Pictures/cover` on macOS) gives `image.path.split('.').last == 'app/cache/<uuid>/cover'` (the last dot is in the package name) or the entire path. The destination becomes `.../bilibeat_covers/cover_1700000000000.app/cache/<uuid>/cover`, whose parent does not exist, `copy` throws, the catch returns null and the cover silently is not set -- no message to the listener (debugPrint is a no-op in release).
findings.fix: Take the extension from the basename only: `final name = image.name; final dot = name.lastIndexOf('.'); final ext = dot > 0 ? name.substring(dot + 1).replaceAll(RegExp(r'[^A-Za-z0-9]'), '') : 'img';` and show a snackbar when the copy fails.

find:sweep-security a39422.notes:
Method: grep over lib/ for http://, Uri.parse, HttpClient, Cookie, File(/Directory(, delete/rename/copy, debugPrint/print, MethodChannel, Random(, md5, image_picker, artUri, audioUrl, badCertificateCallback/HttpOverrides; then read each site. Partial reads (not in filesRead): database_service.dart (1-460, 800-901), lyrics_engine.dart (HTTP helper, NetEase cover), lyrics_store.dart (1-80), audio_player_handler.dart (media item + queue install), online_search_controller.dart, recommendations_controller.dart, playlist_page/track_info_sheet cover call sites. Plugin/SDK source checked: dart-sdk _http/http_impl.dart, audio_service 0.18.19 (Dart + AudioService.java), image_picker_android 0.8.13+19 FileUtils.java.

Found sound:
- Remote strings to file paths: Track ids are gated by AudioDownloadService.isSafeKey (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}$) before any download/delete path; only downloaded tracks reach audioPathForId. Cover cache names are md5 of the URL. Playlist ids used in cover file names are generated locally. Lyrics are keyed inside one JSON file, never a path. Titles, uploader names, tags, lyrics never reach a path.
- Track.audioUrl is persisted but nothing in lib/ ever sets it, so no stale/foreign URL is replayed from disk.
- Cookies: buvid3/buvid4 are in memory only, refreshed hourly, sent only to api.bilibili.com; dart:io strips Cookie/Authorization on cross-origin redirects (shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect). No cookie or identifier is written to disk or sent to NetEase/LRCLIB. Random() is used only for anti-bot filler and a fallback device id, not for anything needing unpredictability.
- TLS: no badCertificateCallback, HttpOverrides or proxy overrides; all hard-coded endpoints are https; Bilibili/NetEase image and stream URLs are upgraded from http to https before use. No iOS ATS exceptions.
- Logging: debugPrint is replaced by a no-op in release (main.dart:20); no bare print() in lib/. (audio_service itself prints artwork load errors; not app code.)
- Android manifest: allowBackup=false plus full data-extraction exclusions, no storage/media permissions, only INTERNET/WAKE_LOCK/FOREGROUND_SERVICE(_MEDIA_PLAYBACK)/POST_NOTIFICATIONS/VIBRATE/REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, all used. Exported AudioService/MediaButtonReceiver are the standard audio_service declarations; the handler exposes no browsable library. MethodChannel handler takes no arguments. All data is in app-private internal storage.
- Secrets: keystore and key.properties are gitignored, never present in git history (git log --all --diff-filter=A), and make_keystore.sh does not put passwords on the command line.
- macOS release entitlements: sandbox + network.client + user-selected files only.
- Stored data: search history is capped at 12 with a clear action; nothing beyond library, history, lyrics, prefs and session is stored.

Not determined: regex backtracking cost of the title-parsing patterns in lyrics_engine.dart on adversarial titles (not analysed); whether the iOS build is actually in use (affects the weight of the backup finding); the OOM threshold in the artwork finding depends on the device (the main-thread full-size decode and the unresized re-download are certain from source, the crash is only for very large photos).

findings.title: A file-write error during a download (disk full) makes `await sink.flush()` hang forever; the download never fails, stays in _inFlight/_tasks and cannot be retried until the process dies
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:534-547 `await for (final chunk in timeoutRes) { sink.add(chunk); ... } await sink.flush(); } finally { try { await sink.close(); } catch (_) {} }`. The sink is `part.openWrite()` (:502, :522), used through add(), never addStream().

Dart SDK, ~/flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/lib/io/io_sink.dart `_StreamSinkImpl._controller` getter: when the target's addStream fails while the sink is not bound, the onError branch only runs `_completeDoneError(error, stackTrace)`; `_controllerInstance` and `_controllerCompleter` are left set and the completer is never completed. `flush()` then does `_isBound = true; var future = _controllerCompleter!.future; _controllerInstance!.close(); return future.whenComplete(...)`, a future nobody completes. Later `sink.add(chunk)` calls go to a controller whose subscription was cancelled and are dropped silently, so the loop runs to the end of the body and then parks on flush; the `finally` with close() is never reached.

Callers: ensureDownloaded (:267-293) removes `_inFlight[id]` only in its `finally`, which never runs; `final existing = _inFlight[id]; if (existing != null) return existing;` hands the same hung future to every later request. DownloadManager.startDownload (download_manager.dart:115 `if (_tasks.containsKey(track.id)) return;`, :142-145 removal only in finally) keeps the task forever. The playback path, audio_player_handler.dart:606-618 `preparing.value = track; try { await AudioDownloadService.ensureDownloaded(track); ...`, never returns either.
findings.failure_scenario: Storage fills up while a song is downloading (ENOSPC on a write). The file consumer fails, the rest of the body is still pulled over the network and discarded, then the coroutine parks on flush(). The row's progress ring and the top-bar 'N downloading' count stay forever, nothing is recorded as failed, tapping download again is ignored, and 下载并播放 for that song shows 'preparing' until another song is chosen. Freeing space does not help; only killing the process does, and the process is long-lived because of the foreground media service. An unhandled async error from the sink's `done` future is also raised.
findings.fix: Do not rely on flush() after add(). Either write with `await sink.addStream(timeoutRes.map(...))` (counting progress in the map), which surfaces the write error, or race the loop against the sink's failure: attach `sink.done.catchError(...)` to a flag or Completer checked on each chunk, and replace `await sink.flush()` with `await sink.close()`, which returns `done` and completes with the error.

findings.title: A lyric lookup that fails for lack of a connection is remembered as 'no lyrics exist' for the whole session
findings.evidence:
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:178-189 `if (_misses.contains(track.id)) { publish(Lyrics.none); return; } ... final fresh = await LyricsEngine.autoFetchLyrics(...); if (fresh.isEmpty) _misses.add(track.id);`. `_misses` is documented at :46-48 as 'Songs the databases had nothing for, this session'.

autoFetchLyrics cannot tell failure from absence: lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:36-53 `_httpGet` catches every error and returns null (`} catch (e) { debugPrint('Lyrics HTTP error: $e'); } return null;`); fetchFromNetEase (:1908-1910) and fetchFromLRCLIB (:1841-1843) skip a null body; autoFetchLyrics (:2165) then returns `Lyrics(source: 'none', ... lines: const [])`.

`_misses` is only cleared by choose (:83), rematch (:104) or a name change (:134). TrackNaming treats the same situation correctly (track_naming.dart:155-158 'Offline is not "unknown": ask again the next time it plays').
findings.failure_scenario: The listener plays newly downloaded songs with no connection (underground, flight mode, a NetEase timeout). Playing from local files offline is the app's core use. Each song shows no lyrics and its id goes into `_misses`. Back online, replaying those songs still shows no lyrics, with no request made, until the app process is restarted (which can be days with the foreground service) or the listener opens the lyrics sheet and taps 重新匹配 for each song.
findings.fix: Have the lookup report failure separately from 'not found' (for example `_httpGet` rethrows, or autoFetchLyrics returns a result carrying a `failed` flag when any request errored and nothing was found) and add to `_misses` only on a completed, empty answer.

findings.title: Auto-naming jobs already queued still rename songs after 自动匹配歌曲信息 is switched off
findings.evidence: lib/services/track_naming.dart:100-106 `static void autoName(Track track) { if (!enabled || _settled(track) || !_attempted.add(track.id)) return; _queue = _queue.then((_) => _name(track))...` checks `enabled` only when the job is queued. `_name` (:119-197) never re-reads `enabled`: it starts `final before = await _stored(track.id); if (before == null || _settled(before)) return;` and ends in `await _save(stored.copyWith(title: found.title, uploader: found.artist, coverUrl: found.coverUrl, named: true, ...))`. setEnabled (:48-51) only flips the flag and writes the pref. The queue is serial and each job makes several network lookups with 10 s timeouts, so jobs pile up: one per track change (init listener :42-45) and one per new download (library_controller.dart:202-204).
findings.failure_scenario: The listener skips through a dozen un-named downloads, sees a song renamed wrongly, opens 设置 and turns 自动匹配歌曲信息 off. The lookups still queued (and the one in flight) complete over the next seconds to minutes and rewrite the title, artist and cover of those songs anyway, with the switch showing off.
findings.fix: Re-check `enabled` at the top of `_name` and again just before each `_save` (returning after `_attempted.remove(track.id)` so the song is reconsidered if the setting is turned back on).

findings.title: play() arriving while restoreSession is in flight is silently dropped
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:689-692 `Future<void> restoreSession() async { if (_restoreStarted) return; _restoreStarted = true; if (_player.audioSources.isNotEmpty) return;`. A second caller returns immediately instead of waiting for the first.

:750-756 `Future<void> play() async { ... if (_player.audioSources.isEmpty) { // A media button can cold-start the service before the UI restores. await restoreSession(); if (_player.audioSources.isEmpty) return; }`.

lib/main.dart:58 `unawaited(handler.restoreSession());` starts the restore right after AudioService.init; it then awaits the session file, the whole library load (compute isolate) and setAudioSources, typically hundreds of milliseconds. I traced audio_service 0.18.19: a click queued before init is flushed inside `configure` (AudioServicePlugin.java:501 invokePendingMethods) and, by microtask order, reaches play() before main's own call, so that single case works. Any play that arrives after main's call but before the restore lands takes the early-return path.
findings.failure_scenario: The process is cold-started (launcher, or a headset/car media button) and a play command (second headset press, lock-screen or Bluetooth play) arrives while the restore started by main() is still loading the library. play() calls restoreSession(), which returns at once because `_restoreStarted` is true, sees an empty queue and returns. The press does nothing and has to be repeated after the restore finishes.
findings.fix: Keep the restore as a future: `Future<void>? _restore; Future<void> restoreSession() => _restore ??= _doRestore();` so play() really awaits the in-flight restore.

findings.title: stop() / swipe-away does not cancel a pending 下载并播放: playback starts later with the service stopped
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:634-657 playTrack: `final token = ++_selection; ... if (!await _ensureLocal(track, token)) return; ... await _install(tracks, start, token: token);` and _install :590 `if (autoplay) _startPlayback();`. The only thing that supersedes a pending request is another `++_selection`.

stop() (:775-784) and onTaskRemoved (:787-791 `if (!_player.playing) await stop();`) do not touch `_selection` or `preparing`: `_resumeAfterInterruption = false; _idleTimer?.cancel(); _progressSaveTimer?.cancel(); _clearSleepTimer(); await saveSession(); await _player.stop(); _broadcastState(); await super.stop();`. The class comment (:38-42) explains that starting the foreground service from the background is what Android 12+ answers by killing the process, and stop() carefully clears `_resumeAfterInterruption` for that reason, but leaves this path open.
findings.failure_scenario: Nothing is playing (or playback is paused). The listener taps 下载并播放 on a search result, then swipes the app out of recents while the download is still running. onTaskRemoved calls stop() and the service ends, but the process and the download live on. When the file lands, _install replaces the queue and calls _player.play(): either music starts from an app the listener just dismissed, or on Android 12+ the foreground-service start from the background is refused and the process is killed.
findings.fix: In stop() bump `_selection` and clear `preparing.value` (as playTrack/playCollection do), so a download that finishes afterwards is kept in the library but not played.

findings.title: With 随机播放 on, the 30-minute idle stop (and any playback error) reshuffles the queue
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:334-338 `_idleTimer = Timer(_idleStopAfter, () { if (!_player.playing) unawaited(stop()); });` and stop() :781 `await _player.stop();`.

just_audio 0.10.6 lib/just_audio.dart: stop() calls `_setPlatformActive(false)` (:1168-1169); `_setPlatformActive` always ends in `await _load(platform, _playlist, initialSeekValues: ...)` for the idle platform as well as the native one (~:1750-1757); `_load` does `source._shuffle(initialIndex: initialSeekValues?.index ?? 0); await _broadcastSequence();` (:1009-1010); DefaultShuffleOrder.shuffle (:3969-3981) is `indices.shuffle(_random)` followed by swapping the initial index to position 0. The same happens again when play() re-activates the platform, and whenever the native player goes idle after an error (:1594-1598).

The new order reaches the UI through `_player.sequenceStateStream.listen((_) => _publish())` (handler :187) because `_order` (:178-180) reads `state.shuffleIndices`.
findings.failure_scenario: Shuffle is on and the listener is at song 12 of 40. They pause for more than 30 minutes (service stopped by the idle timer) and resume. The queue sheet now shows '1 / 40' with a new random order; 上一首 no longer goes back to the song that was played before, and songs already heard come round again. Likewise after one unplayable file is skipped.
findings.fix: Use a ShuffleOrder whose shuffle() is a no-op unless explicitly requested (pass `shuffleOrder:` to setAudioSources and call a dedicated reshuffle only from setShuffle(true) / playCollection), or capture `_player.shuffleIndices` before stop() and restore that order after re-activation.

findings.title: Paging a direct BV/av/short-link search never reaches an end: every scroll near the bottom re-requests the same video
findings.evidence:
lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:467-470 `final directId = extractBvOrAvId(query); if (directId != null) { final direct = await fetchVideoInfo(directId); if (direct.isNotEmpty) return direct; }` ignores `page`, so page 2, 3, ... return the same parts.

lib/state/online_search_controller.dart:109-119 `final results = await BilibiliSdk.search(_query, page: page); ... _results = [..._results, for (final t in results) if (_seen.add(t.id)) t]; _page = page; _loadMoreFailed = false; // Only an empty page proves the end; a page of duplicates does not. if (results.isEmpty) _reachedEnd = true;`. All duplicates, so nothing is added and `_reachedEnd` stays false.

lib/screens/search_view.dart:72-82 `_onScroll` calls `_online.loadMore()` on every ScrollNotification with `metrics.pixels >= metrics.maxScrollExtent - 320`; the only guard is `_loadingMore`, which clears when each request returns.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener pastes the BV number (or a b23.tv share link) of a multi-part video such as a concert or album with 20+ parts, so the result list scrolls. Whenever the list is within 320 px of the bottom, each scroll update fires another `view` request (plus the short-link resolve and a signed retry when refused); the spinner row flickers in and out and requests keep going for as long as the listener scrolls there. No new rows ever appear, and the burst of identical requests invites Bilibili's risk control (412), which then also affects downloads and matching.
findings.fix: Mark the end when a page adds nothing new for an id query: in loadMore, compute the added rows and set `_reachedEnd = true` when `added.isEmpty` and the query is a direct id or link (or have BilibiliSdk.search return [] for `page > 1` on the direct-id and short-link paths).

findings.title: The song sheet favourites the caller's stale Track copy, so a named song is stored in 收藏 under its raw video title
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:102-105 `Future<void> _toggleFavorite() async { Haptics.light(); await DatabaseService.toggleFavorite(widget.track); }` uses `widget.track`, while the same sheet knows it may be stale and renders and adds to playlists through `_latest()` (:236-243 'The library's copy carries any edits made since the sheet's caller captured its [Track]'; :121 `final track = _latest();`; :188 `PlaylistPicker.show(parent, [track])`).

DatabaseService.toggleFavorite (database_service.dart:736) does `favorites.tracks.insert(0, track)` with whatever copy it is given. Bilibili search rows pass raw API results: search_view.dart:249 `_songs(_online.results)` builds `SongTile(track: track, ...)`, and song_tile.dart:57/147 opens `TrackSheet.show(context, track, queue: queue)`. A favourite copy is only corrected by a later updateTrackMetadata for that id (database_service.dart:532-537), which never comes for a song the matcher has already settled (track_naming.dart:95-96, :101).
findings.failure_scenario: A song is downloaded and already named (auto-matched or edited). The listener later finds the same video in a Bilibili search, opens its sheet (the header correctly shows the song name and artist via _latest()) and taps the heart. 收藏 now holds the raw search copy: the list row shows the long video title and the UP主 as artist, `named` is false, and it stays that way since nothing re-names a settled song. The library row and the favourites row of the same song disagree.
findings.fix: `await DatabaseService.toggleFavorite(_latest());`, the same copy the sheet already uses for 加入歌单 and 编辑信息.

find:sweep-async a34172.notes:
Method: grep over lib/ for unawaited, .then(, Future.wait, Timer, StreamSubscription, .listen(, addListener, Completer, compute(, .timeout(, mounted and WidgetsBindingObserver, then read each site. Read in part only: now_playing_page (1-330, 425-445), playlist_page (60-410), lyrics_sheet (1-180), lyrics_view (40-190), marquee_text (75-298), search_view (1-300), home_page (40-100), song_tile (40-110), playback_queue_sheet (20-109), sheet.dart (227-286), wbi_signer (90-183), bilibili_sdk (1-300, 460-510), recommendation_engine (150-216), lyrics_engine (20-75, 1831-1845, 1896-1936, 2140-2168). Plugin behaviour was checked in just_audio 0.10.6, audio_service 0.18.19 and dart:io io_sink.dart. Nothing was run and no file was modified. An earlier pass left docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md; I only read its first two entries, and its #2 is the same flush hang as my first finding, which I re-verified independently against the SDK source.

Found sound:
- Write lock (DatabaseService._writeJsonAtomically): FIFO chain whose completer is always completed in `finally`, no await that depends on another lock holder, unique tmp per call. Every JSON store goes through it (LyricsStore via writeStoreFile); sidecar metadata and part notes are separate files with their own tmp+rename. No lock cycles between DatabaseService._ensureLoaded, LyricsStore._ensureLoaded and AudioDownloadService.
- _loadPrefs concurrent first calls (`_prefs ??=` plus the set-aside guard), LyricsStore pin/clear before load (_clearedBeforeLoad, revisions), and putAutomatic vs pin.
- Handler queue installation: the _selection token is checked after every await; overlapping installs are resolved by just_audio's PlayerInterruptedException plus the _installing counter; the try/finally keeps _installing balanced; restore vs playTrack is guarded by the token in both orders.
- removeTracks: each event carries one id and the just_audio playlist mutation runs synchronously when its lock is free, so overlapping calls do not remove the wrong index. The only stale-index window is a delete landing during the few ms of a queue install, which I judged not realistic.
- _skip/_navTarget under rapid presses; holdAutoAdvance release on every path of _openLyricsSheet and in dispose; sleep-timer timers and subscription are cleared on fire, stop and re-set; interruption resume is cancelled by pause(), stop() and becomingNoisy.
- Position survives stop(): the idle platform is loaded with the current index and position.
- LyricsController generation/revision guards (A→B→A, choose during lookup, rematch); the OnlineSearchController and RecommendationsController token guards; TrackNaming re-reads the stored track after the lookup and aborts on listener edits.
- Widget lifecycles: every StreamSubscription, listener and Timer I enumerated (AppShell, NowPlayingPage, LyricsView, MarqueeText, TrackSheet, TrackDownloadButton, DownloadManagementSheet, SettingsSheet) is cancelled or removed in dispose, and async continuations check `mounted` or a token. LibraryController, DownloadManager and the handler's player subscriptions are process-lifetime singletons.
- CachedCoverImage in-flight dedupe and its addStream-based write, which reports errors (unlike the audio download path).
- MainActivity channel handlers always reply.

Seen but not reported (too narrow, or harmless in release builds):
- promptForText disposes its TextEditingController as soon as showDialog completes, while the dialog is still animating out. This is a debug-only assertion.
- TrackInfoSheet saves from the Track snapshot taken when it opened, so a loudness backfill that lands while the sheet is open is overwritten until the next launch.
- Rapid double-tap on the play-mode button within one platform round trip can leave native loop-one under shuffle.
- A playCollection(shuffle) superseded mid-install leaves shuffle enabled for the request that superseded it.
- After a single-track playback error the player is idle, so no idle timer is armed and the paused foreground notification lingers.

Could not determine from source alone: iOS AVQueuePlayer behaviour when the current item is removed, and how long a cached Android process keeps downloading after task removal (this bears on the stop()/pending-play finding, hence its 0.5 confidence).

findings.title: A lyrics lookup that fails for lack of a connection is recorded as "no lyrics exist" for the rest of the session
findings.evidence: lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:184-189 `final fresh = await LyricsEngine.autoFetchLyrics(...); if (fresh.isEmpty) _misses.add(track.id);` and :178-181 `if (_misses.contains(track.id)) { publish(Lyrics.none); return; }`. autoFetchLyrics (lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart ~2140-2167) returns `Lyrics(source: 'none', ... lines: const [])` both when the providers have nothing and when every request failed: fetchFromNetEase/fetchFromLRCLIB only see `_httpGet` returning null (lyrics_engine.dart:37-53 swallows every transport error and non-200) and return null. `_misses` is only cleared by rematch(), choose(), or a metadata edit (lyrics_controller.dart:83,104,134). TrackNaming already distinguishes the two cases (track_naming.dart:155-158 `// Offline is not "unknown": ask again the next time it plays.`); lyrics do not.
findings.failure_scenario: Songs always play from local files, so offline listening is normal. Play a song with no cached lyrics while offline (subway, flight mode), or while NetEase times out: the view shows no lyrics and the id goes into _misses. Connection returns; the song comes round again (loop/all, or tapped again). _load hits the _misses branch and publishes empty without any request. Because the foreground service keeps the process alive for days, the song stays lyric-less until the listener opens the lyrics sheet and taps 重新匹配 or kills the app.
findings.fix: Have autoFetchLyrics (or the two fetchers) report "could not ask" separately from "asked, nothing found" (e.g. return null / a flag when every _httpGet returned null), and only add to _misses in the second case.

findings.title: Paging a BV-number / link search re-fetches the same video forever; the end of the list is never reached
findings.evidence: lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:460-471 `static Future<List<Track>> search(String query, {int page = 1}) ... final directId = extractBvOrAvId(query); if (directId != null) { final direct = await fetchVideoInfo(directId); if (direct.isNotEmpty) return direct; }` - `page` is ignored on the direct path (same for the b23.tv path at :474-483). lib/state/online_search_controller.dart:109-119 `final results = await BilibiliSdk.search(_query, page: page); ... _page = page; _loadMoreFailed = false; // Only an empty page proves the end; a page of duplicates does not. if (results.isEmpty) _reachedEnd = true;` - a direct result is never empty, so _reachedEnd never becomes true and there is no back-off on success. lib/screens/search_view.dart:72-81 calls `_online.loadMore()` on every ScrollNotification within 320 px of the bottom.
findings.failure_scenario: Paste the BV number (or share link) of a multi-part video - an album or concert with 15+ parts, the case the app explicitly supports. The parts list is scrollable; whenever the list is within 320 px of the end every scroll event starts another `x/web-interface/view` request as soon as the previous one finishes, each returning the same parts (all dropped by _seen). The bottom spinner flickers in and out indefinitely (its insertion/removal changes the scroll extent, which itself generates further scroll updates while the user rests at the bottom), and the burst of identical requests is exactly what trips Bilibili risk control (412) for the following real searches and downloads.
findings.fix: In search(), return [] for page > 1 when the query resolved to a direct id / short link (or return a flag meaning "complete"); in OnlineSearchController.loadMore also set _reachedEnd when a page adds no new ids.

findings.title: Any non-zero Bilibili API code other than -352/412 is read as "no results" / "no such video" instead of a failure
findings.evidence: lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:571-583 in _searchOnce: `final data = json['data']; final dynamic rawResult = data is Map ? data['result'] : null; ... if (resultsList != null) {...} return [];` - `json['code']` is never inspected. The only code check is isRiskControlled (:637-645) `if (code == -352 || code == 412) return true;` (Bilibili's documented block code is negative, -412). So in :535-543 a primary answer such as `{"code":-403,...}` or `{"code":-799,"message":"请求过于频繁"}` is kept as `body` (the unsigned fallback at :545-550 is not tried) and yields []. Same in _tracksOfView (:195, :240) `if (json['code'] == 0 && json['data'] != null) {...} return [];` and _viewBody (:143) `if (plain != null && !isRiskControlled(plain)) return plain;`. The stale-key path makes this reachable: lib/services/wbi_signer.dart:138-141,180-181 hands out the hard-coded `_fallbackKeys` for 2 minutes after one failed `nav` fetch, and the comment at :175-177 says such signatures are rejected by the API.
findings.failure_scenario: The `nav` request for WBI keys times out once (weak signal at launch). For the next two minutes every signed search is signed with the static 2023 key pair; Bilibili answers HTTP 200 with a non-zero code and no data. _searchOnce returns [] for the music zone, search() then tries unfiltered, also []. The UI shows "没有找到，换个关键词或粘贴 BV 号试试" (search_view.dart:239-247) rather than "无法连接哔哩哔哩" with 重试, and the plain fallback endpoint that needs no signature is never used. The same happens under rate limiting (-799): a pasted BV number is reported as not existing and is then keyword-searched as text.
findings.fix: In _searchOnce treat `json['code'] != 0` on the primary as a reason to use the fallback URL, and on the final body throw BiliApiException; add -412/-403/-799 handling. In _tracksOfView return [] only for the known "video missing" codes (-404, 62002, 62004 ...) and throw for the rest.

findings.title: Library/playlist persist failures are swallowed, so edits made while storage is full report success and vanish on restart
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:473-486 `static Future<void> _persistPlaylists() async { try { ... await _writeJsonAtomically(...); } catch (e) { debugPrint('DatabaseService _persistPlaylists error: $e'); } if (!_libraryUpdateController.isClosed) _libraryUpdateController.add(null); }`; identical catch-and-log in _persistDownloaded (:453-461), _persistRecentlyPlayed (:463-471), setPref (:836-843). debugPrint is a no-op in release (lib/main.dart:20). _writeJsonAtomically itself rethrows (:389-391), so the information is available and dropped one level up. The caller that expects it: lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:99-107 `try { await DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata(updated); ... if (mounted) Navigator.pop(context); } catch (error, stack) { ... showAppSnackBar(..., message: '保存失败，请重试'); }` - that catch can never fire. Contrast lib/services/lyrics_store.dart:110-115 / lyrics_sheet.dart:89-96, where the failure does propagate ("歌词已应用，但未能保存").
findings.failure_scenario: The phone's storage fills up - likely for an app whose job is downloading audio (a download that hits ENOSPC is the usual way to get there). The listener then creates a playlist, adds 30 songs, favourites a few, and corrects a song's title in 编辑信息. Every `tmp.writeAsString` throws ENOSPC; each is caught and discarded; the UI updates from memory, the sheet closes, "已加入「…」" is shown. When the process is next killed (30-minute idle stop, OEM task killer) all of it is gone with no indication anything was wrong.
findings.fix: Let the _persist* helpers rethrow (or return bool) and surface one toast (e.g. via a DatabaseService error stream listened to in AppShell) such as "存储空间不足，更改未保存"; keep the swallow only for the fire-and-forget callers at startup.

findings.title: Partial downloads (.part) of failed downloads are never cleaned up once the session's failure record is gone
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:354-360 `} catch (e) { // Deliberately keep the .part file: the next attempt resumes it ... _emit(...); rethrow; }`. The only code that deletes a `.part` is delete(track) (:229-235), reached only through DatabaseService.removeDownloadedTrack (database_service.dart:779-781), which the UI offers only for downloaded tracks (track_sheet.dart:222-228 `if (downloaded) SheetAction(... '删除下载')`, download_management_sheet.dart:160-170 iterates `_downloaded`). Failure records are session-only: lib/services/download_manager.dart:58-61 `Never persisted`, and playback-path failures are never recorded at all (:26-28). storageBreakdown (:191-214) counts only `.m4a` with a `.ready`, so the bytes are invisible in 下载管理. `grep -rn "\.part" lib` shows no startup sweep. The same directory also keeps the `audio_<id>.json` written before the download starts (:275).
findings.failure_scenario: Tap 下载并播放 on a two-hour concert (150 MB+). The connection drops at 80 % (`CDN chunk timeout` / `下载不完整`). The listener picks something else, or the app is restarted. ~120 MB of `audio_<id>.m4a.part` now sits in Documents/bilibeat_audio permanently: nothing lists it, nothing counts it, nothing deletes it unless that exact video is downloaded again to completion. Repeated on a flaky network this silently eats storage - and when the failure was itself ENOSPC, the leftover keeps the disk full.
findings.fix: At startup (in _discoverAudioFiles or a small sweep in AudioDownloadService) delete `*.part` / `*.part.json` (and `.json` without `.ready`) older than a few days and not in _inFlight; also delete the part on DownloadManager.dismissFailed.

findings.title: A failed user-initiated download gives no feedback: DownloadManager.errors has no listener and the failure badge is hidden in search
findings.evidence: lib/services/download_manager.dart:69-72 `/// Emits a human-readable message when a user-initiated download fails — without this a failure was indistinguishable from a success (the ring simply disappeared). Stream<String> get errors => _errorController.stream;` and :141 `_errorController.add('$e')`. `grep -rn errors lib` returns only that declaration - nothing subscribes. The only other indicator is _DownloadsButton, which lib/app/app_shell.dart:211-218 renders only when not searching: `if (_searchActive) TextButton(... '取消') else ...[ const _DownloadsButton(), ...]`. TrackSheet (track_sheet.dart:253-280) and TrackDownloadButton simply fall back to the idle 下载 state.
findings.failure_scenario: In search results (where every download starts) open a song's sheet and tap 下载 while Bilibili refuses the playurl request or the CDN returns 403. The button shows 0 % briefly and reverts to "下载并播放 / 下载" with no toast and no badge; it looks as if the tap was ignored. The red error icon only becomes visible after leaving search. (If the stream were wired up as is, it would show raw text such as `Exception: CDN HTTP 403` or a FileSystemException with the full path.)
findings.fix: Listen to DownloadManager.errors in AppShell next to handler.messages and show a fixed message like "「<title>」下载失败" (emit the track, not `'$e'`).

findings.title: When the music-zone results run out, later pages silently switch to the unfiltered search
findings.evidence: lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:494-501 `musical = await _searchOnce(query, musicOnly: true, page: page); ... if (musical != null && musical.isNotEmpty) return musical; return _searchOnce(query, musicOnly: false, page: page);` - the empty-zone fallback is applied to every page, not only page 1. OnlineSearchController.loadMore (online_search_controller.dart:109-119) appends whatever comes back and ends only on an empty page.
findings.failure_scenario: Search a song whose music-zone results span 3 pages. Scrolling to the end requests page 4: the music zone returns nothing (end reached), so page 4 of the all-zones search is appended instead - gameplay, vlogs, lectures - and scrolling continues through unfiltered pages 5, 6 ... (while unfiltered pages 1-3 were never shown). The comment at :522-523 says exactly these results are noise for a music player.
findings.fix: Only fall back to the unfiltered search when page == 1 (and remember per query which mode page 1 used, so later pages stay in that mode).

findings.title: A response rejected as too small (<1024 bytes) is accepted as a finished download on the next attempt via the 416 path
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:555-557 `if (received < 1024) { throw Exception('音频文件异常 ($received 字节)'); }` runs after the body has been written to `.part` and the note `{'total': total, 'validator': ...}` saved (:511-517); the catch at :354-359 keeps both. Next attempt, :424-441 sends `Range: bytes=<existing>-`; :451-456 `if (res.statusCode == HttpStatus.requestedRangeNotSatisfiable && existing > 0) { await res.drain<void>(); if (known?.total == existing) { return (received: existing, total: existing); }` returns success without the size check, and _download (:319-353) renames it to `.m4a`, writes `.ready` and registers the track.
findings.failure_scenario: The CDN answers 200 with a small non-text body and a Content-Length (e.g. a 300-byte stub served as application/octet-stream for a restricted part). First attempt: fails with 音频文件异常, as designed. The listener taps 重试 (or taps the song again): the same resource answers the Range request with 416, the 300-byte file is marked downloaded, appears in the library, and can never play ("有歌曲无法播放，已跳过") until manually deleted.
findings.fix: Discard the part (and note) before throwing the `<1024` error, or apply the same minimum-size check in the 416 branch.

findings.title: play() during an in-flight session restore is a silent no-op
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:689-692 `Future<void> restoreSession() async { if (_restoreStarted) return; _restoreStarted = true; ...` followed by awaits on loadPlaybackSession, _library() (full DB load + isolate parse + directory scan) and setAudioSources. :750-756 `Future<void> play() async { ... if (_player.audioSources.isEmpty) { // A media button can cold-start the service before the UI restores. await restoreSession(); if (_player.audioSources.isEmpty) return; }`. lib/main.dart:58 starts the restore unawaited immediately after AudioService.init, so by the time any play() is dispatched `_restoreStarted` is already true and the second call returns at once instead of waiting.
findings.failure_scenario: Process is started by (or just before) a headset / Bluetooth / lock-screen play press - the case the comment names. main() has already called restoreSession(); play() calls it again, gets an immediate return, sees an empty source list and returns. Nothing plays and nothing is shown; a second press a moment later works.
findings.fix: Keep the restore as a future (`Future<void>? _restore; Future<void> restoreSession() => _restore ??= _doRestore();`) so play() awaits the in-flight restore.

findings.title: Any exception while loading a store - not only a parse failure - sets the healthy file aside and starts empty
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:308-324 `try { final file = File(path); if (!await file.exists()) return; final playlists = await compute(_parsePlaylistList, await file.readAsString()); ... } catch (e) { debugPrint(...); await _setAside(path); }` (same shape in _loadTracks :198-211, _loadSearchHistory :327-340, _loadPrefs :812-823, and lib/services/lyrics_store.dart:62-79). The catch covers `readAsString` IO errors and `compute` (isolate spawn) failures as well as FormatException. _setAside (:437-451) renames the file to `.unreadable`; `grep -rn unreadable lib` shows nothing ever reads such a file back, and after the rename _loadFuture stays completed, so the next persist writes a fresh file from the empty in-memory store.
findings.failure_scenario: On a launch under memory pressure the isolate for `compute` cannot be spawned (or the read hits a transient EIO). bilibeat_playlists.json - perfectly valid - is renamed to bilibeat_playlists.json.unreadable; the app shows no playlists and no favourites, and the first favourite toggle writes a new one-entry file. For bilibeat_lyrics.json the same path hides every pinned / hand-calibrated lyric. The data is still on disk but the app offers no way back to it.
findings.fix: Set aside only on FormatException / TypeError from the parse (decode on the main isolate as a fallback when compute throws); on IO or isolate errors leave the file alone and reset _loadFuture so the load is retried, refusing to persist that store meanwhile.

findings.title: 匹配 in 编辑信息 reports "没有匹配到这首歌" when the lookup merely failed, and its spinner has no finally
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:59-68 `setState(() => _identifying = true); final found = await TrackNaming.identify(widget.track); if (!mounted) return; setState(() => _identifying = false); if (found == null) { showAppSnackBar(..., message: '没有匹配到这首歌'); return; }`. LyricsEngine.identify returns null for "offline" as well (lyrics_engine.dart ~823 `// Offline is not an answer: ask again next time. if (who.incomplete) return null;`, ~1235 `if (incomplete && !bestExact) return null;`), and TrackNaming._name needs LyricsEngine.identitySettled to tell the two apart (track_naming.dart:148-159) - the sheet does not use it. There is no try/finally around the await, and identify contains unguarded casts on NetEase data (lyrics_engine.dart:957 `((song['name'] ?? '') as String)`, :992 `song['duration'] as num?`); `onTap: _identifying ? null : _identify` (:172).
findings.failure_scenario: Offline (or NetEase timing out), tap 匹配: after up to ~20 s the toast says the song was not matched, which reads as "the catalogue does not know it" - the listener types the name by hand, marking the track matcher 0 so automatic matching never revisits it. If identify throws on an unexpected NetEase field, _identifying stays true: the spinner turns forever and 匹配 is disabled until the sheet is reopened.
findings.fix: Wrap in try/finally; when found == null and !LyricsEngine.identitySettled(...) (or on catch) show "无法连接，请稍后再试" instead.

findings.title: Recommendation paging has no failure back-off and treats a fully filtered page as the end
findings.evidence: lib/state/recommendations_controller.dart:80-86 `if (tracks.isEmpty) _reachedEnd = true; } catch (e) { debugPrint(...); if (pass != _pass) return; } _loadingMore = false; notifyListeners();` - on failure nothing is recorded (compare OnlineSearchController's `_loadMoreFailed`/`_lastFailure` 3 s window, online_search_controller.dart:98-101,123-124), and search_view.dart:77-78 calls `_recs.loadMore()` on every scroll notification near the bottom. RecommendationEngine.recommend (recommendation_engine.dart:199-214) returns only candidates that pass isSongLength / knownIds / excludeIds, so a page whose results are all long-form, owned or already shown comes back empty.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Scroll 为你推荐 to the bottom, then lose the connection: every further scroll event launches a fresh batch of up to four seed searches (each a signed request plus fallback, twice for music/unfiltered), all failing, with only a flickering spinner - no retry affordance and no pause. (b) Online: page 3 of every seed happens to contain only videos longer than 6 minutes or already in the library; recommend returns [] and the list ends for good although pages 4+ exist, until 换一批 is tapped.
findings.fix: Mirror the search controller: remember the failure time and skip loadMore for a few seconds (and show 重试); have recommend() report whether any seed returned raw results, and set _reachedEnd only when none did.

find:sweep-resilience afbf48.notes:
Method: grep-enumerated IO / network / parse / indexing sites across lib/, then read each service, controller and async UI flow. lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart was read only in its network, identity-result, LRC and provider sections (lines ~10-60, 560-665, 815-1010, 1095-1115, 1225-1245, 1500-1670, 1760-2168), not the title parser; now_playing_page, home_page, playlist_page, lyrics_view and mini_player were read only around their async/index sites. Nothing was run, no network requests were made, no files changed.

Confidence caveats: finding 3 depends on Bilibili answering HTTP 200 with a non-zero code for bad signatures / rate limits (consistent with the code's own comments, not verified live). Finding 2's "self-sustaining at rest" part is inferred from Flutter scroll behaviour; the per-scroll-event refetch and the never-reached end are certain from the code. Finding 9's cold-start ordering inside audio_service was not fully traced; the in-flight no-op itself is certain. Finding 8 and 10 need rare server / OS conditions.

Checked and found sound:
- Download transfer: connect/response/chunk timeouts, non-200, text/JSON bodies, truncated bodies, unsolicited 206, If-Range/validator resume, disk-full (surfaces at flush, fails the download, user sees only the fixed 下载失败 text - raw exception text is stored in FailedDownload.error but never displayed), concurrent dedupe via _inFlight, unsafe ids rejected before becoming paths.
- preparing is always cleared (finally + token check); a superseded request cannot clear a newer one's state. _install handles PlayerInterruptedException and failures; empty library / empty collection / no downloaded items are guarded; Random().nextInt is guarded; removeTracks on the last item stops cleanly; saveSession never overwrites with an empty queue; PlaybackSession.fromMap tolerates malformed data.
- _writeJsonAtomically: single lock, unique temp, cleanup in finally, lock always released; newer-schema and corrupt files are set aside rather than overwritten; per-item try/catch when parsing tracks/playlists/lyrics; Track.fromMap tolerates wrong types.
- Search controller: tokens prevent stale writes, generic catch covers TypeErrors from the unguarded `as String?` casts in _searchOnce, loading flags are always reset. Duration parsing uses tryParse. fetchAudioStream / fetchVideoHints / _recognisedMusic / WbiSigner / FingerprintService catch everything and degrade.
- parseLrc int.parse calls are regex-guarded; LyricsView index math is guarded for empty/unsynced lyrics; PlayerSeekBar handles zero duration; formatBytes/formatDuration handle 0; gainFor is clamped and NaN cannot enter via JSON.
- CachedCoverImage: timeouts, .part + rename, in-flight dedupe, zero-length guard, errorBuilder fallback. (A cover that failed while offline is not retried until the widget is recreated - cosmetic, not reported.)
- TrackNaming distinguishes offline from unknown and re-checks the stored track before writing; found.coverUrl null keeps the existing cover.
- Not reported as speculative: performance with ~5000 tracks (whole-library queue reinstall on each tap, TrackCredit cache of 2000 thrashing under LocalSearch), and unbounded IOSink buffering during very large downloads.

findings.title: Lock-screen/notification artwork is fetched and decoded at original resolution for every song (no CDN sizing, no artDownscale)
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:391-397 `artUri: track.coverUrl.isEmpty ? null : Uri.tryParse(track.coverUrl.startsWith('/') ? 'file://${track.coverUrl}' : track.coverUrl,)` - the raw cover URL, not CachedCoverImage.sizedUrl. Sources of coverUrl are originals: bilibili_sdk.dart:199/595 (`data['pic']`, `item['pic']`), lyrics_engine.dart:1612-1618 (NetEase `album.picUrl` returned unparameterised), utils/cover_picker.dart:11-19 (gallery file copied as-is, no maxWidth).
lib/main.dart:41-51 `config: const AudioServiceConfig(androidNotificationChannelId: ..., androidNotificationChannelName: 'BiliBeats', androidStopForegroundOnPause: false)` - artDownscaleWidth/Height are not set.
Plugin (audio_service-0.18.19): lib/audio_service.dart:1031-1090 the mediaItem listener calls `_loadArtwork` -> :1251-1253 `cacheManager.getSingleFile(mediaItem.artUri!.toString())` (DefaultCacheManager, a second cover cache beside bilibeat_covers) for any non-file artUri; AudioService.java:218-236 only sub-samples `if (config.artDownscaleWidth != -1)`, otherwise `BitmapFactory.decodeFile(artUri.getPath())` at full size; :242 `artBitmapCache.put(...)` into an LruCache sized `maxMemory / 8` (:332-336); :809-813 puts that bitmap into the metadata twice (ALBUM_ART and DISPLAY_ICON).
Contrast lib/main.dart:22-27, which deliberately caps Flutter's own image cache at 40 MB / 150 entries because 'A large cache is what gets a backgrounded app killed first under memory pressure'.
findings.failure_scenario: Play through a playlist on mobile data.
