For each song not played recently, audio_service downloads the full original cover (Bilibili video covers are typically 1920x1080 and a few hundred KB; NetEase album originals applied by auto-matching are commonly 1-3 MB and can be thousands of pixels square), although the app already holds a size-matched thumbnail of the same cover. Android then decodes it unscaled: 1920x1080 is ~8 MB of bitmap, a 3000x3000 album cover ~36 MB, a 12 MP photo picked as a custom cover ~48 MB, retained in a native LruCache of up to 1/8 of the heap for the life of the service. A bitmap larger than that cache is never retained, so it is re-decoded on every mediaItem update (track start, the duration update in _onDuration, every metadata edit). Net effect: megabytes of avoidable data per listening session for an app whose audio is fully offline, and tens of MB of extra memory in exactly the backgrounded state the Dart-side cache limit was meant to protect. Sizes are derived from the code paths and typical cover sizes, not measured.
findings.fix: Set `artDownscaleWidth: 512, artDownscaleHeight: 512` in AudioServiceConfig (main.dart), and build artUri from `CachedCoverImage.sizedUrl(track.coverUrl, 512, 512)` for remote covers (or, better, point it at the already cached thumbnail file with a file:// URI so no second download happens).

findings.title: Each keyboard open/close orphans a just_audio position stream: one more periodic timer and player-event listener for the life of the process
findings.evidence:
lib/app/app_shell.dart:120 `final keyboardOpen = MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom > 0;` and :149 `if (!keyboardOpen) const DockedPlayer(),` - the mini player is removed from the tree whenever the keyboard is up.
lib/widgets/mini_player.dart:274-276 `return StreamBuilder<Duration>(stream: handler.positionStream, initialData: handler.position,` is, on the home screen, the only subscriber of the position stream (the other two are now_playing_page.dart:103 and the end-of-track sleep timer, audio_player_handler.dart:964).
just_audio-0.10.6 lib/just_audio.dart:693-704: `_positionSubject = BehaviorSubject<Duration>(onCancel: () => _positionSubject = null); ... _positionSubject!.addStream(createPositionStream(...))`. When the last listener cancels, the subject is dropped but never closed, and the stream it was fed from is never cancelled: createPositionStream (:716-763) only tears down inside yieldPosition `if (controller.isClosed || _durationSubject.isClosed)`, which never becomes true for an orphan. Its `playerEventSubscription = playerEventStream.listen((event) { controller.add(position); currentTimer?.cancel(); if (playing) { currentTimer = Timer.periodic(step(), yieldPosition); } })` therefore stays subscribed and keeps re-arming its timer. The next `handler.positionStream` read builds a fresh subject and a fresh createPositionStream.
findings.failure_scenario: With a song loaded, tap the search bar (keyboard opens, DockedPlayer unmounts, listener count drops to zero, subject orphaned), then dismiss the keyboard (DockedPlayer remounts, new subject + new timer). Every such cycle leaves behind one playerEventStream listener and, while music plays, one Timer.periodic firing every 16-200 ms (200 ms for normal-length songs) that pushes positions into a subject nobody listens to. The process is long-lived (foreground media service), so after e.g. 100 searches there are ~100 dead timers = ~500 callbacks per second during playback, also with the screen off, growing without bound until the process dies. Individually cheap, but it is unbounded and runs in the background.
findings.fix: Hold one subscription for the app's lifetime in the handler: subscribe to `_player.positionStream` once in `_listenToPlayer` and republish it through a ValueNotifier<Duration> (or a handler-owned broadcast stream) that the mini player, player page and sleep timer listen to, so the plugin's subject never drops to zero listeners.

findings.title: Library filtering re-normalises three strings of every track on each keystroke, on the UI isolate
findings.evidence:
lib/services/local_search.dart:44-47 `static int _score(Track track, List<String> terms) { final title = normalize(track.title); final artist = normalize(TrackCredit.artistOf(track)); final raw = normalize(track.rawTitle);` and :77-88 normalize(): a per-rune `buffer.writeCharCode(code)` loop followed by `toLowerCase().replaceAll(_separators, '')` (a 40-alternative character class). Called for every track at :30-34.
lib/screens/search_view.dart:62-68 `_localMatches` recomputes whenever the query string differs, i.e. on every text change delivered through `_query` (app_shell.dart:88-91), which for a Chinese IME is every pinyin letter of the composing text. Nothing normalised is kept between keystrokes; the comment at local_search.dart:6 says 'Instant (runs on every keystroke)'.
findings.failure_scenario: With a library of ~2,000 songs, typing in the search bar runs ~6,000 normalize() calls over roughly 150-300 k characters (rune loop + StringBuffer + lowercase copy + regex replace, three allocations per string) per keystroke, synchronously inside the build of SearchView. That is on the order of 10-30 ms per key on a mid-range phone, i.e. dropped frames in the keyboard/typing animation that grow linearly with the library; the first keystroke after a naming event additionally re-parses every un-named title (TrackCredit.reset, library_controller.dart:226). Estimated from the code, not measured.
findings.fix: Cache the normalised (title, artist, rawTitle) triple per track - e.g. an Expando<_Norm> or a map keyed by Track identity built once per `library.downloaded` list - and only normalise the query per keystroke.

findings.title: Every library event (e.g. tapping the heart) reloads and re-derives the whole library: new list identities invalidate the sort, artist and search caches
findings.evidence:
lib/state/library_controller.dart:36 `DatabaseService.libraryUpdateStream.listen((_) => reload())`; :190-212 reload() always does `_downloaded = List.unmodifiable(results[0] as List<Track>); _downloadedIds = {for (final t in _downloaded) t.id}; _teachArtists();` - a fresh list object even when nothing about the downloads changed. _teachArtists (:218-223) runs `artistNamesOf` (a RegExp split, :129-133) for every named track.
The derived caches key on list identity: :96-98 `identical(_sortedSource, _downloaded)`, :142 `identical(_artistsSource, _downloaded)`, search_view.dart:64 `!identical(_localCacheSource, source)`. So each event re-sorts (:101-112, with `a.title.toLowerCase()` / `artistOf(a).toLowerCase()` allocated inside the comparator), re-groups artists (:144-161) and re-runs LocalSearch over the library.
The event fires for changes that do not touch downloads at all: database_service.dart:486 (end of _persistPlaylists: toggleFavorite, playlist add/remove/reorder/rename, and unconditionally from updateTrackMetadata :538) and :573.
findings.failure_scenario: Library of 2,000 songs sorted by 歌名 or 歌手. Tap the heart on the player or a row: toggleFavorite persists playlists and emits a library update; reload copies three lists, rebuilds the id set, regex-splits every named track's artist, and because `_downloaded` is a new object the home list re-sorts ~2,000 items (about 22 k comparisons, each allocating two to four lower-cased strings) on the UI isolate before the heart animation's next frame. The same happens once per completed download during a batch and once per automatically named song. Roughly 10-40 ms of UI-isolate work per event at that size (estimate), on top of the JSON rewrite the event came from.
findings.fix: In reload(), keep the previous `_downloaded` instance when the new list has the same Track instances in the same order (the stores hand back the same objects), so identity-keyed caches survive events that only changed playlists/favourites; and precompute lower-cased sort keys once per sort instead of inside the comparator.

findings.title: Recommendation token cache (256 entries, cleared wholesale) is smaller than the data it is built from, so every page re-parses all favourites
findings.evidence:
lib/services/recommendation_engine.dart:51-52 `static final Map<String, Set<String>> _tokenCache = {}; static const int _tokenCacheCap = 256;` and :70 `if (_tokenCache.length >= _tokenCacheCap) _tokenCache.clear();`. TasteProfile.build (:94-105) tokenises every favourite, 30 history entries and every search; recommend() (:165-173) rebuilds the profile from scratch on each call, then :210-212 scores every candidate (4 seeds x one Bilibili page each) through the same cache. tokenize (:58) runs `LyricsEngine.cleanTitle`, which the comment at :48 itself calls 'the expensive part' (it builds dozens of RegExp objects per call - lyrics_engine.dart:162-231, 250-432 - and scans knownArtists).
loadMore is driven by scrolling: search_view.dart:72-78 and recommendations_controller.dart:61-70.
findings.failure_scenario: A listener with 300+ favourites opens search and scrolls 为你推荐. Each loadMore calls recommend(): building the profile walks all favourites, the cache hits 256 entries part-way and is cleared, so most titles are parsed again; scoring the new candidates clears it again. With F favourites that is about F + 80 full cleanTitle runs per page on the UI isolate in two synchronous bursts (profile build, then ranking) - on the order of 50-150 ms for 500-1,000 favourites (estimate) - landing exactly while the list is being scrolled.
findings.fix: Size the cache to the data (e.g. cap at favourites + a few hundred, evicting oldest instead of clearing), or cache the built TasteProfile and rebuild it only when favourites/history/search history change rather than on every page.

findings.title: Cold start reads and parses every song's metadata file and awaits ~7 file operations per song before any library data is available
findings.evidence:
lib/services/database_service.dart:118-119 `await _loadTracks('$dir/bilibeat_downloaded.json', _downloadedTracks); await _discoverAudioFiles(dir);` inside _load, which every getter awaits via _ensureLoaded.
:220-235 for every `.ready` file: `await audioFile.exists() && (await audioFile.length()) > 0 && await metaFile.exists()` then `await metaFile.readAsString()`, `jsonDecode`, `Track.fromMap` - on the UI isolate, although :13-17 moved the main file's parse to an isolate for exactly this reason - and only afterwards :251 `if (!_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id))`, a linear scan per file (quadratic overall). The id is already in the file name (:241-245).
:265-281 the prune loop then awaits three more per track: `await ready.exists() && await audio.exists() && await audio.length() > 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: With 1,000 downloads every launch performs ~7,000 sequential awaited file round-trips plus 1,000 small JSON parses and ~1,000,000 id comparisons before `_ensureLoaded` completes. Until then the home page shows its empty 120 px placeholder (home_page.dart:112-113), restoreSession cannot build the queue, and a headset/notification play button that cold-starts the service waits on the same future (audio_player_handler.dart:752-755 -> restoreSession -> _library). At roughly 0.1-0.3 ms per awaited file call on a phone that is about 1-2 s added to every cold start, growing linearly with the library (estimate from the code). Already noted by the persistence reviewer; listed here for the cost model.
findings.fix: List the audio directory once, build a Set of ids from the `.ready`/`.m4a` names, read a meta JSON only for ids missing from `_downloadedTracks` (use a Set for the membership test), and prune by set lookup instead of three stats per track; run it after the library is published rather than inside _load.

findings.title: A lyric lookup that finds nothing still rewrites the entire lyrics store
findings.evidence:
lib/services/lyrics_store.dart:131-140 `_entries.remove(trackId); if (lyrics.isNotEmpty) { _entries[trackId] = lyrics.copyWith(pinned: false); _evict(); } try { await _persist(); }` - the persist is unconditional, although the doc comment at :119 says 'An empty result is not stored'. _persist (:155-158) maps every entry to JSON maps and goes through DatabaseService._writeJsonAtomically, which encodes on the calling isolate, writes with flush, then reads the whole file back and compares (database_service.dart:355, :359, :378).
Caller: lyrics_controller.dart:184-196 calls putAutomatic with whatever autoFetchLyrics returned, including Lyrics.none (network down, instrumental, unknown cover).
findings.failure_scenario: Store at its cap (300 automatic entries plus pins, each ~60 lines of {time,text,translation}: 1.5-3 MB of JSON). Listening offline, or to instrumentals/covers the providers do not know: every first play of such a track in a session ends with an empty result and still builds ~20 k maps, encodes, fsyncs and re-reads the multi-megabyte file on the UI isolate although the store's contents did not change - tens of ms of main-isolate work and megabytes of flash writes per track for nothing, with session/playlist saves queued behind it on the shared write lock. (The cost of the non-empty case is already in the persistence review; this is the no-op variant.)
findings.fix: Persist only when the map changed: `final removed = _entries.remove(trackId) != null; if (lyrics.isEmpty && !removed) return stands();`.

findings.title: Pausing keeps the CPU wake lock for the whole 30-minute idle window
findings.evidence:
lib/main.dart:50 `androidStopForegroundOnPause: false,`. audio_service-0.18.19 AudioService.java:705-712 enterPlayingState() calls `acquireWakeLock()` (a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK, :326); :715-719 `private void exitPlayingState() { if (config.androidStopForegroundOnPause) { exitForegroundState(); } }` and releaseWakeLock is reached only from exitForegroundState (:721-724) and onDestroy (:381). So with this config a pause releases nothing.
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:163 `static const Duration _idleStopAfter = Duration(minutes: 30);` and :333-338 arm the only thing that ends it: `_idleTimer = Timer(_idleStopAfter, () { if (!_player.playing) unawaited(stop()); });`.
findings.failure_scenario: Pause (button, headphones unplugged, sleep timer firing, a call that does not resume) and put the phone down. The foreground service keeps its partial wake lock, so the device cannot enter deep sleep for the next 30 minutes each time; the sleep-timer case is the common one - the timer exists to let the phone rest, and it stays awake half an hour longer. Order of magnitude: a few tens of mA instead of single digits for 30 minutes per pause. The playback reviewer separately reports that the lock may not be released even after the idle stop; this is the cost that remains even if that is fixed.
findings.fix: Shorten the idle window for pauses that cannot auto-resume (sleep timer, becoming-noisy, user pause while backgrounded), or release the lock on pause through a small native call while keeping the service in the foreground, re-acquiring it in play().

find:sweep-performance a5dadf.notes:
Method: grep sweep of lib/ for *Sync IO, jsonDecode/jsonEncode/compute, Timer/Ticker/AnimationController/repeat, BackdropFilter/ImageFilter, image decode sizing, HttpClient, static maps/sets, non-lazy lists, RegExp construction; then read each site. Plugin behaviour checked from source in ~/.pub-cache (audio_service 0.18.19, just_audio 0.10.6, rxdart 0.28.0). Nothing was run; all costs are estimates from code, not measurements. docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md (output of earlier finders) already contains the lyrics-store rewrite (#49), startup discovery (#50/#78), TrackCredit cache (#51), unconditional playlists rewrite (#79) and the post-idle wake lock (#19); I repeated only the ones where the performance lens adds something, and did not re-report #51/#79.

Checked and found sound:
- No synchronous file IO (*Sync) anywhere in lib/. Main library/playlist/lyrics files are parsed with compute().
- Session saves: 2 s debounce after queue changes plus one every 20 s while playing, cancelled on pause; small file. Not high-frequency. No per-progress-tick or per-keystroke JSON writes (search history is written on submit only).
- Download progress: throttled to 64 KiB; rows filter by id; LibraryController._onDownloads only notifies on membership change.
- Lists are lazy (SliverFixedExtentList.builder / ListView.builder / SliverGrid.builder). DownloadManagementSheet uses ListView(children:) but element inflation is still lazy; lyrics use a non-lazy Column, bounded by one song's lines.
- Images: every cover goes through CachedCoverImage with ResizeImage at display size and CDN-sized URLs; Flutter image cache capped at 40 MB / 150. (The exception is the notification artwork, finding 1.)
- HttpClients are static singletons per service with connection timeouts; non-200 bodies are drained. In-memory memos are bounded (_downloadedMemo 1024, _hintsMemo/_identityMemo 300, TrackCredit 2000, LyricsStore 300 automatic).
- Tickers: Shimmer only while loading; MarqueeText only on the player page and only when text overflows; LyricsView rebuilds only when the active line changes; PlayerSeekBar/mini progress rebuild small subtrees at <=5 Hz. just_audio 0.10.6 runs its position timer only while playing. Sleep-timer 1 s ticker and position subscription are cleared on fire/stop.
- RegExp: the hot static patterns in lyrics_engine are static finals and parseLrc's tag regex is hoisted; cleanTitle/_noisyClean do construct many RegExp literals per call (inside token loops), but callers are cached (TrackCredit) or once-per-track (identify), so I only counted it where a cache is defeated (findings 3 and 5).

Not reported, could not quantify:
- ArtworkBackdrop applies ImageFilter.blur(sigma 48) outside the FittedBox, so the filter runs over the full-screen output rather than the 64 dp thumbnail; under Impeller there is no raster cache, so it is recomputed on every frame the player page draws (continuous when a title marquees), contrary to the comment 'only repainted while cross-fading'. Moving the blur inside the FittedBox (small sigma on the thumbnail) would cut the work by orders of magnitude, but I cannot put a number on the current GPU cost without a device.
- Tapping any row re-installs the whole queue (default queue = entire library): N AudioSources over the just_audio channel plus N MediaItems over the audio_service channel per tap. Linear in library size; cost per tap not determinable from source.
- CachedCoverImage calls getApplicationSupportDirectory() (platform round trip) and three file stats per row load instead of caching the directory as DatabaseService does; adds latency before a thumbnail appears, not jank.
- AppShell reads MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf, so the shell and the visible rows rebuild on each frame of the keyboard animation; small.
- lib/screens/search_view.dart, playlist_page.dart, lyrics_engine.dart, bilibili_sdk.dart, track_sheet.dart, lyrics_sheet.dart were read only in the parts relevant to this lens (not listed in filesRead).

findings.title: Changing only the cover of an un-named song marks it as named by the listener with the raw video title as its song name
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:81-98: the early return only fires when title, artist AND cover are unchanged; otherwise `final updated = track.copyWith(title: title, uploader: artist.isEmpty ? TrackCredit.artistOf(track) : artist, coverUrl: _cover, named: true, matcher: 0, rawUploader: track.isNamed ? null : track.uploader);`. For an un-named track `_title` was initialised to `widget.track.title` (line 37), i.e. the video title (or `<video> - P3: <part>`), and `_artist` to the parsed credit (line 39). Consumers of the flag: lib/services/track_naming.dart:95-96 `_settled(track) => track.isNamed && (track.matcher == 0 || track.matcher == matcher)` and :101 `if (!enabled || _settled(track) ...) return;`; lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:61-64 `track.isNamed ? (song: track.title, artist: track.uploader) : (song: track.partTitle, artist: null)`; lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:2146 `final title = song ?? cleaned['songTitle']!;` then :1899 queries NetEase with `'$artist $title'`, and :1753 isTitleMatching accepts by containment; lib/state/library_controller.dart:219-226 teaches `LyricsEngine.knownArtists` from every `isNamed` track.
findings.failure_scenario: A download the matcher has not (yet) named, e.g. title '【4K60帧】周深《大鱼》现场 纯享版'. The listener opens 编辑信息, taps the cover, picks a picture and presses 保存 without touching the text fields. The track is stored with named=true, matcher=0, title = the whole video title. From then on: (1) automatic matching never looks at it again, in this or any later matcher generation (CLAUDE.md: matcher 0 = the listener) so the row keeps the video title forever; (2) automatic lyrics are searched with the whole video title as the song name instead of the parsed '大鱼' (or, for a part of a multi-part video, with '<video> - P3: <part>' instead of the part name), so the lookup misses or accepts any NetEase song whose 2+ character name happens to be contained in that title; (3) the parsed credit (which falls back to the UP主) is frozen into `uploader` and fed to the offline parser as a known artist.
findings.fix: In _save, treat the text as edited only when it differs from what the sheet opened with: if title == track.title and artist == TrackCredit.artistOf(track), save `track.copyWith(coverUrl: _cover)` only (leave named/matcher/uploader/rawUploader as they were). Set named: true / matcher: 0 only when the title or artist field actually changed.

findings.title: Every library write failure is swallowed, so 编辑信息 / playlists / favourites report success and the edit is lost on next launch; '保存失败，请重试' is unreachable
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:453-461 `static Future<void> _persistDownloaded() async { try { ... await _writeJsonAtomically(...); } catch (e) { debugPrint('DatabaseService _persistDownloaded error: $e'); } }`; identical catch-and-log in _persistRecentlyPlayed (:463-471), _persistPlaylists (:473-487, which then still emits the library update), _persistSearchHistory (:489-497), setPref (:836-843) and savePlaybackSession (:864-874). lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:141-143 saveTrackMetadata: `} catch (e) { debugPrint('saveTrackMetadata error: $e'); }`. So DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata (:521-548) cannot throw for a write failure. Caller: lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:99-108 `try { await DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata(updated); AppServices.instance.handler.updateTrackMetadata(updated); if (mounted) Navigator.pop(context); } catch (error, stack) { ... showAppSnackBar(..., message: '保存失败，请重试'); }` - the catch branch is dead. _writeJsonAtomically itself (:389-391) rethrows and even verifies the bytes that landed (:375-387), but no caller except writeStoreFile (lyrics, :890-893) lets that reach the UI. debugPrint is a no-op in release (lib/main.dart:20), so nothing is logged either.
findings.failure_scenario: Storage is full (a music downloader fills storage by design) or the documents volume returns an I/O error. The listener renames a song, creates a playlist, adds 20 songs to it, favourites a track. Each sheet closes normally and the UI shows the change, because the in-memory lists were mutated before the write. On the next launch the old JSON files are loaded: the names, the playlist and the favourites are gone, with no message ever shown. Lyrics behave differently ('歌词已应用，但未能保存'), which shows the intended contract.
findings.fix: Let the _persist* helpers rethrow (keep the debugPrint), and have the mutators either roll back the in-memory change or surface the failure: at minimum TrackInfoSheet's existing catch then works, and playlist/favourite actions can show one shared snackbar ('未能保存，请检查存储空间'). Keep swallowing only for best-effort stores (session, recently played).

findings.title: No Chinese localisation delegates: Flutter's built-in UI strings (Paste / Select all / Copy, Back, Dismiss) are English in a Simplified-Chinese app
findings.evidence: lib/main.dart:77-82 `return MaterialApp(title: 'BiliBeats', debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false, theme: AppTheme.darkTheme, home: const AppShell());` - no `locale`, `supportedLocales` or `localizationsDelegates`; pubspec.yaml:10-17 has no `flutter_localizations` dependency (grep 'localizations|Locale(' over lib and pubspec returns nothing). Flutter source: packages/flutter/lib/src/material/app.dart:254 `this.supportedLocales = const <Locale>[Locale('en', 'US')]`; material_localizations.dart:1209 `String get pasteButtonLabel => 'Paste';`, :1212 `selectAllButtonLabel => 'Select all'`, :1077 `backButtonTooltip => 'Back'`, :1239 `modalBarrierDismissLabel => 'Dismiss'`. Sites that surface them: the search field (lib/app/app_shell.dart:175), the lyric editor whose own hint says '粘贴歌词' (lib/widgets/lyrics_sheet.dart:427-442), 编辑信息 fields (lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:215), promptForText (lib/widgets/sheet.dart:238), and the automatic back buttons of the SliverAppBars in lib/screens/playlist_page.dart:146 and lib/screens/artist_page.dart:57.
findings.failure_scenario: On Android the listener long-presses the search field to paste a BV number or link, or long-presses the lyric editor to paste lyrics: the selection toolbar reads 'Paste' / 'Select all' (and 'Cut' / 'Copy' with a selection). With TalkBack, the back button on a playlist or artist page is announced as 'Back' and sheet scrims as 'Dismiss'. CLAUDE.md: 'UI copy is Simplified Chinese'; the icon-button convention explicitly relies on tooltips for screen readers. The resolved app locale is also en_US, so Han text is shaped without a zh-Hans locale hint.
findings.fix: Add `flutter_localizations: {sdk: flutter}` to pubspec.yaml and in MaterialApp set `locale: const Locale('zh', 'CN')`, `supportedLocales: const [Locale('zh', 'CN')]`, `localizationsDelegates: GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates`. Optionally add zh-Hans to the iOS project's knownRegions / CFBundleLocalizations so system-provided pickers follow.

findings.title: Recommendation taste profile keys 'UP主' weights on Track.uploader, which is the song's artist once a track is named
findings.evidence: lib/services/recommendation_engine.dart:14-15 `/// UP主 name -> weight. final Map<String, double> uploaders;`; :86-88 `if (t.uploader.isNotEmpty) { uploaders[t.uploader] = (uploaders[t.uploader] ?? 0) + weight; }`; :111-112 `double score(Track track) { var score = (uploaders[track.uploader] ?? 0) * 2.0;`; :119-131 seedQueries doc 'the UP主s the user returns to' takes the top two keys. lib/models/track.dart:35-43: once named, `uploader` is the artist and the real UP主 moves to `rawUploader`. Automatic matching is on by default (lib/services/track_naming.dart:23 `static bool enabled = true;`) and names favourites/history copies too (database_service.dart:532-544). Candidates come straight from BilibiliSdk.search (bilibili_sdk.dart:616-621 `uploader: author`), i.e. they carry UP主 names.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener's favourites are mostly auto-named 周深 songs uploaded by three clip channels. The profile's `uploaders` map now holds '周深' and collaboration strings like '周深 & 五月天' rather than the channels. When candidates are ranked, `uploaders[candidate.uploader]` is looked up with the candidate's UP主 name, so the strongest (x2) term is 0 for every candidate except videos uploaded by an account literally named like the artist; the channels the listener actually returns to are never favoured, and a multi-artist credit string is sent verbatim to Bilibili as a seed query. Ranking silently degrades to title-bigram overlap. Invariant in CLAUDE.md: never use track.uploader directly once naming exists.
findings.fix: Build two maps: UP主 weights from `t.rawUploader ?? (t.isNamed ? null : t.uploader)` and artist weights from LibraryController.artistNamesOf(t)/TrackCredit.artistOf(t). Score a candidate with the UP主 map on `candidate.uploader` plus the artist map on TrackCredit.artistOf(candidate); seed with individual artist names and UP主 names.

findings.title: Player keeps its own copy of track metadata (_latest) that outlives a delete, and auto-naming is not retried for a song re-downloaded in the same session
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:145 `final Map<String, Track> _latest = {};` (never cleared; removeTracks :853-866 does not touch it), :170 `Track _resolve(Track tag) => _latest[tag.id] ?? tag;`, :622-625 `final library = await DatabaseService.getDownloadedTracks(); return {for (final track in library) track.id: _resolve(track)};` - the handler's cached copy wins over what the library stores now. lib/services/track_naming.dart:34 `static final Set<String> _attempted = {};` and :101 `if (!enabled || _settled(track) || !_attempted.add(track.id)) return;` - ids are only removed again on an offline lookup (:135, :157), not when the download is deleted. Re-registration stores the caller's copy untouched: database_service.dart:767-771 `if (_downloadedTracks.any((t) => t.id == track.id)) return; _downloadedTracks.insert(0, track);`.
findings.failure_scenario: A song is downloaded and auto-named this session ('大鱼' / 周深; `_latest[id]` holds that copy, `_attempted` holds the id). The listener deletes the download and later the same session downloads it again from a Bilibili search row. The library now stores the raw search copy, and LibraryController.reload's `TrackNaming.autoName(track)` returns immediately because the id is still in `_attempted`. The home list, search and the song's sheet show the video title and UP主, while tapping it plays a queue built through `_resolve`, so the mini player, the full player and the system notification show '大鱼 - 周深' for the same row; the nowPlaying listener then calls autoName with that named copy, which is 'settled', so nothing reconciles the two until the app is restarted. CLAUDE.md states playback has one source of truth and nothing in Dart keeps a second copy.
findings.fix: On DatabaseService.downloadRemovedStream drop the ids from `_latest` (in removeTracks) and from TrackNaming._attempted; or make `_library()` trust the stored copy and use `_latest` only for tags already inside the native queue.

findings.title: README states Android 6.0+ but the build's minSdk is 24 (Android 7.0)
findings.evidence: README.md:14 `2. 在 Android 设备上打开下载的 .apk 文件（需 Android 6.0 及以上版本）。` android/app/build.gradle(.kts):37 `minSdk = flutter.minSdkVersion`. ~/flutter/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt:26 `val minSdkVersion: Int = 24` (Flutter 3.44.8, the version pinned in CI and CLAUDE.md).
findings.failure_scenario: Someone following the README sideloads the release APK on an Android 6.0 (API 23) device: the package installer rejects it ('解析软件包时出现问题' / app not compatible) although the README says that version is supported.
findings.fix: Change README.md line 14 to 'Android 7.0 及以上版本' (or pin minSdk explicitly in android/app/build.gradle so the documented floor does not move with the Flutter SDK).

findings.title: assets/logo.png (381 KB) is bundled into every build but nothing loads it
findings.evidence: pubspec.yaml:26-27 `assets:\n    - assets/`; `ls -la assets` -> only logo.png, 380950 bytes. `grep -rn "logo\|AssetImage\|Image.asset\|rootBundle" lib` returns nothing. git log shows it was added for a header logo (16dd9fe 'feat: vertical playlist bars, header logo, recropped app icon'); the 5.0.0 shell (lib/app/app_shell.dart) has no header mark. tool/make_brand_assets.py:84 still regenerates it with the comment '# in-app header mark'.
findings.failure_scenario: Every Android APK, iOS .ipa and macOS bundle carries ~0.37 MB of uncompressed PNG that no code path can display; the brand script keeps regenerating an 'in-app header mark' that does not exist, so a future icon refresh will appear to update an in-app logo and change nothing.

findings.title: Several tap targets are below the documented 48 pt minimum, including the adjacent 重试 / 忽略 pair
findings.evidence: lib/widgets/download_management_sheet.dart:184-186 `return SizedBox(width: 44, height: 48, child: IconButton(tooltip: tooltip, padding: EdgeInsets.zero, ...` used side by side for 重试 and 忽略 at :141-156 (21 pt glyphs, no gap). lib/app/app_shell.dart:196-198 `IconButton(tooltip: '清除', visualDensity: VisualDensity.compact, ...` inside a 44 pt high field (:163); lib/screens/home_page.dart:619-621 `IconButton(tooltip: '不再提示', visualDensity: VisualDensity.compact, ...`; lib/screens/search_view.dart:317-321 history `_Chip`: InkWell with `EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 14, vertical: 8)` around 14 pt text (about 35 pt tall, no minimum-size wrapper); lib/screens/home_page.dart:213 lens switch `_height = 44` with a bare GestureDetector. CLAUDE.md UI conventions: 'Touch targets are at least 48 pt'.
findings.failure_scenario: In 下载 with a failed download, the retry and dismiss buttons are two 44 pt-wide targets touching each other at the right edge; a slightly-off tap on 重试 hits 忽略, which removes the failed entry (DownloadManager.dismissFailed) and with it the only place the failure was shown, so the song silently is neither downloaded nor listed. The other sites are simply harder to hit than the convention promises.
