find:sweep-conformance ab0254.notes:
Method: grep-enumerated every site for each invariant across lib/, then read the surrounding files (most of app/, screens/, state/, widgets/ in full; lyrics_engine.dart, bilibili_sdk.dart, audio_download_service.dart, lyrics_sheet.dart, sheet.dart only in the relevant sections). Nothing was run, no network requests were made. docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md (an earlier, unverified pass by the subsystem finders) was skimmed by title only to avoid repeating it; the missing DownloadManager.errors listener, re-download storing the raw copy, snack bars under sheets, the NowPlayingPage._open latch and the knownIds gap are already there and are not repeated here.

Invariants found to hold:
(a) Current song: only handler.nowPlaying / queueNotifier / playingNotifier are read; LyricsController._trackId and NowPlayingPage._calibrating are derived guards, not a second 'current song'. The one second copy of metadata is the handler's _latest map (finding 5).
(c) All library JSON goes through _writeJsonAtomically (downloaded, recently played, playlists, search history, prefs, session, lyrics via writeStoreFile). Writes outside it are by design and tolerant: per-track meta (AudioDownloadService._atomicWriteString, tmp+rename), the .part.json resume note, the cover cache, picked-cover copy.
(d) Artist display: every UI site and the media-session MediaItem (audio_player_handler.dart:388) use TrackCredit.artistOf / LibraryController.artistOf. Remaining raw .uploader reads are correct for named tracks (lyrics_controller, track_naming) or have no visible effect (lyrics_sheet.dart:122 stores the UP主 as the artist of user-written lyrics, never shown), except recommendation_engine (finding 4).
(e) nowPlaying is a TrackNotifier; the only ValueNotifier<Track?> is handler.preparing, which never carries an edited copy.
(f) All song lists use SongTile; taps go through openTrack except deliberate cases (queue sheet jumps, edit/pick selection). The recent rail on Home draws cover cards rather than SongTile but taps through openTrack.
(g) Hard-coded colours outside the theme are few and currently equal theme values or are shader masks: artwork_backdrop.dart:59-61 (background 0x08080A at three alphas), shimmer.dart:66-68, progress_ring.dart:19, marquee_text.dart:242-245, lyrics_view.dart:194-197, settings_sheet.dart:142 Colors.white. No visible defect; they would drift if AppColors.background changed.
(h) Every IconButton has a tooltip (script-checked) and custom tappables carry Tooltip or Semantics labels. Size exceptions are in finding 8.
(i) Pinned lyrics: LyricsStore.putAutomatic checks revision and pinned before and after the write, _evict skips pinned, the load merge keeps session pins, and the controller does not start a lookup over a pinned state on a metadata edit. Only the listener's own 重新匹配 clears a pin.
(j) All on-disk names still start with bilibeat_ (downloaded, recently_played, playlists, search_history, prefs, session, lyrics, bilibeat_audio/, bilibeat_covers/).
(k) No English or Traditional strings in the app's own copy; exception texts in English are only logged. The English comes from Flutter's default localisations (finding 3).
(l) playTrack / playCollection / restoreSession build the queue only from DatabaseService.getDownloadedTracks(), after _ensureLocal for the tapped track; load-time discovery prunes entries whose files are gone.
(m) rawTitle: copyWith cannot change it and the three constructors in bilibili_sdk.dart set it to the video title.
(b) 'Screens do not read DatabaseService directly' holds for reads of library data in screens/ (only a pref read in home_page.dart:58). Two widgets do bypass LibraryController: download_management_sheet.dart:53/84 (own libraryUpdateStream subscription and getDownloadedTracks) and track_download_button.dart:70/100 (own subscription plus a file-stat 'downloaded' flag next to library.isDownloaded). I could not construct a lasting wrong state from either, so they are not reported as findings.

Dead code the analyzer cannot see (public, so not flagged), no user-visible effect on its own: TrackDownloadButton.onPlay is never passed, so its 'play' state and '播放' tooltip are unreachable; DatabaseService.addTrackToPlaylist (single-track) has no caller; DownloadManager.isFailed has no caller; AppTypography.display/overline and the bottomNavigationBarTheme are unused. Untracked tool/song_model/ (43 MB incl. .pt weights and crawl dumps) and docs/audit-2026-10-06/ are not gitignored; CLAUDE.md and README do not mention tool/song_model.

Documentation checked and accurate: fixture counts (540 titles, 126 surveyed videos), iOS 13.0 deployment target, CI Flutter 3.44.8 with --exclude-tags live, analyzer error promotions, debug-key fallback warning in build.gradle, 15-minute rule (lyrics_engine.dart:1577), TrackNaming.matcher semantics, release-mode debugPrint silencing (no stray print()). Stale comments only: database_service.dart:742 calls the id 'bvid_cid' (it is bvid_p<page>); recommendation_engine.dart:142 says 为您推荐 while the UI says 为你推荐.

Not determined: whether the missing zh locale changes Han glyph variants on a given device (depends on platform font fallback, not verifiable from source); finding 5 was traced by reading only and has no existing test covering delete-then-re-download in one session.

findings.title: 下载并播放 that finishes while the app is in the background starts playback without a foreground service on Android 12+ (no notification, no wake lock, no media session)
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:638 `if (!await _ensureLocal(track, token)) return;` ... :657 `await _install(tracks, start, token: token);` and in _install :590 `if (autoplay) _startPlayback();` -> :596 `unawaited(_player.play()...)`. Nothing on this path looks at the app lifecycle or at whether the media service is already in the foreground.

The handler's own header (:38-42) states the constraint: "resuming after an audio interruption never has to start a foreground service from the background — which Android 12+ forbids". main.dart:50 `androidStopForegroundOnPause: false` only keeps the service in the foreground AFTER something has played; on a fresh launch (session restored paused, :717 `autoplay: false`) or after the 30-minute idle stop the service is not in the foreground.

audio_service-0.18.19 AudioService.java:523-526 `boolean wasPlaying = this.playing; ... this.playing = playing;` then :559-560 `if (!wasPlaying && playing) { enterPlayingState();` and :705-712 `private void enterPlayingState() { ContextCompat.startForegroundService(this, new Intent(AudioService.this, AudioService.class)); ... acquireWakeLock(); mediaSession.setSessionActivity(contentIntent); internalStartForeground(); }` - no try/catch; startForegroundService throws ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException when the app is in the background (targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion, android/app/build.gradle:38). The throw is caught only at AudioServicePlugin.java:998-1000 `catch (Exception e) { e.printStackTrace(); result.error(e.getMessage(), null, null); }` and on the Dart side swallowed at audio_service.dart:1137-1138 `catch (e) { _asyncError.add(e); }`. Because `this.playing` was already set to true before the throw, later setState calls see wasPlaying == true and never retry enterPlayingState; mediaSession.setActive(true), acquireWakeLock() and startForeground() are all skipped for that whole stretch of playback. ExoPlayer itself is started by just_audio independently, so audio does begin.
findings.failure_scenario: Android 12+, battery-optimisation exemption not granted. Open the app (cold start, or more than 30 minutes after pausing), search, tap a result that is not downloaded -> 下载并播放 (snackbar 下载完成后播放). Nothing has played in this process, so the media service is not in the foreground. Lock the screen or switch apps while the file downloads (a long recording on mobile data takes well over the ~5 s grace period). When the download lands, _install calls _player.play(): ExoPlayer starts, but audio_service's enterPlayingState throws inside startForegroundService. Result: the song plays from a background process with no notification, no lock-screen/headset controls and no wake lock, and is cut off when the system freezes or kills the cached process (or the song never audibly starts). The state only heals when the listener returns to the app and toggles pause/play. When a song was already playing or paused earlier in the session the service is already foreground and the path works, which is why this is easy to miss in testing.
findings.fix: Do not autoplay from the background unless the service is already in the foreground. In playTrack/_install, when the request had to wait for a download and `WidgetsBinding.instance.lifecycleState != AppLifecycleState.resumed` and nothing has played since launch/idle stop (track a `_serviceForeground` flag set on the first playing=true and cleared in stop()), install with autoplay: false and start playback on the next `resumed` (AppShell already observes the lifecycle), or simply leave it ready and say so. Alternatively put the service in the foreground when a play-path download starts (a brief play/pause-free `AudioService` foreground entry is not exposed by the plugin, so the lifecycle gate is the minimal fix).

findings.title: A 下载并播放 request that is superseded keeps downloading with no visible trace and no way to stop it, and lands in the library
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:635-636 `final token = ++_selection; preparing.value = null;` - a new selection only clears the indicator. The older request is still inside :608 `await AudioDownloadService.ensureDownloaded(track);` and afterwards merely returns :609 `return token == _selection;`; on failure :612 `if (token == _selection) { _messages.add(...) }` says nothing. AudioDownloadService.ensureDownloaded/_transfer (audio_download_service.dart:259-294, 418-559) take no cancellation signal, and on success always run :352 `await DatabaseService.saveDownloadedTrack(track);`.

The download is also invisible everywhere else: download_manager.dart:44-45 `/// Playback-path downloads (started inside the audio handler) are intentionally NOT tracked here`, so app_shell.dart:243-245 (`library.activeDownloads.length` ... `if (active == 0 && failed == 0) return const SizedBox(width: 4);`) shows no ring, the 下载 sheet lists nothing, and track_sheet.dart:253 `DownloadManager.instance.taskFor(track.id)` is null so the song's own sheet offers 下载并播放 / 下载 again as if nothing were happening. The existing test 'a newer request wins over a slower older one' (test/playback_handler_test.dart:120-139) only asserts what is displayed, not that the older transfer continues.
findings.failure_scenario: On mobile data, tap a search result that turns out to be a 2-hour concert video (100+ MB) -> 下载并播放. The mini player shows 正在准备「…」. Realising the mistake, tap the result you actually wanted (or any downloaded song): the 正在准备 line now names the new song or disappears. The concert keeps downloading in full with no ring, no entry in 下载管理 and no cancel; minutes later it silently appears in the library (and is then auto-matched), or it fails silently leaving a large .part file. The same happens for every additional result tapped while an earlier one is still preparing: all of them download to completion, only the last one plays.
findings.fix: When a newer selection supersedes a preparing download, either cancel it (thread a cancel token from _ensureLocal into ensureDownloaded/_transfer: cancel the response subscription and keep or discard the .part), or hand it to DownloadManager (create the task entry so it shows in the top-bar ring and 下载管理, with failures recorded there). At minimum, register play-path downloads with DownloadManager so TrackSheet and the downloads button reflect them.

find:journey-first-play ad56e0.notes:
Method: walked the journey through the code (AppShell -> SearchView -> OnlineSearchController -> BilibiliSdk.search -> openTrack/TrackSheet -> handler.playTrack/_ensureLocal -> AudioDownloadService -> DatabaseService -> LibraryController/TrackNaming -> _install -> skip -> saveSession/restoreSession), plus audio_service 0.18.19 (AudioService.java, AudioServicePlugin.java, audio_service.dart) and just_audio 0.10.6 play() from the pub cache. Nothing was run and no network request was made. Finding 1 is a deduction from plugin source plus Android's documented background-FGS rule; it should be confirmed on an Android 12+ device (logcat for ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException) before fixing. Partially read only: lib/models/playback_state.dart, lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart, lib/widgets/sheet.dart, lib/screens/home_page.dart, test/playback_handler_test.dart.

docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md already exists in the checkout (untracked, 90 numbered findings from the earlier part of this run). I did not repeat what it already holds. Journey issues I independently re-derived and that are already listed there: BV/av/short-link queries ignore `page`, so loadMore re-fetches the same video on every scroll (#7/#29); paging past the last music-zone page continues with unfiltered results at that page number (#28/#42); a multi-part video found by keyword is stored as P1 under the whole video's title and total duration (#43); scrolling library matches pages a hidden stale Bilibili query (#45/#66); short-link resolution reads the whole video page inside a 6 s budget (#40); a play-path success does not clear a DownloadManager failure (#36/#74); backupUrl is never tried when baseUrl fails (notes); play() during an in-flight restore is dropped (#73).

Checked and found sound on this journey:
- Search controller tokens: a slow older search/loadMore cannot write into a newer query; clear() during a request; retry; history token vs clearHistory; chip submit sets the field and the trimmed query matches `_online.query` so results show.
- Id extraction for BV (case of the prefix, boundaries), av digits -> aid, full URLs (www/m, ?p=, bvid= params), b23.tv links carrying a BV directly; "AV1 编码"-style text falls through to keyword search when no such video exists; single-line field strips pasted newlines so share text still resolves.
- Row-tap contract: downloaded -> playTrack, otherwise sheet; double tap on a row hits the modal barrier, double tap on 下载并播放 is ignored by the popping route; reopened sheet + second 下载并播放 or 下载 joins the in-flight future (AudioDownloadService._inFlight) and DownloadManager's double-tap guard holds.
- preparing: set only for the current token, cleared by every newer selection and in finally for the current one; it cannot stick except through a hung download (already reported as the disk-full hang). Leaving search (取消/Back) does not touch the handler; the mini player and the AppShell snackbar still report the outcome.
- Download -> play hand-off: saveDownloadedTrack is awaited before ensureDownloaded returns, so _library() contains the new track; a track on disk but missing from the store is still inserted at index 0 and is rediscovered from its meta JSON on next launch; play() is a no-op when already playing so the old song hands over without a gap in state; TrackNaming renames reach the queue through _latest/_publish; SongIdentity.coverUrl is nullable so a match without artwork does not blank the cover.
- Skips at the ends: next past the end wraps (列表循环) or parks paused at the first item (off); previous at the start wraps or stays; single-item queue restarts; _navTarget keeps rapid presses one step each; shuffle order used throughout.
- Relaunch: saveSession never overwrites with an empty sequence (launch before restore, lifecycle paused before restore), saved on pause/20 s/2 s after queue change and on lifecycle paused/detached; restore drops ids no longer in the library, falls back to index 0/position 0 when the current id is gone, does not record history, does not autoplay; a tap during restore wins via the token and PlayerInterruptedException handling.
- audio_service forwards state in a loop that survives a failed setState (errors go to _asyncError), so one refused foreground start does not stop later state updates.

Could not determine from source: how long Android lets the Dart isolate keep downloading after the app is backgrounded with no foreground service (the cached-app freezer would stall the transfer and surface later as a chunk timeout), and whether swiping the task away while a download is preparing destroys the Flutter engine before the download can complete and autoplay.

findings.title: Saving 编辑信息 after changing only the cover marks an un-named song as listener-named with its raw video title
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:81-98: the early-out only fires when title, artist AND cover are all unchanged; otherwise `final updated = track.copyWith(title: title, uploader: artist.isEmpty ? TrackCredit.artistOf(track) : artist, coverUrl: _cover, named: true, matcher: 0, rawUploader: track.isNamed ? null : track.uploader);` -- `named: true` and `matcher: 0` are set unconditionally, even when the title field still holds the prefilled video title (line 37 `TextEditingController(text: widget.track.title)`) and the artist field the parsed guess (line 39).
Consumers of that flag: lib/services/track_naming.dart:97-98 `_settled(track) => track.isNamed && (track.matcher == 0 || track.matcher == matcher)` so autoName/_name never look at it again; lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:61-64 `_namedBy` returns `(song: track.title, artist: track.uploader)` for a named track, and :184-188 passes that to `LyricsEngine.autoFetchLyrics(track.rawTitle, song: named.song, ...)`, where lyrics_engine.dart:2146 `final title = song ?? cleaned['songTitle']!` uses the whole video title as the song name; lib/state/library_controller.dart:219-225 teaches `LyricsEngine.knownArtists` from every `isNamed` track, and lyrics_engine.dart:1350 `if (isOwn(norm) || _knownArtists.containsKey(norm)) return true;` then trusts that name as a singer without asking NetEase.
findings.failure_scenario: A song has just been downloaded (auto-matching is still running its lookups, or is switched off, or found nothing), so its title is still e.g. "【4K60帧】周深《大鱼》现场 纯享版". The listener opens 编辑信息, taps the artwork, picks a picture and presses 保存 without touching the text fields. The track is stored as named=true, matcher=0, title = the video title, uploader = whatever the offline parser guessed (the UP主 when the title has no readable singer). From then on: automatic matching never names it (this or any later matcher generation), the in-flight lookup is discarded (track_naming.dart:170-177 sees `named` changed), lyric lookup searches for the full video title as a song name instead of the parsed 大鱼, and the guessed artist (possibly the UP主) is fed to the matcher as a known singer for other videos.
findings.fix: In _save, only claim the name when the listener actually changed title or artist: if `title == track.title && artist == TrackCredit.artistOf(track)` keep `named`, `matcher`, `uploader` and `rawUploader` as they are and write just the new cover (`track.copyWith(coverUrl: _cover)`).

findings.title: Library writes swallow disk errors, so 编辑信息's 保存失败 path is unreachable and every library change reports success while nothing is saved
findings.evidence:
lib/services/database_service.dart:453-461 `_persistDownloaded` wraps `_writeJsonAtomically` in `try { ... } catch (e) { debugPrint('DatabaseService _persistDownloaded error: $e'); }`; same in `_persistPlaylists` (473-487, which then still emits the library update) and `_persistRecentlyPlayed` (463-471). `_writeJsonAtomically` itself says (375-376) `One retry, then propagate the failure to the caller` and rethrows (389-391), but no library caller lets it through. AudioDownloadService.saveTrackMetadata (audio_download_service.dart:141-143) swallows as well.
lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:99-108 expects a throw: `try { await DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata(updated); ... if (mounted) Navigator.pop(context); } catch (error, stack) { ... showAppSnackBar(..., message: '保存失败，请重试'); }` -- updateTrackMetadata (521-548) can no longer throw for a write failure. Likewise track_sheet.dart:304-305 shows `已加入「…」` and artist_page.dart:37 `已存为歌单` unconditionally.
findings.failure_scenario: The phone's storage is full (the usual state in which a download has just failed in a music downloader). The listener renames a song, favourites two others and builds a playlist. Each temp-file write fails with ENOSPC; the in-memory lists are already mutated, the UI shows the new state and the success toasts, and the edit sheet closes normally. After the next launch all of it is gone: the files on disk are the old snapshots. Lyrics, by contrast, do surface the same failure (now_playing_page.dart `校准未能保存`).
findings.fix: Let the persist helpers rethrow (or return a bool) for the deliberate, user-initiated mutations (updateTrackMetadata, playlist create/rename/add/remove/reorder, toggleFavorite) and have the callers show a failure snack instead of the success one; keep swallowing only for background writes (history, loudness, discovery).

findings.title: Per-id session state survives 删除下载: a song re-downloaded in the same session shows the old name in the player and the raw video title in the library, and is not auto-matched again
findings.evidence:
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:145 `final Map<String, Track> _latest = {};` is written by updateTrackMetadata (932-935) and _backfillLoudness (463) and never cleared; removeTracks (853-866) only removes native sources. :170 `Track _resolve(Track tag) => _latest[tag.id] ?? tag;` and :622-625 `_library()` returns `{for (final track in library) track.id: _resolve(track)}` -- so an old `_latest` entry overrides the library's current copy when a queue is built.
lib/services/track_naming.dart:36 `static final Set<String> _attempted = {};` and :103-106 `if (!enabled || _settled(track) || !_attempted.add(track.id)) return;` -- the id stays in the set after the song is deleted (database_service.dart:779-786 removeDownloadedTrack touches neither).
The re-download registers the caller's raw copy: audio_download_service.dart:352 `await DatabaseService.saveDownloadedTrack(track)`; library_controller.dart:202-204 then calls `TrackNaming.autoName(track)` for the arrival, which returns at the `_attempted` check.
findings.failure_scenario: Download a song from search; it is auto-matched to "大鱼 / 周深" (so `_attempted` and `_latest` both hold its id). Delete the download (wrong take, glitchy file) and download it again from the search result in the same session. The library row, artist grouping and local search now show the raw video title and UP主 for the rest of the session (autoName is skipped), while tapping it plays under the previous name/cover in the player, queue sheet, notification and 最近播放 (queue built through `_resolve`). If the earlier copy had been edited by hand, that stale hand edit is what the player shows while the library shows the video.
findings.fix: On DatabaseService.downloadRemovedStream, drop the ids from the handler's `_latest` (and `_loudnessRequested`) and from TrackNaming._attempted; or make `_library()` prefer the stored copy and use `_latest` only for tags already in the native queue.

findings.title: 存为歌单 on the artist page has no in-flight guard: a double tap creates two identical playlists and pushes two pages
findings.evidence: lib/screens/artist_page.dart:63-65 `IconButton(tooltip: '存为歌单', onPressed: () => _saveAsPlaylist(context, group), ...)` on a StatelessWidget with no busy flag; :31-39 `final playlist = await DatabaseService.createPlaylist(group.name); await DatabaseService.addTracksToPlaylist(playlist.id, group.tracks.reversed.toList()); ... if (context.mounted) unawaited(PlaylistPage.open(context, playlist.id));`. Nothing covers the button until PlaylistPage is pushed, and that only happens after two whole-file persists (database_service.dart:603 and :704), each of which is write + flush + rename + read-back verification behind the global write lock (346-401). Every other create path opens a modal dialog first (promptForText), which blocks a second tap; this one does not.
findings.failure_scenario: On an artist page the listener double-taps the 存为歌单 icon (or taps again because nothing visibly happens while the two file writes run, e.g. with a large playlists file or while a lyrics/library write holds the lock). Both taps run _saveAsPlaylist: two playlists named after the artist with the same songs appear under 歌单, and two PlaylistPages are pushed on top of each other.
findings.fix: Make the action re-entrancy safe (a static/State `_saving` flag cleared in finally, disabling the button while set), or push the playlist page first and fill it afterwards.

findings.title: Picked covers are stored at full camera resolution and the Android media session decodes them unscaled every time the song's metadata is published
findings.evidence:
lib/utils/cover_picker.dart:11 `final image = await ImagePicker().pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery);` (no maxWidth/maxHeight/imageQuality) and :19 `await File(image.path).copy(saved.path);` -- the original file is kept as the track cover (track_info_sheet.dart:52-55, 93).
lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:391-397 publishes it as `artUri: Uri.tryParse(track.coverUrl.startsWith('/') ? 'file://${track.coverUrl}' : track.coverUrl)`; lib/main.dart:40-53 builds AudioServiceConfig without artDownscaleWidth/Height.
audio_service-0.18.19 lib/audio_service.dart:1058-1059 sends a file:// art path straight to the platform; android/.../AudioService.java:218-238: `if (config.artDownscaleWidth != -1) { ...inSampleSize... } else { ... bitmap = BitmapFactory.decodeFile(artUri.getPath()); }`, :242 `artBitmapCache.put(artUriString, bitmap)` where the cache is `maxMemory / 8` (331-336, sizeOf = byteCount), and :790 `artBitmap = loadArtBitmap(artCacheFilePath, null)` keeps the bitmap in a field while the item is current. The Flutter side is fine (cached_cover_image.dart:283 ResizeImage); only the service path is unscaled. The handler re-publishes the media item on announce, on duration change (_onDuration, 286-297) and on every metadata edit.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener sets a photo from the gallery (12 MP = about 48 MB as ARGB_8888; 50 MP modes = about 200 MB) as a song's cover. Each time that song becomes current, the background media service decodes the full image and holds it for as long as the song is current; with a 256 MB heap class the LRU budget is 32 MB, so the bitmap is larger than the cache, is evicted immediately and decoded again on every mediaItem update (twice per track start: announce, then duration). A paused or background player carrying tens to hundreds of MB of artwork is exactly what the low-memory killer removes first, which the handler otherwise goes to lengths to avoid (main.dart image-cache budget, foreground-while-paused).
findings.fix: Bound the picked image at the source (`pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery, maxWidth: 1200, maxHeight: 1200, imageQuality: 90)`) and/or pass `artDownscaleWidth: 512, artDownscaleHeight: 512` in AudioServiceConfig.

find:journey-library aab062.notes:
Walked the library-management journey end to end (home lenses, playlist page, artist page, song sheet, info sheet -> LibraryController -> DatabaseService / handler / TrackNaming / LyricsController / download services). docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md from the earlier pass already lists related items (re-download re-registers the raw copy #11/#23/#24/#34, batch-add order #60, favourite stores the caller's stale copy #62/#76, snack bars under the info sheet #65, queue-row 播放 #64, delete-before-current announces the next song #72, lyrics not refreshed on rename #55, artist splitter 'feat' #71); I did not repeat those.

Checked and found sound:
- Edit of the playing / a queued song: DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata replaces the library, every playlist copy and the history copy; handler._latest + _publish refresh nowPlaying (TrackNotifier), queueNotifier, mediaItem and the audio_service queue; the session file stores ids only; artist grouping, sorted list and SearchView's local cache are invalidated by list identity on every reload; TrackCredit cache is reset when known artists change. TrackNaming re-reads the stored copy and backs off when title/uploader/matcher/named changed, so a hand edit during a lookup wins.
- Delete of a playing / queued / multi-playlist song: files go first, removeTracks walks the native sequence from the end (indices stay valid), playlists/favourites/history keep their copies by design, saveSession refuses to overwrite with an empty queue and restore filters by library. No UI offers delete for an in-flight download (delete appears only once the library lists the song), and DownloadManager has no cancel by design.
- Playlists: create/rename/delete/reorder/cover all go through one write lock in call order with snapshots taken per call; rapid reorders stay consistent because _pendingOrder and the in-place playlist.tracks mutation agree; onReorderItem's adjusted index matches _moveWithin; swipe-remove hides the row via _removing until reload; addTracksToPlaylist de-duplicates inside the batch and against the playlist; delete pops the page before removing. Double taps on sheet actions are absorbed because a popping ModalRoute ignores pointers and dialogs/sheets push a barrier synchronously (the artist page's 存为歌单 is the one action with awaits before any route change - reported).
- Artist page: reads the group live by name; renaming the artist on a song moves it out of the group immediately and playlist copies made by 存为歌单 are updated by updateTrackMetadata. (If the last song leaves, the page stays open showing 0 首 - cosmetic, not reported.)
- Sort: setSort notifies before persisting, sortedDownloaded is cached per (list identity, sort); a sheet opened with an older sorted list still plays correctly because the handler re-resolves every queue item against the library by id.

Considered and not reported (window too narrow to be a realistic scenario): TrackInfoSheet saves a copy built from the Track captured when it opened, so a loudness backfill landing while the sheet is open is dropped for the session; updateTrackMetadata is not atomic across its three files, so a process death between the downloaded-file and playlist-file writes leaves playlist rows with the old name; removeTracks versus a concurrent _install.

Could not determine without running: whether AppShell's Scaffold resizes for the keyboard (would decide whether createAndOpenPlaylist's context.mounted check can fail when the 新建 tile scrolls out of the cache extent). There is no UI that calls setPlaylistCover(id, null), so a custom playlist cover can be replaced but not removed - a missing feature rather than a defect.

findings.title: The session "no lyrics" memo is keyed by track id only: a song renamed while it is not the playing track keeps showing 暂无歌词 and is never looked up under its new name
findings.evidence:
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:46-48 `/// Songs the databases had nothing for, this session ...` / `final Set<String> _misses = {};`
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:178-181 `if (_misses.contains(track.id)) { publish(Lyrics.none); return; }` - consulted before any request, with no regard to the name the miss was recorded for.
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:189-190 `if (fresh.isEmpty) _misses.add(track.id);` / `if (!owns()) return;` - the miss is recorded for the query built from the Track instance passed to that _load (183-188 `_namedBy(track)` / `autoFetchLyrics(track.rawTitle, song: named.song, artist: named.artist)`), and is recorded even when that lookup no longer owns the track.
The only rename handling is for the track that is playing at the moment of the rename: lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:130-135 `if (track.id == _trackId) { ... if (nameKey == _nameKey || state.value.lyrics.pinned) return; _misses.remove(track.id); }`. A rename of a track that is not current never reaches the controller: lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:932-935 `updateTrackMetadata` only does `_latest[updated.id] = updated; _publish();` and _publish (229-237) touches nowPlaying only when the current source is that track. When the song is played later, `track.id != _trackId`, so line 134 is skipped and line 178 answers from the stale memo.
Both rename routes hit this: lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:99-100 (编辑信息 opened from any list row via track_sheet.dart:210, for a song that is not playing) and lib/services/track_naming.dart:115-118 `_save` (automatic naming is a serial queue, track_naming.dart:105-107 `_queue = _queue.then((_) => _name(track))`, so with several fresh downloads it routinely lands after the listener has moved to another song).
findings.failure_scenario: 1) Download several songs from search and play through them. Song A (title e.g. a messy live-clip title) starts; the lyric lookup uses the raw-title parse, finds nothing, A enters `_misses`, pane shows 暂无歌词. 2) The listener skips on (or A ends). A's automatic naming, queued behind the other new downloads, completes now and names it 大鱼 / 周深 - or the listener, having seen 暂无歌词, opens A's row in the library and fixes the name in 编辑信息 precisely so that lyrics can be found. 3) A plays again in the same process (the playback service keeps the process alive for hours or days): no request is made, 暂无歌词 again, although the song now has a name that both providers would match. Only 重新匹配, a second edit while it is playing, or killing the app recovers. The controller's own comment at 131 says a better name deserves a fresh lookup; that only holds when the rename happens while the song is on air.
findings.fix: Record what was asked, not just for whom: make `_misses` a `Map<String, String>` of track id -> `_nameKeyOf(track)` (the name the empty lookup was made with) and treat it as a miss only when the stored key equals the current track's key (`_misses[track.id] == _nameKeyOf(track)`). Also move the `_misses` write below the `owns()` check or key it with the looked-up track's name, so a lookup made under an old name cannot mark the renamed song.

findings.title: Changing only the cover (or only the artist) in 编辑信息 marks the raw video title as the listener's own song name: the song is never auto-matched again and lyric lookups switch to the whole video title
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:81-87 the only no-op case is `title == track.title && artist == TrackCredit.artistOf(track) && _cover == track.coverUrl`; any other save, including a cover-only change with the title field untouched, goes to 90-97: `final updated = track.copyWith(title: title, uploader: artist.isEmpty ? TrackCredit.artistOf(track) : artist, coverUrl: _cover, named: true, // The listener's own answer: the matcher never revisits it. matcher: 0, rawUploader: ...)`.
The title field is prefilled with the video title for an unnamed song (track_info_sheet.dart:36-37 `TextEditingController(text: widget.track.title)`).
Consequences downstream: lib/services/track_naming.dart:101-102 `_settled(track) => track.isNamed && (track.matcher == 0 || track.matcher == matcher)` and 105-106 `if (!enabled || _settled(track) || ...) return;` - never named automatically again, also not when the matcher constant is raised.
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:61-64 `track.isNamed ? (song: track.title, artist: track.uploader) : (song: track.partTitle, artist: null)` and lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart:2145-2146 `final cleaned = cleanTitle(rawTitle); final title = song ?? cleaned['songTitle']!;` - once `named` is true the uncleaned video title (for a part: the whole "<video> - P3: <part>" string, since models/track.dart:83 isNamed now wins over partTitle) is sent as the song name instead of the parsed song / the part name.
lib/state/lyrics_controller.dart:67-70 `if (track.isNamed) { return '${track.uploader} ${track.title}'.trim(); }` - the lyric sheet's prefilled search becomes artist + full video title.
findings.failure_scenario: A freshly downloaded song still carries its video title (auto-naming is switched off, has not reached it yet in the queue, or found no match). The listener opens 编辑信息 only to pick a nicer cover and taps 保存. The track is now stored as named=true, matcher=0 with title "【周深】大鱼 现场版 4K". From then on automatic matching skips it for good (it reads as the listener's answer), the row keeps the video title forever, the lyric sheet opens with the search "周深 【周深】大鱼 现场版 4K", and any later automatic lyric lookup (after 重新匹配 or a cache eviction) asks the providers for the whole video title; for a multi-part track it asks for "<concert> - P3: 大鱼" where it used to ask for 大鱼.
findings.fix: In `_save`, only claim the name when the listener changed it: compute `renamed = title != track.title || artist != TrackCredit.artistOf(track)`; when `!renamed` save `track.copyWith(coverUrl: _cover)` and leave title, uploader, named, matcher and rawUploader as they were.

findings.title: Tapping a lyric line whose time lies beyond the end of the audio seeks past the end and skips to the next song
findings.evidence:
lib/widgets/lyrics_view.dart:172-173 `final seconds = (line.time + widget.lyrics.offset).clamp(0.0, 86400.0);` / `widget.onSeek?.call(Duration(milliseconds: (seconds * 1000).round()));` - clamped to a day, not to the track.
lib/screens/now_playing_page.dart:392 `onSeek: _handler.seek,` and lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart:794 `Future<void> seek(Duration position) => _player.seek(position);` - no clamp against `_player.duration`.
just_audio-0.10.6 lib/just_audio.dart:1328-1329 forwards the position unchanged (`.seek(SeekRequest(position: position, index: index))`) and android/.../AudioPlayer.java:1040-1041 calls `player.seekTo(windowIndex, position)`; a position at or past the item's duration ends the item, and with the queue in 列表循环/随机 the player moves to the next one (with 单曲循环 it restarts). The seek bar cannot produce such a position; the lyric view is the only caller that can. Deduced from source, not run.
Lyrics longer than the audio are normal here: automatic matching attaches the full studio song's LRC to short clips and live cuts, and a positive calibration offset pushes the last lines further out.
findings.failure_scenario: A 1:30 clip of a live performance is matched to the full 4:30 song's lyrics. The listener scrolls down in the lyric view and taps a line timed at 3:10 (or simply the last line after calibrating by +5 s on a full-length track). Instead of nothing happening or jumping to the end, the clip ends at once and the next song in the queue starts playing; the lyric view switches to that song.
findings.fix: Clamp the target in `_tap` (or in the page's onSeek wrapper) to just before the end: `final total = handler.durationNotifier.value; if (total > Duration.zero && target >= total) return;` (or clamp to `total - 500 ms`), so a line outside the audio is not seekable.

find:journey-lyrics aecb45.notes:
Read-only: nothing in the repo was modified, no flutter/dart/build command was run and no network request was made. Also read in part (not in filesRead): lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart (lines 28-56, 240-262, 1670-2168: HTTP helper, title matching, LRC parse/serialise, both providers, candidate search, autoFetchLyrics), lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart (_publish/_announce, seek/skip, loop mode, holdAutoAdvance, updateTrackMetadata, sleep timer), lib/services/track_naming.dart, lib/services/track_credit.dart, lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart (save path), lib/widgets/sheet.dart (showAppSheet), database_service.dart store-file helpers, test/lyric_paste_test.dart, just_audio 0.10.6 (seek, positionStream), and the untracked docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md from the earlier run of this audit.

The earlier run already recorded these on this journey, which I re-traced and agree with but do not repeat: failed lookup == miss for the whole session (#12), cached automatic lyrics rejected/deleted when the provider title has a subtitle (#13), translation lines split by the editor round trip (#15), kana/hangul titles never matching (#16), 重新匹配 deleting pinned lyrics before the new lookup (#54), rename re-publishing the cache made under the old name (#55), float round trip on tap-to-seek with an offset (#57), default sheet query ignoring the part name (#58), wheel scrolling on macOS (#59), player popping the top route when the queue empties (#63). The first finding above is a different root cause from #12 (stale memo after a rename, not failure-vs-absence), though a fix for both would touch the same set.

Walked step by step and found sound:
- Song starts -> automatic fetch: every await in LyricsController._load is followed by owns() (generation + current id + store revision); A->B->A, null track, rename and dispose all invalidate in-flight work; _load always ends in publish or in a state already set by choose/rematch, so the pane cannot stick on the shimmer. Loudness backfill and cover-only updates produce a new Track instance with the same name key and do not trigger a reload.
- Choosing a result / pasting: the sheet acts on the Track it was opened for; choose() pins synchronously (revision bump before any await), shows it only if that song is current, and putAutomatic re-checks revision and pinned before and after its write. I found no path where an automatic result replaces a pinned entry on screen or on disk. A superseded pin's persist is skipped in favour of the newer one; write failure reaches the snackbar.
- Calibration: offset is absolute and stored apart from the lines; each tap pins; the calibrating Track is captured, so a tap that lands after a manual skip is saved for the right song and not shown on the next; skip, back, 完成, toggling lyrics and dispose all release the auto-advance hold exactly once (the release closure is idempotent, holds are counted). The position read for calibration is the last positionStream tick (up to 200 ms old for songs over 160 s), but the highlight is evaluated on the same ticks, so the bias cancels on average; not raised.
- Track changes during fetch or calibration: results of a lookup that lost ownership are dropped and not stored; the page ends calibration from its own nowPlaying listener.
- Offline: pinned lyrics are published synchronously from LyricsStore.peek; matching automatic entries are served from the store without a request.
- Info edited: lyrics are keyed by Track.id (bvid_p<page>), which copyWith never changes; a pinned entry is left alone on rename (line 133) and automatic ones are re-evaluated.
- Deleted and downloaded again: nothing in the delete path touches LyricsStore (only LyricsController and LyricsSheet reference it), so pins and calibration survive; the id is the same on re-download.
- LyricsView: listeners/timer cleaned up, keys rebuilt when the lines object changes, offset-only changes keep scroll state, children are disposed before the page's position notifier.

Smaller observations, not raised as findings:
- LyricsSheet reads the store (LyricsStore.peek) while the pane reads controller state. They can differ only when an unpinned stored entry fails _matches and the track is in _misses (a lookup that lost ownership returned empty): the pane shows 暂无歌词 while the sheet offers 编辑 prefilled with, and 校准 for, lyrics that are not on screen. Needs a rename plus an interrupted lookup; rare.
- Saving an emptied editor returns null and nothing happens (lyrics cannot be removed by clearing the text; the sheet stays open without feedback).
- plainLines drops blank lines, so pasted untimed lyrics lose their verse breaks.
- Offline, the sheet's search shows 没有找到歌词 (no distinction from an empty answer), and searchCandidates waits for both providers, so one slow provider delays the other's results by up to its timeouts.

Could not determine without a device/network: the exact player behaviour on a seek past the end on iOS/macOS (the Android path is read from plugin source; hence the 0.55 confidence), and what NetEase returns for a whole video title as the search term (second finding's lyric consequence; the auto-matching consequence is certain from code).

findings.title: A naming answer reached with missing or partial Bilibili hints is written to the library as final (matcher = current)
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:124-125 `final hints = await BilibiliSdk.fetchVideoHints(before.bvid, cid: before.cid);` -- the result is never checked for completeness outside the legacy branch (134 `if (hints.owner.isEmpty && before.rawUploader == null)` is inside `if (legacy)`).
bilibili_sdk.dart:247-248 "Never throws: offline (or refused) is [VideoHints.none], and is asked again next time"; 261 `if (view is! Map && tags is! List) return VideoHints.none;`; 269 `final music = part == 0 ? null : await _recognisedMusic(bvid, part);` then 288 `musicTitle: music?.title ?? ''`; 291-292 "Half an answer (one request failed) is used but not kept." -- only the in-memory memo declines to keep it.
lyrics_engine.dart:926 `var incomplete = results.contains(null);` tracks only NetEase failures; with hints empty the function still reaches 1244 `_remember(memoKey, identity)`, so track_naming.dart:148 `identitySettled` is true and 188-196 saves `named: true, matcher: matcher` (or 180-183 stamps an older answer with the new matcher).
track_naming.dart:95-96 `_settled` then stops any further look.
findings.failure_scenario: Bilibili refuses the view/tag or the WBI-signed player/wbi/v2 request (412 risk control, the state release 0.1.2 was about) while NetEase answers. A cover uploaded by UP主 小明 in the 翻唱 zone, titled e.g. "大鱼 周深", is downloaded. With hints the zone/tags mark it a rendition and the performer becomes the UP主; with VideoHints.none (or with musicTitle silently empty because only the recognition request failed) the title-only path credits 周深 as exact, replaces the thumbnail with the release artwork, and stores matcher 4. Because the song is now settled it is never asked about again when Bilibili is reachable. The same happens on a matcher bump: the one re-check of an old answer is spent without hints and stamped with the new generation.
findings.fix: Have fetchVideoHints report completeness (e.g. a `complete` flag false when view, tags or music could not be fetched) and in `_name` treat an incomplete fetch like the offline case: `_attempted.remove(track.id); return;` before asking, for both the legacy and normal paths.

findings.title: Parts of a multi-part video are named after a song the video-wide tags mention, not the part
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:81-83 asks about `track.partTitle` with `context: track.rawTitle`; bilibili_sdk.dart:257 fetches tags per bvid (video-wide), only music is per cid.
lyrics_engine.dart:902-906 adds up to two tags as song queries: `queries.putIfAbsent('$searchArtist $t'.trim(), () => {'song': t, 'tag': '1'});`
970 `final named = isolated || inRaw || tagNorms.contains(nameNorm);` -- a tag alone makes the song "named".
730 `var normCredits = normRaw + _normalize(_preprocess(context));` so the singer in the video title credits every part; 1021-1022 `final onlyTags = !inRaw && (fromTag || !isolated); if (onlyTags && inTitle.isEmpty && !original) continue;` therefore passes.
1084 `bestExact = inTitle.isNotEmpty && !bestRendition;` and the only veto is 1102 `if (hints.musicTitle.isNotEmpty && !bestApart)`, which needs Bilibili to have recognised some other music in that part.
findings.failure_scenario: A concert uploaded as parts: video "周深 2023演唱会" tagged 周深, 大鱼; P1 "开场", P2 "大鱼", P3 "Talk", P4 a song NetEase does not list. P1/P3/P4 are downloaded. Their own names find nothing; the tag query "周深 大鱼" returns 大鱼 by 周深, credited through the video title, so each part is saved as 大鱼 / 周深 with the 大鱼 release artwork (bestExact) whenever Bilibili recognised no music in that part (speech, or the recognition request failed). The library ends up with several different recordings all named 大鱼.
findings.fix: When `context` is non-empty (a part), do not let a tag stand in for the name: skip the tag-song queries, or require `inRaw` (the part's own name contains the song) for tag-sourced candidates.

findings.title: Switching 自动匹配歌曲信息 off does not stop lookups already queued or in flight
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:100-106: `if (!enabled || _settled(track) || !_attempted.add(track.id)) return; _queue = _queue.then((_) => _name(track))...` -- `enabled` is read only when a job is enqueued.
track_naming.dart:119-197 `_name` never reads `enabled`; 188-196 writes the new title/artist/cover unconditionally.
track_naming.dart:48-51 `setEnabled` only flips the flag and saves the pref.
findings.failure_scenario: The listener batch-downloads an album (20 parts). Each arrival is enqueued by LibraryController.reload (library_controller.dart:202-204) on the serial `_queue`; each lookup takes seconds. Seeing the first few songs renamed wrongly, the listener opens 设置 and turns the toggle off. The remaining ~17 queued songs are still looked up and renamed over the next minute, with the switch showing off. Each must then be fixed by hand.
findings.fix: Check `if (!enabled) { _attempted.remove(track.id); return; }` at the top of `_name` and again just before the final `_save` calls.

findings.title: Lyrics fetched from the raw-title parse survive a rename to a different song
findings.evidence:
lyrics_controller.dart:131-134 "Same song, edited metadata. A better name deserves a fresh lookup" -> `_load(track, generation)`.
lyrics_controller.dart:148-154 `_matches`: `final parsed = LyricsEngine.cleanTitle(track.rawTitle)['songTitle'] ?? ''; return LyricsEngine.isTitleMatching(storedTitle, parsed) || LyricsEngine.isTitleMatching(storedTitle, track.title);`
lyrics_controller.dart:172-177 `if (stored != null && stored.isNotEmpty && (stored.pinned || _matches(stored, track))) { publish(stored); return; }` -- returns before the fresh lookup at 183-188 that would use `named.song` / `named.artist`.
The first lookup on a new download runs from the parse (61-64 `_namedBy` gives no song/artist for an unnamed track) and is stored by putAutomatic (192) typically before TrackNaming's slower chain (hints + several searches) lands via handler.updateTrackMetadata.
findings.failure_scenario: A new download starts playing. Lyrics are fetched for what the offline parser reads from the video title (say the show name in the first 《》, or the right name but another artist's song of that name, since no artist is known) and stored. Seconds later auto-naming names it a different song/artist using Bilibili's recognition. nowPlaying notifies, the name key differs, `_load` runs again, finds the stored lyrics, `_matches` passes because the stored title still matches the raw-title parse, and the old lyrics are republished. They stay on every later play (the store is persistent) until the listener manually re-matches. If naming happens to finish first the result is correct, so the outcome depends on request timing.
findings.fix: For a named track compare stored lyrics only against `track.title` (drop the raw-title parse branch when `track.isNamed`), and when the name key changed on the playing track skip the stored-automatic shortcut altogether.

findings.title: Re-check by a newer matcher corrects name/artist but keeps the earlier answer's album artwork
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:188-196 `await _save(stored.copyWith(title: found.title, uploader: found.artist, coverUrl: found.coverUrl, named: true, ...))`.
track.dart:191 `coverUrl: coverUrl ?? this.coverUrl` -- a null `found.coverUrl` keeps whatever is stored.
lyrics_engine.dart:14-15 "The original release's artwork; only offered when [exact]"; 1231-1232 `String? cover; if (bestExact) cover = await _netEaseCover(best!['id']);`.
The video thumbnail is not kept anywhere once replaced (no rawCoverUrl on Track; VideoHints carries no picture).
findings.failure_scenario: Matcher N judged a clip exact and stored "大鱼 / 周深" with NetEase's album art in place of the video thumbnail. TrackNaming.matcher is raised; on next play the song is re-checked and found to be a cover (exact false, coverUrl null). Title and artist become the cover singer's, but the row, player and notification keep 周深's release artwork for good; nothing can restore the thumbnail short of deleting and re-downloading.
findings.fix: Keep the video's picture (store it once as a raw cover, or return `pic` in VideoHints) and, when a re-check yields a non-exact identity for a song an earlier matcher gave release artwork, restore it.

findings.title: A song deleted and downloaded again in the same session is not named, and the player shows stale metadata
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:34 `static final Set<String> _attempted = {};` is cleared only on inconclusive lookups (135, 157); 101 `!_attempted.add(track.id)` returns for any id tried earlier.
database_service.dart:779-785 `removeDownloadedTrack` drops the library row (and audio_download_service.dart:229-235 the meta file); the re-download stores the search copy with the video title (database_service.dart:767-771).
audio_player_handler.dart:145 `_latest` is written at 463 and 933 and never cleared; 170 `Track _resolve(Track tag) => _latest[tag.id] ?? tag;` and 623-626 `_library()` resolves every library track through it.
findings.failure_scenario: Song X is downloaded and auto-named (id in `_attempted`, named copy in `handler._latest`). The listener deletes the download and downloads it again from search in the same session (for example hoping for a fresh match). LibraryController.reload calls autoName (library_controller.dart:203) but `_attempted` rejects it, so the library row keeps the raw video title until the app is restarted. Meanwhile playing it resolves through `_latest`, so the player, notification and lyrics show the old song name/artist while the list shows the video title.
findings.fix: Subscribe to DatabaseService.downloadRemovedStream in TrackNaming (remove ids from `_attempted`) and in the handler (remove ids from `_latest`).

findings.title: 收藏 from the track sheet stores the caller's stale Track copy instead of the library's named one
findings.evidence:
track_sheet.dart:102-104 `Future<void> _toggleFavorite() async { Haptics.light(); await DatabaseService.toggleFavorite(widget.track); }` while the sheet itself knows better: 234-241 "The library's copy carries any edits made since the sheet's caller captured its [Track]" / `_latest()`, used for display at 121 and for 加入歌单 at 188.
database_service.dart:736 `favorites.tracks.insert(0, track);` stores it verbatim; database_service.dart:532-537 only rewrites playlist copies when updateTrackMetadata runs, which TrackNaming never does again for a settled song (track_naming.dart:122).
findings.failure_scenario: From a search result the listener opens the sheet for a song that is not downloaded, taps 下载, waits while it downloads and is auto-named (the sheet title updates through `_latest()`), then taps 收藏 in the same sheet. Favorites receives `widget.track` -- the search copy with the raw video title, UP主 and no loudness. 收藏 then lists the video title while 本地 lists the song name, permanently. The same happens when favoriting an already named song from any online search or recommendation row.
findings.fix: Use `_latest()` in `_toggleFavorite` (and have DatabaseService.toggleFavorite/addTracksToPlaylist prefer the downloaded copy for an id it knows).

findings.title: Videos that can never be one song still cost a full Bilibili hints fetch on first play of every launch
findings.evidence:
track_naming.dart:124-125 fetches hints first; bilibili_sdk.dart:255-258 (view + tags), 322-335 (signed player/wbi/v2 + bgm/detail) -- up to four Bilibili requests, more when the plain view is refused and retried signed (143-156).
Only afterwards lyrics_engine.dart:711-716 rejects offline: `if (category || _severalSongs.hasMatch(rawTitle) || durationSeconds > _longestSong) { _remember(memoKey, null); return null; }`.
track_naming.dart:176-186: for an unnamed track with `found == null` nothing is saved, and `_attempted` / `_identityMemo` / `_hintsMemo` are in-memory only, so the verdict is forgotten at exit.
findings.failure_scenario: The library holds 20-minute live sets, 【合集】 uploads and other titles the catalogues do not know. Each launch, the first time each of them becomes the playing track, the app sends 3-4 requests to Bilibili (and for unknown-but-short titles up to ~8 NetEase searches as well) to re-derive a negative answer already known, on an account/IP that is already subject to Bilibili risk control. Shuffling a library of such tracks produces a steady stream of signed player requests in the background.
findings.fix: Run the offline exclusions (duration > 15 min, category brackets, _severalSongs) in TrackNaming before fetchVideoHints, and persist a negative verdict per matcher generation (e.g. `matcher` on an un-named track) so it is not re-asked until the constant is raised.

find:journey-matching a38eca.notes:
Read in part (not full): lib/services/lyrics_engine.dart (1-56, 128-160, 515-1633, 1734-1766, 2136-2168), lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart (1-400, search Track construction), lib/services/audio_player_handler.dart (95-394, 425-475, 520-760, 900-1028), lib/services/database_service.dart (380-901), parts of audio_download_service.dart, track_sheet.dart, search_view.dart. Nothing was run; all findings are from reading. Finding 2 (part tags) and finding 4 (lyrics) depend on parser/NetEase behaviour I could not execute, hence the lower confidence.

Checked and found sound:
- Listener edit vs in-flight match: _name re-reads the stored track and compares title/uploader/matcher/named (track_naming.dart:162-169); TrackInfoSheet always writes matcher 0, so any edit (including cover-only) is detected. The remaining window is a couple of microtasks.
- matcher 0 is never revisited (_settled), and the save path of a re-check goes through stored.copyWith so loudness and other fields are preserved.
- Network failing halfway through identify: NetEase failures set `incomplete` / `who.incomplete` and return without _remember, so track_naming removes the id from _attempted and retries on next play; no partial answer is written (the gap is only on the Bilibili-hints side, finding 1).
- Result propagation: DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata rewrites downloaded, on-disk meta, every playlist copy and history; handler.updateTrackMetadata -> _publish updates nowPlaying, mediaItem (notification) and the queue; LibraryController reloads and re-teaches known artists, invalidating artist and sort caches; ArtistPage tolerates its group disappearing. Session file stores ids only.
- No feedback loop: the save re-notifies nowPlaying, autoName sees a settled track and returns.
- Requests per play when inconclusive: nowPlaying only announces on id change (loop-one does not retrigger), and hints/identity/singer memos bound repeat cost within a session.
- Startup: `enabled` is loaded before the nowPlaying listener is attached; LibraryController does not auto-name on its first load.
- Compilation / >15 min: identify returns null and remembers it; nothing is written for an unnamed track, an older automatic name is kept and stamped (by design).

Not reported but worth knowing: libraries saved before rawTitle existed (pre 3.10.2) load with rawTitle = title, so a title edited back then is indistinguishable from an unnamed video title and is eligible for auto-naming; I could not determine whether such data still exists. TrackNaming has no behavioural tests beyond `settled()` (test/track_test.dart).

findings.title: Once a download has filled the disk, every library write fails silently while the UI confirms it; the kept .part keeps the disk full
findings.evidence: Every persister swallows the write error. lib/services/database_service.dart:473-487 `_persistPlaylists`: `} catch (e) { debugPrint('DatabaseService _persistPlaylists error: $e'); }` followed by `if (!_libraryUpdateController.isClosed) _libraryUpdateController.add(null);` - the success event is emitted even when the write failed. Same pattern at :453-461 (_persistDownloaded), :463-471 (_persistRecentlyPlayed), :864-874 (savePlaybackSession), :836-843 (setPref). Callers then confirm: lib/widgets/track_sheet.dart:304-305 `await DatabaseService.addTracksToPlaylist(playlist.id, tracks); showAppSnackBar(messenger, message: '已加入「${playlist.name}」');`; database_service.dart:736-738 toggleFavorite `await _persistPlaylists(); return true;`. lib/widgets/track_info_sheet.dart:99-108 has a `catch` that shows '保存失败，请重试', but DatabaseService.updateTrackMetadata (:521-548) can never throw, so that path is dead. Each write needs room for a second full copy: :358-359 `tmp = File('$path.$unique.tmp'); await tmp.writeAsString(payload, flush: true);`. What holds the disk full: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:354-357 `// Deliberately keep the .part file: the next attempt resumes it via Range` - the partial file that consumed the last free bytes is never removed (no code in lib/ deletes a .part except AudioDownloadService.delete, :233, reachable only for a track that is already in the downloaded list).
findings.failure_scenario: Storage runs out while a long video downloads (ENOSPC). The partial file stays on disk, so the app's free space stays at zero. The listener, unaware, keeps using the app: favourites three songs (heart turns on), creates a playlist and adds songs ('已加入「…」'), edits a song's name in 编辑信息 (sheet closes as saved), plays for an hour. Every one of those writes failed in the temp-file step and was only logged. When the process is next killed, all of it is gone: favourites, the playlist, the edit, the listening position and 最近播放 revert to the last state written before the disk filled. Nothing ever told the listener a save failed.
findings.fix: Let persist failures surface: have the _persist* helpers return success (or rethrow) and make the mutating API propagate it, so callers show '保存失败' instead of the success snackbar (track_info_sheet already has the branch). At minimum emit one user-facing message through a stream AppShell listens to when a write fails. Separately, delete the .part (and its note) when the transfer fails with a FileSystemException rather than a network error.

findings.title: Audio is never fsynced before it is marked ready: a power loss shortly after a download leaves a permanently 'downloaded' file that is truncated or zero-filled
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:543-547 `await sink.flush(); } finally { try { await sink.close(); } catch (_) {} }` - IOSink.flush only hands the bytes to the OS; nothing calls RandomAccessFile.flush (fsync) on the .part. Then :328 `await part.rename(path);`, :338 the note recording the expected total is deleted (`if (await note.exists()) await note.delete();`), :341-344 the `.ready` marker is created. From then on the only integrity test is :181-183 `if (!await ready.exists()) return false; if (!await audio.exists()) return false; return await audio.length() > 0;` and the same test in the start-up prune, lib/services/database_service.dart:276-278. By contrast the small JSON files are written with `flush: true` (audio_download_service.dart:105, database_service.dart:359), so after a power cut the sidecar and the ready marker can be durable while the audio's data blocks are not.
findings.failure_scenario: The phone's battery dies (or it hard-reboots) within the file system's writeback window after a song finishes downloading, e.g. while a batch of downloads is running. After reboot `audio_<id>.m4a` exists with a non-zero length but is short or contains unwritten blocks; `.ready` and the sidecar exist. The start-up prune keeps it, the library shows it as downloaded, and playing it ends early or produces '有歌曲无法播放，已跳过' every time. Nothing re-downloads it (isDownloaded is true); the listener has to guess that deleting and downloading again fixes it. The expected size that could have detected this was thrown away with the part note.
findings.fix: Before the rename, open the .part and fsync it (`final raf = await part.open(mode: FileMode.append); await raf.flush(); await raf.close();`). Optionally write the expected byte count into the `.ready` marker and have _statDownloaded / the start-up prune compare it with the file length.

findings.title: A failed `.ready` marker write is swallowed: the song is reported downloaded for this session, vanishes at next launch, and leaves an undeletable orphan file
findings.evidence: lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:340-349 `try { final readyFile = File(_readyPath(dir, _key(track))); if (!await readyFile.exists()) { await readyFile.create(recursive: true); } } catch (e) { debugPrint('ready create failed: $e'); } await saveTrackMetadata(track, force: track.loudness != null); _downloadedMemo[_key(track)] = true;` then :351-352 emits done and calls `DatabaseService.saveDownloadedTrack(track)`. The memo now contradicts the disk. Next launch, lib/services/database_service.dart:221 only discovers files that have a `.ready` (`entity.path.endsWith('.ready')`) and :276-287 prunes any listed track without one (`exists = await ready.exists() && ...` -> `prunedIds.add(t.id)`), persisting the pruned list at :296. audio_download_service.dart:204-205 `storageBreakdown` skips an m4a without a ready marker, and delete() is only reachable for tracks in the downloaded list.
findings.failure_scenario: The last megabytes of a download exhaust free space (or the process is killed between the rename at :328 and the marker at :343). The audio file is complete and renamed, but creating the marker fails; the sidecar write and the downloaded.json write fail too (both swallowed). The session continues normally: the row shows downloaded, the song plays. At the next launch the song is gone from the library without explanation, while its full-size m4a stays in bilibeat_audio, counted nowhere in 下载管理 and removable only by clearing app data - on a device that is already out of space. Downloading it again needs the same space a second time before the orphan is replaced.
findings.fix: Treat a failed marker as a failed download (rethrow instead of logging) so the memo is not set and the user sees the failure; and make start-up discovery adopt a non-empty `audio_<id>.m4a` that has a sidecar but no `.part`/note and no marker (re-create the marker) or delete it, instead of leaving it orphaned.

findings.title: System clock moved backwards pins WBI signing to stale or hard-coded keys for the length of the jump; downloads fail until restart
findings.evidence: lib/services/wbi_signer.dart:131-136 `if (_cacheTime != null && DateTime.now().difference(_cacheTime!).inHours < 12) { ... return {'imgKey': _cachedImgKey, 'subKey': _cachedSubKey}; }` - a negative difference (cache stamped in the 'future') is always < 12, so the cached pair never expires until the clock passes the stamp plus 12 h. :138-141 `if (retryAfter != null && DateTime.now().isBefore(retryAfter)) { return _fallbackKeys; }` with :180 `_retryAfter = DateTime.now().add(_retryEvery);` - after a backwards jump of N hours the hard-coded 2-year-old pair is used for N hours + 2 min with no attempt to fetch live keys. The stream URL has no unsigned fallback: lib/services/bilibili_sdk.dart:389-395 signs and requests only `x/player/wbi/playurl`, and a refusal returns null (:446) -> audio_download_service.dart:304-306 `throw Exception('无法获取音源下载链接')`. The media service keeps the process (and these statics) alive for days (main.dart:50 `androidStopForegroundOnPause: false`).
findings.failure_scenario: The device clock is ahead (set by hand, or wrong after a flat battery) when the app makes one signed request with no connectivity: `_retryAfter` is stamped two minutes into that wrong future. The clock is then corrected by network time, i.e. jumps back several hours or days. For that whole span every signed request uses the hard-coded fallback keys (or, in the other branch, a cached pair that Bilibili has since rotated): playurl is refused, so every download and every 下载并播放 ends in '下载失败' although search (which has a plain fallback) works. Only force-stopping the app clears it. A timestamp from the wrong clock is also sent as `wts`.
findings.fix: Use a monotonic source for both windows (a `Stopwatch` started at fetch / at failure) instead of DateTime, or treat a negative `difference` and a `_retryAfter` more than `_retryEvery` ahead of now as expired.

findings.title: Start-up prune is skipped entirely when the audio folder itself is missing, so a library with no files is shown as fully downloaded for one launch
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:214-217 `static Future<void> _discoverAudioFiles(String dir) async { try { final audioDir = Directory('$dir/bilibeat_audio'); if (!await audioDir.exists()) return;` - the early return also skips the prune loop at :261-296 that exists precisely for `entries whose files vanished externally`. Nothing has created the folder at that point: it is only created by AudioDownloadService._dir() (audio_download_service.dart:69-72), which first runs after the library has loaded (handler._install / isDownloaded). So the downloaded list is published as-is; LibraryController.isDownloaded (library_controller.dart:58) says yes for every song. playCollection (audio_player_handler.dart:669-685) filters only against that list and installs sources for files that do not exist; a row tap goes to playTrack -> _ensureLocal (:603-608), where `AudioDownloadService.isDownloaded` stats the disk, says no, and starts a download.
findings.failure_scenario: The bilibeat_audio folder is removed while the JSON files remain (macOS: the user or a cleaner deletes it from the app container; any platform: a restore that brings back the small JSON files but not the audio). On the next launch the whole library is listed as downloaded. 播放全部 / 随机播放 builds a queue of non-existent files and fails with '无法播放「…」'; tapping a single song silently re-downloads it over whatever network is active, contrary to the row-tap contract (playback_actions.dart:13-14 `nothing downloads silently from a tap`). Because that launch re-creates the empty folder, the launch after it prunes everything.
findings.fix: Do not return early: when the folder is missing, skip only the discovery listing and still run the prune (or create the folder first), so the library reflects the disk on the first launch.

findings.title: Temp files from an interrupted atomic write are never removed
findings.evidence: lib/services/database_service.dart:357-359 `final unique = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch; tmp = File('$path.$unique.tmp'); await tmp.writeAsString(payload, flush: true);` - a uniquely named temp file per write; the only cleanup is the `finally` at :392-398, which runs only if the process survives. lib/services/audio_download_service.dart:103-117 `_atomicWriteString` does the same for sidecars and has no cleanup at all, not even when `writeAsString` or `rename` throws. `grep -rn '\.tmp' lib` finds no sweep: _load (:111-129) and _discoverAudioFiles never look for `*.tmp`. Writes are frequent and not small: the session file every 20 s while playing (audio_player_handler.dart:326-329), and the whole lyrics store on every newly matched song (lyrics_store.dart:155-158).
findings.failure_scenario: The process is killed (OEM task killer, low-memory kill, crash, power loss) while one of these writes is between creating the temp file and renaming it, or a sidecar write fails with ENOSPC. A `bilibeat_lyrics.json.<micros>.tmp` (as large as the lyrics store), `bilibeat_playlists.json.<micros>.tmp`, or `audio_<id>.json.<micros>.tmp` is left in the documents directory. Because each name is unique, no later write replaces it; the files accumulate over the life of the install and are invisible in 下载管理.
findings.fix: At the start of DatabaseService._load, delete `bilibeat_*.json.*.tmp` in the documents directory and `*.tmp` in bilibeat_audio; wrap _atomicWriteString in try/finally that deletes its temp file on failure.

find:journey-hostile aa1f92.notes:
Method: walked start-up (main -> AudioService.init -> AppServices/TrackNaming/restoreSession -> DatabaseService._load -> LibraryController) and each service under the listed hostile conditions. Nothing was run; no network requests were made. docs/audit-2026-10-06/findings.md (untracked, from the earlier interrupted run) already lists 90 unverified findings; I did not repeat those. Ones on this journey that I re-derived independently and agree with: #2/#21 (IOSink.flush never completes after a write error - confirmed against dart-sdk/lib/io/io_sink.dart:184-196 and 257-267, so a disk-full download hangs rather than fails), #35/#75 (abandoned .part files), #73 (play() during an in-flight restoreSession returns without playing, because _restoreStarted is set before the first await and main.dart:58 always starts the restore first), #52/#80 (set-aside stores and the cover sweep), #9 (a code -352 body from the signed view fallback is read as 'no such video').

Checked and found sound:
- Cold start offline: nothing on the start-up path awaits the network; restoreSession, the library load and prefs are local only. Loudness backfill and auto-naming fail quietly and are retried later.
- Each persisted JSON truncated / empty / wrong shape: downloaded, recently_played, playlists and search_history go through _readPayload + a typed cast inside try, and any failure sets the file aside as .unreadable instead of overwriting it; a truncated or missing downloaded.json is rebuilt from the per-track sidecars (which updateTrackMetadata keeps current with force: true). session.json of the wrong shape returns null and is simply rewritten. A corrupt lyrics file is set aside. The app starts in every case.
- Kill in the middle of a JSON write: temp file + rename under one write lock; the previous snapshot survives (only the stray temp file remains - reported). Snapshot/lock ordering is FIFO, so two queued persists cannot land out of order.
- Kill in the middle of a download: .part + note remain; resume is guarded by If-Range, Content-Range start, total length and validator, and a 416 is accepted only when the recorded total matches. Kill between rename and marker leaves an orphan that a re-download replaces.
- CDN link expiring / different file on resume: a fresh link is fetched per attempt (Track.audioUrl is never set anywhere in lib/, so the cached-URL branch at audio_download_service.dart:297 is dead), and a mismatching partial is discarded and restarted.
- 412 / -352 on search and video info: search falls back plain -> unfiltered and throws BiliApiException (UI shows retry); the stream URL has no fallback but fails with a message on the playback path.
- Documents directory moving (iOS reinstall): audio paths are derived from the current directory at every queue install, the session stores ids only, and picked covers are rebased in _rebaseCovers before the sweep runs.
- Session persistence: saveSession refuses to overwrite with an empty queue, so a launch that has not restored yet cannot wipe the saved session; restore filters ids against the pruned library.
- Android backup is fully disabled (allowBackup=false plus data_extraction_rules), so no partial-restore state arises there.

Could not determine without running: how ExoPlayer/just_audio 0.10.6 behaves when the restored current file is unreadable (whether a later play() re-prepares); the exact post-power-loss file state on f2fs vs ext4 (the fsync finding rests on general file-system semantics, hence the low confidence); whether Bilibili ever answers the signed view endpoint with HTTP 200 + code -352.
